A bet is a choice made in uncertainty. It may lead someone to pray, to spend time with believers, or to listen to words of faith. Even Pascal recognized that belief cannot simply be chosen, and suggested starting by acting as if one believes.

But a bet cannot create true faith. Faith is not a policy or a strategy. It is the heart’s recognition of truth.

The Wager may encourage someone to seek out faith, but it is not faith itself. Pascal did not present it as proof that faith is true.

Our Belief Rests on Proof, Not on Odds

Here is the key difference. Pascal says that reason cannot decide. In Islam, we do not accept this. Our tradition affirms that reason can know the truth.

Imam Bajuri states the proof plainly: the world originated, and everything that originated must have an originator. [Bajuri, Tuhfat al-Murid] The steps beneath it are these. Bodies carry qualities that visibly change — motion after stillness, color appearing and altering, things coming to be and passing away.

What changes in that manner is originated; bodies are never free of such qualities; and what is inseparable from the originated is itself originated. So the world originated. And it cannot have brought itself about, for its existence and its non-existence stood equal, and no side of an even balance tips without something to tip it. [Bajuri, Tuhfat al-Murid]

This is the settled method of the theologians, and the Quran points to it: “Verily in the creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are a multitude of mighty signs for those of insight and mind: Those who make remembrance of Allah standing and sitting and on their sides at rest, and who reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth: ‘Our Lord, You have not created all this in vain.’” [Quran 3:190–191; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Notice that the verse points to the alternation of night and day. It is change itself that is the basis of the proof.

Fear Is Not a Defect

Now, let us address what may be troubling you. You may think that faith held out of fear is somehow lesser. It is not. Fear of Allah is a praiseworthy quality, and the Quran connects it to knowledge, not to weakness. What is discouraged is not fear itself, but fear without hope. Despair is what is warned against.

The believer walks between the two: hope and fear.

A weak motive does not take away from true faith. If your heart affirms that Allah is One and that Muhammad is His Messenger (Allah bless him and give him peace), you are a believer. Whether your faith is surrounded by fear, hope, love, or habit, it remains valid.

What to Do

Do not spend your life worrying about your motives. This is not the path the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) taught us.

Instead, do two things. Learn the proofs, so your faith is based on knowledge and certainty. And keep the company of those whose love for Allah grows, and practice what increases love, so that fear is balanced with hope. The One you fear is the One who wrote for Himself, before creating creation, ‘My mercy has outstripped My wrath.’ [Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim]

Faith that begins in fear and matures into love
references: Hajek, “Pascal’s Wager,” Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

records.title: Is a Tournament Permissible if Entry Fees May Fund the Prizes?
records.question: I am paying a fee to my club, and my club pays an organization to host the tournament. The fee guarantees that I get to play all my matches, whether my team wins or loses. At the end, the winning teams get trophies. I tried to contact the trophy company to ask whether the awards are paid for with player registration money, but they did not respond.
records.answer:
It is permissible for you to play, compete, and to take the trophy if you win. Your payment is in order. You don’t have direct interaction with the organization; it is a separate contract that doesn’t involve you.

As for the trophy, it’s based on skill, and whoever is skillful enough to win the tournament. It’s not a game of chance, as with gambling, so you don’t have anything to worry about. [Maydani, Lubab]

records.title: How Should I Deal With Waswasa About Kufr?
records.question: I suffer from waswasa about kufr. I experience intrusive thoughts of disbelief and sometimes become confused about whether they reflect my beliefs. I regret them immediately, but they leave me anxious and fearful for my faith.
records.answer:
May Allah give you ease and well-being.

Kufr is an active choice, just like a vegetarian would make an active choice to start eating meat. The fact that you’re distressed shows that you have Iman. Some of the companions disliked thoughts about such matters, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and give him peace, called that clear faith. [Muslim]

Meaning, the fact that they don’t like it shows that they have true Iman, so do not worry about this. The bigger issue is that you have intense OCD symptoms, and you need to see a therapist and possibly a doctor.

Some medication may help you in this situation, but therapy is the means that will actually help you heal this issue.

Fighting it, trying to ignore it, endless searching for answers online, and forcing yourself not to think of a particular thought – none of these things are solutions. The solution is to find a good therapist.

Ask Allah for help, and pray in istikhara, and proceed insha’Allah. You’ll have some relief from this soon.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Review Video Games With Impermissible Content?
records.question: I run a YouTube channel reviewing video games. Some games contain haram elements, though I do not believe those aspects are permissible and do not endorse them. I enjoy the gameplay, story, art, and positive themes. Is praising or recommending such games kufr?
records.answer:
Reviewing such games is not kufr, but anything that promotes sins is sinful, so you should stop reviewing them. Games that have nudity and other impermissible elements should be avoided.

Review generally entails praising or promoting a game or criticizing certain elements of it.

If the game has impermissible elements and you’ve encouraged people to purchase it, according to some scholars, you will be assisting them in committing sins, so it is best to avoid it. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Ask for stories that entail some element of Shirk. If it is like any other story that depicts the religious beliefs of other religions. They are permissible to read/engage with; however, one must hate the Kufr within his heart.

In many situations, the stories themselves, due to the way they depict these false deities, are proof of the truth of the fact that there can be no god other than Allah.

Do what will enhance your iman, and choose to review games that won’t harm you or anyone else.

records.title: Is a Secret Nikah Permissible if We Fear Our Parents Will Refuse?
records.question: My partner and I intend to marry, and regret remaining in a relationship outside of nikah. As we are both still studying and not financially stable, we fear our parents would refuse a proposal.
records.answer:
There are basic underlying factors of suitability in a marriage, and in their absence, a secret nikah would not be valid at all. The way around this is to present the situation to your parents and discuss potential ways to mend or resolve it. [Maydani, Lubab]

It’s clear what being in this relationship entails and the harm it does to your religious practice. Continuing with something that is displeasing to Allah Most High, in this way, won’t bring you any good in your life.

Consider approaching your parents and asking them to allow you to get married while you remain in your own family home until you’re able to provide adequately for your wife.

records.title: How Can I Trust Allah’s Justice During Hardship?
records.question: I have doubts about Islam because I have suffered throughout my life, as have many others. I do not see Allah helping anyone, nor have I witnessed any miracle, divine intervention, or protection. I used to pray every day for a good life, but it seems that was too much to ask.
records.answer:
I am sorry for your pain. You have suffered for a long time and asked Allah for relief, but did not see it. Now you feel burdened by the thought that your doubts have put you beyond hope. Please know that this is not true.

Your Doubts Do Not Damn You

Doubts that come to you without your choosing are not disbelief. Disbelief is when the heart knowingly rejects the truth. If you are troubled by questions you did not seek, and you wish they were not there, this is not rejection. It is a sign that faith remains in your heart.

This is not a soft reading. Companions came to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) and said, “We find within ourselves something that any of us would find too grave to utter.” He asked, “Have you actually found that?” They said yes. He said, “That is pure faith.” [Muslim]

Notice what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not say. He did not tell them to renew their faith. Instead, he told them that their discomfort at these thoughts was itself a sign of faith. A heart without faith does not recoil from such thoughts.

So do not think of yourself as among those who are lost. Nothing you have written puts you in that place.

On Not Seeing Allah Help Anyone

Now, let us turn to the more difficult part. I will not pretend that it is easy.

You say you have seen no intervention, protection, or miracle. But this assumes that if Allah were helping, you would always be able to see it. Often, Allah’s help comes in ways we do not notice: a harm that never reaches us, a difficulty that is quietly removed, or a delay that protects us from something worse.

These blessings do not always announce themselves.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “The supplication of any one of you will be answered so long as he does not become hasty.” He was asked what hastiness is. He said, “He says: ‘I have called, and I have called, and I do not see that He is answering me’ — and thereupon he becomes weary and abandons supplication.” [Bukhari and Muslim]

This describes the situation you are in. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned it because it is common, and because it is something a believer can overcome.

Suffering Is Not Evidence of Injustice

The step your reasoning takes is from “I have suffered” to “there is no just God.” That step looks obvious and is not.

Allah tells us plainly what this life is: “Who created death and life to try you as to which of you is finest in works” [Quran 67:2; Keller, The Quran Beheld]. A world made as a trial is not a world where the absence of suffering was ever the promise. And He tells us the limit within which the trial runs: “Allah does not tax any soul but what it can bear” [Quran 2:286].

From this, two important truths follow. They are not just words of comfort, but realities taught by our faith.

The first is that nothing you have endured was wasted. “No fatigue, illness, anxiety, grief, harm, or distress befalls a Muslim — even a thorn that pricks him — without Allah expiating thereby some of his sins.” [Bukhari and Muslim]

The second is that affliction is not a mark of divine displeasure. It is often the reverse. “Whomever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts.” [Sahih al-Bukhari] And: “Greatness of reward goes with greatness of trial. When Allah loves a people, He tries them.” [Tirmidhi and Ibn Maja; hasan]

I am not asking you to be grateful for your suffering. But do not see it as a sign of Allah’s displeasure or a verdict against you.

What Was Actually Promised

You prayed every day for a good life, and you felt it was too much to ask. But consider what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught us about supplication.

The Beloved Messenger of Allah (peace & blessings be upon him & his folk) said: “There is no Muslim who makes a supplication containing no sin and no severing of kinship but that Allah grants him by it one of three things: either He hastens its answer for him, or He stores it up for him in the next life, or He turns away from him an evil equal to it.” They said, “Then we will make many supplications.” He said, “Allah is more abundant.” [Musnad Ahmad]

Two of these three answers to supplication are not visible to us in this life. You may have been looking for only one kind of answer, while Allah may have given you another criterion you can see.

The ease that Allah promised comes with hardship, not instead of it. Allah says: “So verily with hardship comes utter ease: Verily with hardship comes utter ease.” [Quran 94:5–6; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

What I Would Have You Do

Three things, in order:

First, do not judge yourself harshly. This is the first burden to let go of. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave us clear words about this.

Continue to ask Allah. The only failure mentioned in the hadith is to stop asking. Allah Most High says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me.” [Bukhari and Muslim] What you expect from Allah shapes what you receive from Him.

Two. Do not carry this alone. You have been reasoning your way through the deepest question in religion by yourself, in the middle of your own suffering, which is the worst possible condition for it.

Third, seek out a teacher. Take a class on the foundations of faith. Let someone with knowledge guide you and support you.

You reached out for help. This is not the action of someone who has given up. I do not believe you have lost hope.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Use My Former Employers’ Logos?
records.question: I am starting a service-based business. To help build trust, I want to show the logos of companies where I used to work as an employee, even though I was not working for them through my new business.
records.answer:
You are allowed to display the logos, since your work history is a genuine credential. Still, Sacred requires you to be honest in how you present it. When people see a row of company logos on a service business website, they usually assume those companies are your clients.

Because that is not the case, and it could influence people to hire you, showing the logos without any explanation is considered deceptive, even if you do not say anything untrue.

How Deception Is Measured

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) passed by a heap of grain, inserted his hand into it, and discovered dampness concealed beneath the dry outer layer. He then stated, “He who deceives is not one of mine.” [Muslim]

Here, the seller did not make any false statement, but the manner in which the goods were presented was deceptive.

Cheating (ghish) and misrepresentation (tadlis) involve any instance in which a false impression is given, even if no false declaration is made.

Being honest, only if someone asks is not enough, because people form their impression before they even think to ask. Most visitors will not ask; they will just assume that a business that served those companies can be trusted, and may hire you because of that.

Keep the Logos, Fix the Frame

You do not lose any marketing value by fixing this. Just add a clear label above the logos, like “My experience includes roles at” or “Companies I have worked with in my career.”

This way, you keep your social proof, since being trusted as an employee by respected companies is a strong credential, and you avoid giving a false impression. One clear line is enough. Labels like “Clients” or “Trusted by” or logos without any explanation are still not allowed.

Be confident in choosing honesty. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the champions of truth, and the martyrs.” [Tirmidhi] Build your business on this foundation and ask Allah to bless it.

records.title: Can We Delay Marriage to Complete Our Studies?
records.question: I am 19, and she is 17. We both want to marry early, but her family opposes me, and she has about 9 years of medical school ahead of her. Should we prioritize marriage or education, and may we keep communicating with marriage as the intention?
records.answer:
I realize that this situation is important to you, and I’d like to make it clear that I take your worries seriously. Part of your question has a straightforward answer, and that answer relates to all the other points.

The Communication

Private communication is forbidden even if you intend to get married. Good intentions aren’t enough to make something permissible if it isn’t. You must cease all communication until you are married; otherwise, you will not receive blessings in this regard.

Allah (Most High) says, “But if any of you cannot afford to marry a free believing woman, then ˹let him marry˺ a believing bondwoman possessed by one of you.

Allah knows best ˹the state of˺ your faith ˹and theirs˺. You are from one another. So marry them with the permission of their owners, giving them their dowry in fairness, if they are chaste, neither promiscuous nor having secret affairs …” [Quran, 4:25]

This may be difficult, but it must be clearly stated. Instead, Sacred Law allows you to make a proposal. You should approach her guardian, and you may see her face and hands, as the Prophet did before engagement. After that, everything should be done openly. [Keller, Reliance of the Traveller, m2.2]

Why Her Family Cannot Be Bypassed

Marriage is not valid except with a guardian and two upright witnesses. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin] The guardian is an integral of the contract, since a woman does not conduct her own marriage, on the strength of the hadith, “Let no woman marry a woman to another, nor marry herself to another.” [Ibn Maja; Daraqutni]

So there is no private route to this. You should also know that a guardian’s own shortcomings in religion do not strip him of his guardianship, since most of the later Shafi’i scholars hold that a sinful man may still be a valid guardian. [Keller, Reliance of the Traveler, m3.4]

Where a guardian refuses to marry his charge to a suitable match, the recourse is the Islamic judge, who then contracts the marriage himself. [Keller, Reliance of the Traveler, m3.9] That is a formal and public process, not something two young people arrange between themselves.

Marriage or Medicine

This is not the choice you think it is. Sacred Law does not require her to give up studying medicine, and there is no urgent decision to make right now. She is seventeen, and her guardian does not accept you. At this time, you cannot make a lawful proposal, so there is nothing to choose between yet.

I want to add something gently. If she wears hijab and prays only because you encourage her, and not from her own belief, it may not last through the years ahead. Give her space to make her religious practice her own.

What to Do Now

Stop all private contact now and ask for forgiveness for what has happened. Focus on your studies and work to become the kind of person her guardian would respect.

If, when you are able to marry, her family still refuses without a valid reason, seek help from a qualified scholar or an Islamic court where you live, instead of trying to solve it yourself. If things still do not work out, our archive advises honestly: you may need to move on, and Allah will always provide for you.

You have prayed istikhara. Istikhara is not about waiting for a dream, but about asking Allah to guide you and then taking action. Part of your answer has already come through the ruling you received. Trust this process. Allah is not keeping good from you; He is arranging it for you.
references: Keller, Reliance of the Traveller, m2.2
Keller, Reliance of the Traveler, m3.4
Keller, Reliance of the Traveler, m3.9

records.title: When Is Cosmetic Treatment Permissible in Islam?
records.question: Is treating age-related wrinkles permissible in principle, and where do maintenance, treatment of sun damage, microneedling, red light therapy, and tretinoin fall?
records.answer:
The principle is shorter than the list of treatments. What the Sharia forbids is permanent alteration of a sound created form for the sake of beauty alone. Caring for the body and repairing damage done to it is a different matter, and everything you have named falls on that side of the line.

Criteria of Permissible and Unlawful Skincare

The prohibition rests on the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud (Allah be pleased with him), in which the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) cursed those who tattoo, pluck their eyebrows, and file their teeth for beauty, thereby altering the creation of Allah. [Bukhari; Muslim]

Note the qualifier in the text itself: for beauty. Imam Nawawi draws the ruling straight from it. What is forbidden is doing such things for the purpose of beautification; where there is a need, such as medical treatment or a defect, there is nothing wrong with it. [Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim]

That a visible sign of aging may be treated is settled by the Sunna. When Abu Quhafa was brought on the day the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) entered Mecca, his hair and beard white, the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Change this with something, and avoid black.” [Muslim]

Grey hair is age itself, and he ordered it changed. Aging, then, is not a category the Sharia prohibits.

Maintenance, Treatment, and Prohibited Change

There are three categories, and only the third is unlawful.

Maintenance is the care of a trust. Cleansing, moisturizing, and sunscreen preserve the body Allah has entrusted to you.

Treatment involves repairing damage, and in this case, your medical viewpoint is very significant. The most noticeable kind of facial aging is photoaging, which is damage accumulated due to ultraviolet radiation rather than the form that Allah intended it to take.

Sun damage is indeed damage. The need to treat it falls exactly within the exception stated by Imam Nawawi, and modern dermatology doesn’t alter the principle so much as it shows us how much of what we refer to as aging was, in fact, never genuine aging at all.

Changes made for the sake of beauty alone consist in the permanent alteration of a sound feature, such as reshaping a healthy nose, getting a tattoo, or having surgical work carried out on a part of the face that is in no way defective.

According to Ustadh Farid Dingle, with regard to our case, surgical procedures involve altering what Allah created in you and are therefore prohibited except when they are corrective, while non-surgical procedures are permitted provided they cause no short- or long-term harm.

Your Specific Treatments

Tretinoin is a topical medication that repairs photodamage; it treats the condition but does not reverse the changes that have already occurred. It is lawful.

Red light therapy is non-invasive and stimulates the skin’s natural repair process. It is lawful.

Superficial dermastamping and microneedling have no permanent effect; they cause a controlled superficial injury so that the skin is able to repair itself, which is simply the body carrying out what Allah has made it to do.

The procedure is permissible provided that Ustadh Farid specifies: a qualified practitioner, sterile technique, and no lasting harm. It is important to ensure that any serum used does not contain forbidden ingredients.

Principle and Practical Guidance

Look after your skin, protect it from the sun, and address the damage it has already caused. You should apply sunscreen every day, since it alone will do more than all the other things on your list combined. Reserve the scalpel for cases where true correction is needed.

You needn’t remove every line from your face, since a face that has lived has its own dignity; treat the damage, keep the body in trust, and leave the rest alone. Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, and He is the One who has written our years.

records.title: Does Removing Detailed Eyes Make 3D Models Permissible?
records.question: If I replace the detailed, realistic eyes of a pre-made 3D creature model (Godzilla) with a featureless glowing light, does it now have “incomplete features,” making it permissible to use in fights with other fictional creatures?
records.answer:
Changing the eyes as you described does not make the image incomplete on its own. In the Hanafi school, an image is considered complete if it has a head and a face that looks like a living face from a normal distance. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Even as glowing lights, the eyes are still seen as eyes, and the creature still appears complete with a head, face, and detailed body. The exception applies only if the head is removed, the face cannot be recognized, a vital limb is missing, or the image is so unrealistic that it no longer looks like a living being.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever makes an image will be charged on the Day of Judgment to breathe a spirit into it, and he will never be able to.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

Two more points. The creature’s fictional status does not change the ruling, because it still has the form of a living being. Using a pre-made model does not change that either, since editing the model and using it in your own work still amounts to making and using the image.

Having the monsters fight is not a separate issue, as long as the game contains nothing else that is impermissible.

The governing principle is that only depictions that no longer read as living beings fall outside the prohibition. So blur or cover the entire face rather than one part of it, or make the creatures look unrealistic enough that they no longer appear as living beings.

records.title: Can a Shafi‘i Woman Marry Without Her Guardian?
records.question: I am Hanafi, and I married a 20-year-old Shafi’i woman in Indonesia. She agreed freely; we had an imam, two witnesses, and the full mahr.
records.answer:
According to the Hanafi school, your marriage is valid as long as you are a suitable match (kafa’a) for her. In Hanafi law, an adult woman can marry with her own consent in front of witnesses [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar].

However, under Shafi’i law, the marriage is invalid because a guardian is required for the contract. If the father is unavailable, guardianship should go to a judge or religious authority (hakim) and not be skipped [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin; Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj].

The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, “A woman’s marriage is invalid if she marries without her guardian’s permission,” and in the same hadith it is stated that “the ruler is the guardian of someone who has no guardian.” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi; Ibn Maja]

If a father blocks all contact, his daughter can still marry. In this case, guardianship passes to the religious authority after you have made reasonable efforts to reach him and have recorded those attempts.

Because this step was possible but not taken, your marriage is now affected by the difference between the two schools.

The main principle is that your marriage should be free of doubt.

To ensure this, you should renew your marriage contract (tajdid al-nikah) as soon as possible through the wali hakim. In Indonesia, this is done at the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA).

The process is quick, meets the requirements of both schools, and protects your wife and any future children. Keep trying to contact her father kindly, and keep a record of your efforts.

records.title: Is My Prayer Valid Despite Urinary Incontinence?
records.question: I have urinary incontinence and am classified as a ma’dhur (legally excused) person.
records.answer:
Allah Most High says, “Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you.” [Quran, 2:185]

The Ritual Ablution of a Legally Excused Person

According to the Shafi’i School, your ritual ablution (wudu) typically expires with the performance of an obligatory act. A ritual ablution does not suffice for more than one obligatory act. [Shirbini, Mughni]

The ritual ablution of a legally excused person is the same as dry ablution. A person may only perform one compulsory prayer with this ablution. [Mughni al-Muhtaj] This applies when joining the prayers as well. Each requires its own ritual ablution.

Jam al-Taqdim

What you described above is effectively an apparent joining of the prayers as you read both at their respective times, albeit back-to-back. According to the relied-upon view, for the Asr to be considered joined to Dhuhr, it must be performed in its entirety during Dhuhr time.

Sulaiman Ibn Umar says, ‘A fifth condition is added: that the time of the first prayer must certainly remain. Thus, if the time certainly expires during the second prayer, or one is doubtful as to whether it has expired, then the combining of the prayers is invalid, as is the prayer, according to what al-Bulqīnī concluded through his juristic analysis. [Sulaiman Ibn Umar, Hashiyat al-Jamal]

The opposing view holds that your prayer is valid. You may adopt this view without compunction. [Ibid]

Seekers’ Guidance offers a clear, structured grasp of Shafi‘i fiqh under the guidance of qualified teachers. Do register here and begin this life-changing journey.

records.title: Is Receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) Permissible?
records.question: I have received a job offer from D-Wave Quantum, a company that develops quantum computing hardware and software. Its core business appears to be permissible.
records.answer:
It is admirable that you seek to ensure that your income is permissible. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect.’ [Quran, 65:2–3]

It is not permissible for you to receive Restricted Stock Units from D-Wave as part of your compensation, nor dispose thereof. These stocks represent impermissible income in the form of interest.

This financial income (interest) is generated from D-Wave’s consolidated cash and marketable investment securities. As of March 31, 2026, D-Wave’s consolidated cash and marketable investment securities balance totaled $588.4 million, which takes the impermissible income way above the 5% threshold established by AAOIFI.

Finance income in D-Wave appears to be a conscious business decision. Companies that state in their memorandum of association or utilize interest-generating instruments as part of their business modus operandi are shari’a non-compliant. AAOIFI states, ‘3/4/1 That the corporation does not state in its memorandum of association that one of its objectives is to deal in interest, or in prohibited goods or materials like pork (swine) and the like’. [AAOIFI]

I appreciate that this may be disappointing, especially after receiving a job offer. If possible, consider asking your employer whether the Restricted Stock Units can be replaced with an equivalent cash payment or another form of compensation.

More importantly, remember that your career is defined not solely by its financial rewards but also by the good you can achieve through it.

Continue to place your trust in Allah, seek what is lawful, and know that no one leaves something for His sake except that He replaces it with something better.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Use Fictional Characters as Metaphors for Pharaoh or the Nafs?
records.question: May one write intense violence in fiction where the point is to condemn it rather than glorify it?
records.answer:
Both of your questions are answered in the affirmative.

Writing about violence and about other impermissible matters is permissible so long as it is done to make a broader point about their immorality and impermissibility. The subject of a story is not the same as its endorsement.

A narrative that depicts cruelty in order to expose it is doing something the Quran itself does when it recounts the conduct of tyrants.

Writing fiction with the approach and the purpose you have described is likewise permissible. A character who serves as an antitype for Pharaoh or the Dajjal, or who stands for the soul or for the lower self, is a figure of speech extended into narrative. Metaphor is not misrepresentation.

What Actually Decides the Matter

The governing consideration is not the subject but the effect. Our archive’s answer on writing fiction draws the distinction plainly: between literature that is wholesome and read for good purposes, and literature that is the contrary.

So the test to keep returning to as you write is a simple one — what does this leave in the reader? If the violence sickens the reader of violence, you have done your work. If it thrills, something has gone wrong in the telling, whatever the intention was going in.

Write, then, and keep that question in front of you. It is the kind of care that turns a permissible craft into a good one.

records.title: Does the Hadith of the Sun’s Prostration Bear on the Earth’s Rotation?
records.question: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3199, it says that the sun will prostrate, but the prostration will be rejected. Will this also affect the Earth’s rotation, or something else?
records.answer:
You read the text closely and then follow it out to its consequences. That is exactly the right instinct, and it is rarer than you would think.

Here, it has run into a hidden assumption, and naming that assumption is most of the answer.

The short Answer

No. The report does not describe an event in the seen order of things such that it would show up in the mechanics of planetary motion. It is a report about the unseen, and it is not the kind of statement that competes with an account of how the earth turns.

What the Report Actually Says

Abu Dharr (Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said to him at sunset: “Do you know where it goes? … It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne, then it seeks permission and is given permission.

And a time is near when it will prostrate, and it will not be accepted from it, and it will seek permission and not be given it, and it will be told: Return whence you came. So it will rise from its west. And that is His saying, ‘And the sun runs to a resting place appointed for it: that is the ordaining of the Almighty, the All-knowing.’” [Sahih al-Bukhari 3199]

The narration is in the Sahih. The question is not whether it is sound. The question is how it is read.

The Assumption to Examine

Your question contains a premise: that the sun’s prostration is an event of the same order as the earth’s rotation (a physical motion, in physical space, occupying physical time), such that adding one would have to disturb the other.

That premise is what needs testing, not the hadith. And the commentators tested it a thousand years ago.

How the Commentators Read It

Ibn Hajar sets out the range of readings without insisting on one. He cites Ibn al-Arabi (“Some people denied its prostration, though it is sound and possible”), then notes that others took it as its permanent state of subjection, and adds his own:

“It is possible that what is meant by the prostration is the prostration of the angel charged with it; or that it prostrates by the state it is in, so that the expression signifies an increase in submission and humility at that moment.” [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari]

Three different readings, all orthodox, none of which touch celestial mechanics.

Imam Khattabi, whom Ibn Hajar quotes on the matter, puts the epistemic point cleanly: it may be that the sun rests beneath the Throne in a manner that we do not encompass. [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari]

And Ibn Kathir directly addresses the physical objection.

He notes that the scholars had long held the heavens to be spherical, and that nothing in this hadith says the sun ascends above the heavens to prostrate; rather, it sets from our sight while continuing in its own orbit, and when it reaches the point furthest from the Throne, that is the place of its prostration. [Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, cited in Qastallani, Irshad al-Sari]

Note what that settles. Even on the most literal reading available in the tradition, the report describes nothing that interrupts the sun’s course.

And When the Sun’s Prostration is Not Accepted?

The report describes the end of the world’s ordinary course, when the sun rises from the west. That is a sign of the Hour.

At that point, the question of whether the earth still rotates as it does today is no longer a live one: the ordinary order is precisely what is being wound up. So there is no consequence to trace back into physics from a moment that lies past the end of the physical order as we have it.

The Larger Habit that Will Serve You Past this One Question

Reports about the unseen are received, not reverse-engineered. Allah Most High says, “And His alone are the keys to the unseen, unknown to any but Him.” [Quran 6:59; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Imam Tahawi states the posture the scholars have always taken toward such reports: “No one is safe in his religion but one who submits to Allah Mighty and Majestic and to His Messenger (Allah bless him and give him peace), and refers the knowledge of what is unclear to him back to the One who knows it… And the foot of Islam is not firm except upon the back of submission and surrender.”

He then adds the warning that fits your question: “Whoever seeks the knowledge of what has been withheld from him, and whose understanding is not content with submission, his seeking veils him from pure monotheism, clear knowledge, and sound belief.” [Tahawi, al-Aqida al-Tahawiyya]

That is not a bar on thinking. It is a boundary marker. It says: some reports give you a fact about the unseen without giving you its mechanism, and pressing them for a mechanism produces confusion rather than knowledge.

Three Questions for the Next One

When a hadith seems to collide with something you know, run these in order.

One. Is the report sound? Here, yes: it is in the Sahih, so this is settled.

Two. Is the thing it seems to collide with actually established, or is it my own inference? Here it was an inference: that the prostration must be a physical event in the seen order.

Three. Am I reading the text in its own register, or forcing another frame onto it? Here, the register is the unseen, and the frame being imported is celestial mechanics.

Run those three, and this tension dissolves, as most do.

Let this report do what it was given to do. It is telling you that the largest, most indifferent-looking thing in your sky is a servant, under command, asking permission, and that one day permission will be refused. That is a lesson about your Lord and about the end, and it lands on the heart, not on the orbital calculation.
references: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, cited in Qastallani, Irshad al-Sari

records.title: Why Does Allah Allow Me to Keep Falling Into the Same Sin?
records.question: There is a person stuck in a difficult situation, and in a sin he cannot come out of. He is trying his best to find a way out, but keeps falling back into it, and he believes the environment he is in plays a big role.
records.answer:
This is a deeply important question. You are not seeking a legal ruling but rather asking why your sincere efforts have not resulted in relief. You are also wondering whether anyone is truly responding to your striving.

Let us address this concern first, and then consider the underlying question.

Cause and Effect Is Not an Alternative to Allah

The thought that things happen by cause and effect, and that perhaps no one is behind them, is a common confusion. In reality, cause and effect are not alternatives to Allah.

Rather, they are the means Allah Most High has created and sustains. He alone is the One who connects every cause to its effect.

“Know that if the whole community were to gather to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah had already written for you; and if they were to gather to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something Allah had already written against you.” [Sunan al-Tirmidhi; hasan sahih]

This hadith affirms that people act, but it reminds us that their actions are not decisive. The world operates through causes, but all causes are under Allah’s control.

It is important to recognize that being troubled by such thoughts is itself a sign of faith.

The Companions once came to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) and expressed that they found within themselves thoughts too grave to mention. He asked if they truly experienced this, and when they said yes, he replied, ‘That is pure faith.’ [Sahih Muslim]

Feeling discomfort at such thoughts is itself a mark of sincere belief.

You Are Reading Your Struggle Backward

The question remains: why has this sin not been lifted?

It is a mistake to see continued struggle as a sign of being abandoned. In reality, someone who is abandoned does not continue to strive.

The fact that you have fallen and risen repeatedly, that you are still seeking, asking, and trying to find a way forward, is itself a sign that Allah has not left you.

“Every son of Adam is prone to error, and the best of those who err are the oft-repentant.” [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Maja, and Sunan al-Darimi; hasan] Read that carefully. The best are not those who never fell. They are those who kept returning.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) also taught that if people did not sin, Allah would replace them with others who would sin and then seek His forgiveness, and He would forgive them. [Sahih Muslim]

This shows that returning to Allah after sin is not a failure, but a path to His mercy.

The Wisdom You Asked About

You asked about the wisdom in this. There are many possible reasons, and only Allah knows the full reality. I will mention three possible wisdoms.

First, this ongoing struggle may be breaking something within you that immediate success would have left untouched. If a person overcame his sin on the first attempt, he might believe he succeeded by his own strength.

You have been protected from this illusion. Instead, you have been given need, and neediness before Allah is the true state of a servant.

Second, the delay in relief has allowed you to continue turning to Allah in supplication. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, ‘Supplication is itself worship.’ [Sunan Abi Dawud and Sunan al-Tirmidhi; hasan sahih]

Your asking is not simply a means to an end; it is itself an act of devotion and closeness to Allah.

Third, know that nothing of your struggle is wasted. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said that no fatigue, illness, anxiety, grief, harm, or distress befalls a Muslim, even a thorn that pricks him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it. [Bukhari and Muslim]

The pain and effort you experience are themselves a means of purification.

On the Environment — Take It Seriously

You mentioned that your environment has a significant impact. This is an important point, and it is here that practical steps become essential.

The best-known case of repentance in the hadith literature ends with an instruction about location: the man who had killed a hundred was told to leave his land, because the people there were bad, and to go to a land where Allah was worshipped.

Therefore, do not limit yourself to praying for relief from the sin. Take practical steps to change what is within your ability.

Identify the specific triggers—whether it is a particular time, device, place, person, or state of mind—and create a barrier between yourself and the cause of the sin. Do not rely solely on willpower; instead, introduce practical obstacles. Change what you can when you are most vulnerable. Surround yourself with people who inspire you to do better.

Establish a regular act of worship to anchor your routine. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, ‘The most beloved of deeds to Allah is the most constant, even if little.’ [Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim]

A small, consistent practice is more beneficial than a large one that is quickly abandoned.

What Not to Do

Never stop repenting, even if you fear you may fall again. Each act of repentance is accepted, and a setback does not erase your sincere turning to Allah.

Do not judge Allah’s care for you by whether the sin has been removed. Rather, recognize His concern in the fact that you still care and are striving to change.

Do not try to overcome this alone. Seek support from someone who can guide you consistently, such as a teacher, counselor, or a sincere companion. Most people need help to break free from deeply rooted habits.

“This religion is easy, and no one ever strains against the religion without it overcoming him. So aim straight, draw near, take glad tidings.” [Sahih al-Bukhari]

Remain steadfast, strive to draw closer to Allah, and accept the glad tidings. These words are meant for people in your situation.
references: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Maja, and Sunan al-Darimi; hasan
Sunan Abi Dawud and Sunan al-Tirmidhi; hasan sahih

records.title: What Does a Moderator Owe a Muslim Community He Cannot Fully Police?
records.question: One of the problems we have is gender interactions. We have male-only and female-only channels, but there is a general channel that both males and females can access, and sometimes conversations there can be unnecessary.
records.answer:
Caring for so many young Muslims is a great trust. It is clear you feel this responsibility deeply. Know that you are not required to carry more than what the Sacred Law asks of you.

You are not responsible for preventing every wrong on your server. Your duty is to set up a system that discourages wrong and to respond to what you see. You are accountable for your effort and the system you put in place.

The results are with Allah, and He does not hold you to what is beyond your ability.

You Are a Custodian, Not a Camera

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.” [Sahih al-Bukhari; Sahih Muslim]

Mulla Ali al-Qari, glossing this, relays from Sharh al-Sunna that the shepherd here means “the guardian entrusted with what is under his charge.” [Mulla Ali al-Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih]

Entrusted. Not omniscient. A trustee is answerable for how he handles what is in his keeping, not for what happens while he is asleep.

This is the language of trust (amana), and Allah frames it so: “Verily Allah charges all of you to deliver trusts to those they are due to faithfully.” [Quran 4:58; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Your amana is the space and the young people in it. Discharging it means running the space well. It does not mean reading every line.

The hadith you are probably measuring yourself against says the same thing, if you read it closely. “Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand; and if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.” [Sahih Muslim]

Notice the two conditions built into it. Whoever sees, not whoever might have seen had he been online. And if he is unable, the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) himself wrote the exemption into the command.

A mod who was asleep at 3 a.m. did not see it, and could not have. There is no sin on him for it.

The SpongeBob Problem Is Not a Modesty Problem

Here is where a category has slipped. Immodest conversation between men and women is what your gender rules exist to prevent. A debate about whether SpongeBob has a driver’s license is idle and falls under the kind of idle talk our religion discourages. Allah describes the believers as those who turn away from idle words.

This is a quality to strive for, not a rule to enforce strictly on young people. A general channel will have light conversation.

If you treat every unnecessary comment as a violation, you may tire your moderators and push young people away. It is important to keep the main boundaries clear line that actually matters.

Keep your main rules clear. They are there to prevent immodesty, flirtation, private conversations, and harm. They are not meant to make every sentence serious. Allow some light conversation.

Remember the difference between what your space allows and what it encourages. Your rules set the minimum standard.

The culture you build—what you praise, what you model, and how your moderators speak—raises the standard. Raising the standard comes from positive example, not from making the rules too strict.

The Worse-Server Argument Is Sound, and the Scholars Say So

You mentioned not wanting to be too strict because other servers are much worse. This is not something to apologize for. It is a valid consideration in fiqh, and scholars mention it as a condition for forbidding wrong.

records.title: Is a Half-Sister and Her Daughters Mahram?
records.question: Is my half-sister from my mother’s previous marriage unmarriageable kin (mahram) to me, and are her daughters unmarriageable kin to me as well?
records.answer:
Your half-sister through your mother is your unmarriageable kin (mahram) for life, and so are her daughters and their daughters after them.

In the Hanafi school, what makes a woman your sister in the Shariah is that she shares a parent with you. One shared parent is enough.

A sister through your father and mother, a sister through your father alone, and a sister through your mother alone all stand in the same place: marriage between you is never lawful.

Imam Kasani (Allah have mercy on him) states that a man’s sisters are unlawful to him by the explicit text of the Quran, whether they are through both parents, through the father alone, or through the mother alone, and he gives the reason plainly: the word “sister” in the verse applies without restriction. [Kasani, Badaʾiʿ al-Sanaʾiʿ]

Allah Most High says:

حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَـٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمْ وَعَمَّـٰتُكُمْ وَخَـٰلَـٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأُخْتِ

“It has been made unlawful for you to wed your female ancestors, your female descendants, your sisters and half sisters, your aunts and great-aunts, on up, from your father’s side or your mother’s, the female descendants of your brothers or half brothers, the female descendants of your sisters or half sisters…” [Quran 4:23; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The verse answers both halves of your question in the same clause. It names half-sisters and their female descendants.

Imam Mawsili (Allah have mercy on him) enumerates the seven kinds of unmarriageable kin by lineage on exactly this basis: mothers, however far up, daughters however far down, sisters from whichever side they may be; the paternal and maternal aunts, all of them, and a brother’s daughters and a sister’s daughters, however far down the line descends. [Mawsili, al-Ikhtiyar li-Taʿlil al-Mukhtar]

So your sister’s daughters are your unmarriageable kin, and so are their daughters, and the line does not run out.

Nothing in this turns on your mother’s earlier marriage or on how it ended. The tie that decides the ruling is the mother you share, and that tie cannot be undone.

A Clear Distinction

One distinction is worth keeping clear, since it can easily blur within a single household. If the girl is your mother’s daughter, she is your sister and your unmarriageable kin.

If she shares no parent with you at all, say she is the daughter of your mother’s former husband by another wife, then she is a stepsister, and stepsiblings are not unmarriageable kin to one another.

In practice, then, your sister and her daughters are close family to you and not strangers.

She need not cover before you as she would before an unrelated man; you may be alone together, and you may travel with her as her unmarriageable male relative. The same holds with her daughters, since you are their maternal uncle.

One Shared Parent Is Enough

The governing principle is simple: a single shared parent establishes full unmarriageable kinship, and that kinship descends to a sister’s daughters and to their daughters after them.

So treat your sister and her daughters as the near family Allah has made them. Visit them, keep the ties of kinship warm, and know that the closeness these rulings protect is itself part of what they were given for.

records.title: Is the Quran Timeless if Slavery Rulings Changed?
records.question: If the Quran is timeless, why are some of its rulings, like those on slavery, no longer applicable?
records.answer:
You have honestly followed a hard question, and the fear beneath it deserves a straight answer.

Nothing in the Quran has been repealed. The verses that once regulated slavery stand in the Book as they were revealed, and no one has struck a word of them out.

What ended was the institution those verses regulated, and revelation had been working to end it long before the modern world arrived at the same conclusion.

Three different things are folded together in your question, and separating them dissolves most of the difficulty.

Abrogation closed when revelation closed. During the lifetime of the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace), Allah Most High replaced some rulings with others, a process known as abrogation (naskh). It ended when the religion was completed:

«ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلْإِسْلَـٰمَ دِينًا»

“This day have I wholly perfected for you your religion, and completed upon you My blessing; And I please that Islam be your religion.” [Quran 5:3; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Once a thing is complete, nothing is left to add to it, and nothing after it revokes any part of it. So abrogation is not what happened to the rulings on slavery, and neither is anyone’s editing.

A ruling can stand at full strength while the occasion it addresses disappears. Much of the Sharia speaks to situations that may or may not arise in a given life. The rules for shortening the prayer on a journey take hold of the hour you travel, and they were not repealed on all the days you stayed home.

Ibn al-Qayyim (Allah have mercy on him) states the principle plainly: “A ruling revolves with its cause (illa) and its occasioning factor (sabab), present when they are present and absent when they are absent, and for this reason, when the Lawgiver attaches a ruling to an occasioning factor or a cause, that ruling falls away when the two fall away.” [Ibn al-Qayyim, Iʿlam al-Muwaqqiʿin]

The rulings that governed slavery worked this way. They regulate a relationship between two people, and where that relationship does not exist, they have nothing to attach to. The law did not move. The world did.

This needs to be said carefully, because a false claim stands very close to it. Rulings are not rewritten to fit an era.

The Hanafi codification known as the Majalla carries a maxim, at article 39, allowing that rulings may change as the times change, and its commentator Ali Haydar (Allah have mercy on him) fixes the scope exactly:

“The rulings that change with the change of times are the rulings resting on custom and habit, because as times change, people’s needs change, and upon that change, custom and habit shift as well, and with the shift of custom and habit, the rulings change.” [Ali Haydar, Durar al-Hukkam]

Custom and habit, then. A ruling grounded in a text of revelation was never on that list, and no age gets to put it there.

Slavery was an institution revelation inherited and set about ending. Every society in that world ran it. Revelation did not found the institution; it took hold of one already running, narrowed the way in to a single channel, and opened every possible way out.

Freeing a person became an expiation for sin, a form of charity, and in places a plain obligation. Two verses of Sura al-Balad put the freeing of a slave (manumission) at the height of what a human being is asked to climb: «وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْعَقَبَةُ» «فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ»

“And what may teach you what the final sheer impasse is? To free a human neck from bondage;” [Quran 90:12–13; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

And the freeing of bondsmen is written into the Quran’s own definition of devotion, in the same breath as keeping the prayer and giving the due alms [Quran 2:177].

When a body of law narrows one door and opens ten, the direction of travel is not hard to read.

So the end of slavery is not a concession the Sharia made to modern sensibilities. It is the Sharia’s own aim arriving. Our answer on the treatment of war captives says the rest plainly: the institution is obsolete, and the scholars of Islam condemn it.

What revelation worked to end, no Muslim may work to revive.

The same principle runs in the other direction, too, which is how you can tell it is a principle and not a convenience.

Some exegetes mention the old distinction between free and enslaved women as one reason behind the command to cover; slavery is gone, and that obligation is untouched, because it rests on the command itself and on modesty, not on a wisdom a commentator suggests for it.

Timeless Means Nothing Expires, Not That Everything Is Running at Once

A law is timeless because none of it lapses, and none of it can be edited. Timelessness was never a claim that every provision runs in every century. The rulings on slavery were never withdrawn.

They sit in the Book, intact, describing a world the Book itself was dismantling, and they are silent now for the best reason a ruling can be silent: what they governed is gone.

Bring the next question like this one to a teacher while it is still a question, before it hardens into something heavier, and consider a course in the foundations of Islamic law, where this distinction is the first tool you are handed.

The Book that told you to free a human neck from bondage is the same Book in your hands, unchanged in a single letter. The unease you felt was not weak faith. It was a conscience this very Book trained, doing what it was trained to do.

records.title: Can I Take a Student Loan If the Government Pays the Interest?
records.question: Am I sinning if I take out a student loan, live only on the bursary, and hold the loan untouched to return it before the interest begins, when the Canadian government pays the bank’s interest until then?
records.answer:
Your concern to seek what is pleasing to Allah in a system that does not make it easy is itself a praiseworthy effort.

Allah rewards those who strive for what is right, even when the path is not clear. According to the Hanafi school, the issue lies in signing the contract itself.

The loan becomes impermissible because it includes a condition for increase (riba), and this is established as soon as you sign, regardless of who pays the interest in the end.

Ali Haydar (Allah have mercy on him) states the rule in a single line in the standard commentary on the Majalla: “Every loan in which a benefit is stipulated is unlawful.” [Ali Haydar, Durar al-Hukkam]

The key point here is that the prohibition is in the agreement to pay extra, not in who actually pays it. A loan in Shariah is meant to be repaid in the same amount, and any agreed-upon benefit beyond that, such as interest, is not permitted.

Imam Kasani (Allah have mercy on him) defines a corrupt condition as one that runs counter to what the contract requires and penetrates to the very core of the contract [Kasani, Badai al-Sanai].

In your agreement, the interest term sits in that core. The government’s undertaking sits alongside it.

The government’s promise to pay the interest while you study does not remove the interest clause from the contract. It is not a true waiver.

As you described, the interest is still part of the agreement, becomes due, and is paid by the government to the bank. This may ease your burden, but it does not change the nature of the contract you have signed.

Because the issue is in signing the contract itself, even if you do not use the loan and return it before interest is charged, the problematic condition remains.

Your plan may save you from paying interest, but it does not remove the contract’s impermissible term.

The Canadian mechanics differ from the British schemes our earlier answers address; the contract does not. Allah Most High drew the line at the kind of contract itself. He says: وَأَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟, “while Allah has made trade lawful and usury unlawful.” [Quran 2:275; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

It is important to look honestly at your situation. In our tradition, exceptions to clear prohibitions are allowed only in cases of true necessity, and that necessity has a specific meaning.

As Mufti Taqi Usmani (Allah preserve him) explains, quoting Ibn al-Humam (Allah have mercy on him), necessity is when a person would perish or come close to it if they do not take the prohibited step.

Facing financial difficulties or concerns about tuition is a hardship, but it does not constitute a necessity.

From what you have described, you plan to live on the bursary. If the bursary is enough for your needs, then the loan is only a backup, not your main support.

If you ever reach a point where you truly cannot meet your basic needs without this loan, please write again with the details. That would be a different situation, and we can look at it together.

Take the Bursary and Leave the Loan

Take practical steps. Write to your financial aid office and ask if the grant or bursary can be given to you without the loan. Apply for scholarships and work-study opportunities. See if a lighter course load would still be covered by your bursary.

Ask a trusted family member or your local Muslim community if they can help with an interest-free loan (qard hasan). If you have already signed the loan, cancel it and return the money as soon as you can.

Turn to Allah in repentance. Allah is more ready to forgive than we are to seek forgiveness.

One promise is worth holding as you close that door: “And whoever fears Allah, He grants him a way out of every plight, And provides for him whence he could not even guess.” [Quran 65:2–3; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

It is made to the person who declines the easy door precisely because it was the easy one. Today, that person is you.

records.title: Which of My Web Development Tasks Count as Assisting in Sin?
records.question: I work on a fruit-selling website whose stock photos show some of a woman’s nakedness. Which of my five tasks are direct and which indirect assistance in sin? Is my salary lawful, and may I have AI place the images so I never see them?
records.answer:
Your concern is praiseworthy, and your confusion is understandable. These are new situations, but the principles remain the same.

Of your five tasks, only the fourth is not permitted in the Hanafi school. Uploading these photos yourself is direct involvement in what is not allowed.

The other four tasks are permitted: optimizing a site that already has such images, working on the backend or non-visual aspects, rebuilding a site where the images are already present, and migrating posts where some comments might contain impermissible pictures.

The Ruling Follows Your Own Hand, Not the Name of the Project

Hanafi scholars distinguish between the one who does something directly (mubashir) and the one who only causes it indirectly (mutasabbib). The direct doer is held to a stricter standard.

Ghanim al-Baghdadi (Allah have mercy on him) states the rule: “The immediate doer is liable even if he neither intended nor transgressed, and the indirect causer is not liable unless he transgresses.” [Ghanim al-Baghdadi, Majma al-Damanat, 1.165]

So, when considering any task, do not focus on the project name. Rather, ask whether you are the one placing the image before others.

A migration script simply moves content without your choice, and the mere possibility that a comment might contain something impermissible is not a reason for worry.

Optimizing and rebuilding are permitted in themselves. Simply avoid looking at the images as you work. If, however, rebuilding requires you to place those images again, then that becomes the fourth case.

Where Indirect Involvement Still Carries Blame

Allah Most High says:

وَتَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ

“And aid one another in devotion to your Lord in every good and godfearingness, and do not aid one another in sin and transgression.” [Quran 5:2; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Ibn Abidin (Allah have mercy on him) explains that if you know your action will help a specific wrong, it becomes prohibitively disliked (makruh tahriman) in the Hanafi school, which is sinful though not strictly unlawful.

If you do not know, or if harm is only possible and not certain, then there is no blame.

Your Wage Is Lawful, and Your Worship Is Not Held Hostage

Neither the fourth case nor looking at such images is among the major sins (kaba’ir). Both require repentance (tawba), and Allah accepts repentance from His servants.

Your salary remains fully lawful, as it is payment for your work as a developer.

Any mistake in your work is attached to the action itself, not to your income.

You do not need to estimate or give away any part of your income. Since your earnings are lawful, the concern you mention about acceptance does not apply to you.

Asking to Be Excused from This Task Is a True Solution. Using AI to Avoid the Images Is Not the Same

Ask your employer to excuse you from working with these images, rather than assigning the task to someone else.

If your employer assigns it to another, that person has chosen to take it and is responsible for it. This is a real way out, and you are not passing the responsibility on.

Using AI is not the same, and your caution is correct. As explained before, an AI-generated image that resembles a human has the same ruling as a human image. What is not permitted in a photograph is also not permitted in a generated image.

If you use a tool to place the images, no other person has chosen to do so. The tool is not responsible.

You are still the one acting, even if indirectly. Not seeing the image protects you from looking at what is not permitted, but it does not change the ruling of the fourth case.

Keep the Work, Hand Back the Images

Responsibility is with the one who acts, and it is knowledge that makes a lawful act blameworthy. Keep your job, and do the backend work and migrations with peace of mind. This week, ask to be excused from placing those images. Someone who is this careful about his work is not someone whose worship Allah will turn away.

records.title: What Is the Ruling on Refunding Worn Shoes?
records.question: I bought shoes for my son, and after about a month of wear, we found that the two shoes were different sizes.
records.answer:
Yes, you may return the shoes as requested and accept the full refund. Do so with a clear heart and no worry.

The refund comes to you in a way you might not expect. The shoes were faulty when you bought them. In the Hanafi school, a fault at the time of sale gives the buyer the option of defect (khiyar al-ayb). But this option does not remain after later events.

Al-Majalla, the Ottoman code of Hanafi law, states that if a new defect appears while the goods are with the buyer and an old defect is then discovered, the buyer cannot return them. Instead, the claim is only for a price reduction.

A month of wear is a new fault. If your son kept wearing the shoes after you noticed the mismatch, that would be considered accepting the fault.

So you could not have demanded this refund. But you did not ask for it; they offered it to you.

A sale can be undone if both sides agree. This is called rescission by mutual consent (iqala). Al-Majalla makes this clear: both parties may end the sale by agreement after it is completed.

The code even mentions a case like yours. If the seller agrees to take back goods with an old fault after a new fault has appeared, the claim for a price reduction no longer applies. The buyer can return the goods or keep them.

The manufacturer’s offer is this agreement. It gives you a new, valid reason to return the shoes, even if your earlier right had expired.

The only thing that could have made this doubtful is hiding the truth. But you were open: you told them the shoes had been worn, and your photos showed both the wear and the fault.

They made their decision with full knowledge, and the price was theirs to release. This is the mutual consent Allah Most High asks for in trade.

يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَأْكُلُوٓا۟ أَمْوَٰلَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِٱلْبَـٰطِلِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَـٰرَةً عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنكُمْ

“O you who believe, devour not your wealth between you through falsehood; But only through trade by your complete mutual consent.” [Quran 4:29; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The virtue in this exchange is theirs. You owe nothing for the month your son used the shoes. If you wish, you may offer something in thanks, but you are not required to.

One point to check: if you bought the shoes from a shop rather than the manufacturer, their payment is a voluntary act of goodwill, not a formal return of the sale. They are free to offer it, and you are free to accept it. The ruling is the same in both cases.

Their Consent Is What Makes the Refund Lawful

The key principle here is consent. A seller may release what belongs to him, and once he does, you are not taking more than your right. Return the shoes as agreed, keep your records, and let your heart be at ease. Your honesty in this matter is praiseworthy, and it will benefit you in greater matters as well.

records.title: How Should I Relate to People Who Have Mocked Allah or Islam?
records.question: What is the ruling regarding interaction, friendship, and closeness with three types of people
records.answer:
You have sorted this carefully, and I will answer in your order. But let me settle the last part first, because it is the one carrying weight for you.

No, You Do Not Become a Disbeliever

Keeping company with someone who has mocked the religion does not remove you from Islam. Not if you knew, not if you found out later, not if you kept them close afterward.

Faith is the heart’s assent (tasdiq) to what the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) brought. What is established by assent is undone only by rejection: the heart’s own denial of what it knows.

Nothing another person says can reach into your heart and reverse it. The consequence of keeping bad company falls entirely in the register of sin and blameworthiness, and depending on the case, may be no sin at all. It never touches Iman.

Set that fear down, and the rest of the question becomes manageable.

What the Prohibition Actually Is

Much confusion here comes from reading the verses on alliance (muwalat) as a general ban on warmth towards non-Muslims. They are not that, and the commentators say so plainly.

Imam Tabari, on the verse most often cited in this discussion, settles what taking them as allies means: “Allah, exalted be His mention, forbade the believers all of them to take the Jews and Christians as helpers and confederates against the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and others besides them; and He informed them that whoever takes them as helper, confederate and ally in place of Allah and His Messenger and the believers is one of them in partisanship against Allah and against His Messenger and the believers.” [Tabari, Jami al-Bayan]

And on the clause that frightens people most, “whoever of you allies with them is of them,” he says: “whoever allies with them and aids them against the believers is of the people of their religion and creed.” [Tabari, Jami al-Bayan]

Read what he specifies: helpers and confederates against the believers. Aiding them against the believers. Not neighborliness, not business, not affection.

Imam Jassas, our own school’s commentator on the legal verses, glosses the term the same way.

He defines allegiance itself: “Allegiance runs in two directions. One of them is the one who attends to the affairs of one whose conduct he approves, by support, aid, and protection.” [Jassas, Ahkam al-Quran]

And on the verse forbidding the believers to take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers, he draws the ruling: “The verse entails the prohibition of seeking victory through the disbelievers, seeking their aid, leaning upon them, and placing trust in them.” [Jassas, Ahkam al-Quran]

Support, aid, protection, reliance, trust in a contest: that is the register the prohibition occupies.

And the Quran itself draws the line in two consecutive verses: “Allah but forbids you from those who have fought against you in religion and expelled you from your homes and abetted your expulsion, to help or befriend them as allies.” [Quran 60:9; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

And immediately before it, of everyone else: “Allah does not forbid you from those who have not fought against you in religion or expelled you from your homes to be good and kind to them and show them justice: Verily Allah loves the thoroughly just.” [Quran 60:8; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Siding against the believers is what is barred. Kindness and justice are commanded.

An Objection Worth Naming

I should tell you that Imam Jassas says something harder a few lines earlier, and you may come across it.

Having gathered the verse on not taking Allah’s enemies as allies together with reports about not residing among the idolaters, he writes: “These verses and reports indicate that the disbelievers ought to be dealt with in harshness and coldness rather than gentleness and softness, so long as there is no situation in which one fears for the loss of his life, or the loss of some of his limbs, or great harm befalling him in himself; for if he fears that, he is permitted to display gentleness and alliance without holding it as a belief.” [Jassas, Ahkam al-Quran]

Two things about that passage. Look first at what he is commenting on: the verses and reports he has just assembled all concern enemies in a state of open hostility: those who fight, expel, and are to be broken from.

Look second at what he says in the next line, which I quoted above: allegiance means support, aid, and protection. He is describing a posture toward a hostile enemy, not a rule for your neighbor or your cousin.

And the Quran has already settled the case, his run of verses does not reach: “Allah does not forbid you from those who have not fought against you in religion or expelled you from your homes to be good and kind to them and show them justice.” [Quran 60:8; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

A ruling framed for wartime does not travel to peacetime by itself. Read Jassas beside that verse, and the picture is coherent: severity where there is hostility, goodness and justice where there is none.

Your Second Group: Non-Muslims Who Do Not Mock

This one is straightforward. Ordinary friendship, good treatment, business, neighborliness, and kinship with non-Muslims who do not attack the religion are permitted. Quran 60:8 above is the governing text, and it names goodness and justice as what Allah loves.

Apostates are a harder case in the books, because turning away from Islam after entering it is treated more gravely than never having entered.

But even there, the concern is the effect on your own religion and the message that keeping close company sends, not the loss of your faith. Judge it by that: does the closeness pull at your religion, or not?

Your First Group: Those Who Have Mocked

Here, the text is precise, and it is more merciful than people expect: “When you hear the verses of Allah denied and mocked, sit no more with them until they turn to something wholly else.” [Quran 4:140; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

And: “when you see those who idly discuss Our verses, get up and leave them till they turn to something wholly else.” [Quran 6:68; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Read the condition and the release together. What triggers the obligation is the mockery happening, and what lifts it is their turning to something else. Both verses are bound to the act, not to the person.

You are commanded to leave the gathering while it is going on. You are not commanded to sever a person permanently for something once said.

Three things follow.

If it is happening now, leave. That is the direct command.

If it was said and is past, the ruling on sitting with them has lapsed. What remains is your own prudence: does their company harm your religion?

And if it was ignorance rather than contempt, which you rightly raise, the case is lighter still, and correcting them gently is worth more than withdrawing from them.

Many people say indefensible things about the religion, having never once been told it accurately.

Relatives Are a Separate Case

This cuts across everything above, and it is where the most damage is done by an overly strict reading.

Kinship rights are not conditional on the relative’s religion or conduct. Allah commands good companionship, even of parents who work actively to pull you into associating partners with Him: “if they do their utmost to make you worship with Me what you know nothing of, obey them; But companion them for the time in this world with gracious kindness.” [Quran 31:15; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Obey them not, and companion them with gracious kindness. In one breath. If that is the standard for a parent calling you to shirk, then a relative who once mocked the religion in ignorance or anger keeps their rights of kinship in full.

Do not cut them off. Do not sit with them while they are mocking.

Your Third Group, and Your Maxim

Your use of the principle that certainty is not lifted by doubt is apt, and I want to affirm it, but check what you are applying it to.

Applied to the words: if you are unsure whether what was said counted as mockery, the default holds. The certain thing is a Muslim’s standing and the general permissibility of the company; a doubt does not overturn it. So do not act on a suspicion.

Applied to yourself: your own Islam is the certainty, and nothing you have described comes close to a doubt against it, let alone an established one.

And if you later learn for certain that they did mock, and you keep them close? You are not a disbeliever.

You may or may not be sinful, depending on what the closeness does: does it normalize contempt for the religion, does it wear at your own faith, or is it a kinship you are maintaining while making your position clear? Judge that honestly and act on it.

On the Schools of Aqida

The Asharis and Maturidis do not differ in substance on your question: keeping company does not remove a person from Islam. Where discussion exists in the books, it concerns the mocker’s own standing, not the standing of the one who sits with him.

And on that, one caution is worth more than any detail I could give you. Takfir, declaring a specific person outside Islam, is not for a private individual to undertake.

It has conditions that are difficult to establish, and the tradition treats it as dangerous precisely because getting it wrong is grave in both directions. Leave it to those qualified to rule.

In Practice

Leave any gathering where the religion is being mocked, while it is being mocked. That is the command, and it is the whole of what is obligatory here.

Keep your kinship ties regardless.

Choose your close friends by what they do to your religion, not by a category you have assigned them.

Correct ignorance kindly where you can; you may find that most of what alarmed you dissolves under a straight explanation.

And do not audit your own faith over the company you keep. That question has an answer: your faith is intact.
