records.question: A class at my masjid on the basics of purity and prayer has left me with far more doubts than I had before, and although I am trying to use the Hanafi rule that certainty is not lifted by doubt, I have ended up back where I was before I began practicing.
records.answer:
You went to that class to strengthen your prayer and came out frightened, and carrying that alone for a week is hard.

Do not stop praying; nothing you have described has broken your wudu or your prayer, and the report that frightened you is not established.

The Report Is Not Established

The wording is on record. Al-Sakhawi (Allah have mercy on him) gives it as “Whoever deliberately abandons the prayer, his name is written on a door of the Fire, among those who enter it,” and traces it to Abu Nuaym’s al-Hilya from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (Allah be pleased with him). [al-Sakhawi, al-Ajwiba al-Mardiyya]

Notice where it is not. It is not in al-Bukhari, not in Muslim, and not in the four Sunan.

The chain preserved for it turns on Ismaʿil ibn Yahya al-Taymi, of whom Ibn al-Qaysarani (Allah have mercy on him) records that he narrates fabrications from trustworthy men, and reports that have no basis. [Ibn al-Qaysarani, Tadhkirat al-Huffaz]

That is not a report to build fear on, and it should not have been handed to a room of beginners.

The weight of the prayer is not in question, and I will not soften it. But the established warnings address a man who knows, is able, and turns his back.

You are a convert of one year who is praying, frightened, and asking. You are not that man. You are his opposite.

You Have the Right Principle, and You Are Running It Backward

The Hanafi rule you named is the correct one, and al-Hamawi (Allah have mercy on him) sets it out in his commentary on al-Ashbah wa al-Nazaʾir: what was established stays as it was, so whoever is certain of purity and doubts whether he broke it is in a state of purity, and whoever is certain he broke it and doubts whether he purified himself is not. [al-Hamawi, Ghamz Uyun al-Basaʾir]

Read that as an instruction rather than as a test. It does not ask you to weigh the doubt. It tells you the matter is already settled, and you are free to stop thinking.

That is where it has gone wrong for you. You are treating it as a question to answer each time afresh, which means you examine every doubt before dismissing it, and the examining is what feeds it.

What you are describing has a name in our tradition, waswasa, baseless misgiving, recognized and treated for centuries. You do not need to go and read about it. You need to stop supplying it.

The Religion Is Ease, and You Have Been Straining

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “This religion is ease, and no one ever strains against the religion without it overcoming him. So aim straight, draw near, take glad tidings, and seek help by traveling at morning, at evening, and a portion of the night.” [Sahih al-Bukhari]

Read the middle clause slowly, because it describes your week. No one strains against the religion without it overcoming him.

You have been straining. And the instruction that follows is to aim straight, draw near, and take glad tidings. Nowhere in it are you told to try harder.

He also said, “When I command you to do something, do as much of it as you are able.” [Sahih al-Bukhari] As much as you are able. Not perfectly, and not free of doubt.

A One-Month Rule: Do Not Repeat Anything

For one month, and then we look at it again.

Make wudu once, properly, the way you were taught. Do not repeat it and do not check it until something you actually saw or felt breaks it. A suspicion is not something.

Pray each prayer once. Do not repeat a prayer for a doubt about your wudu, a doubt about the number of rakʿas, or a word you think you mispronounced. If you finished it, it counted.

Read nothing further on purity this month. You have enough. More will not settle you; it will give the doubt fresh material to work with.

When a doubt arrives, say “I have wudu” or “I prayed,” once, and move. Do not argue with it. You cannot win an argument with something that is not making one.

And keep going to the class. Take what helps you and let the rest go past. You are not required to master the syllabus this year.

Holding On by Your Fingertips Is Worth More

You wrote that this is exactly why you did not practice at first. Look at what that admits. You were not praying; you began anyway, and now, under real pressure, you are still here asking rather than walking off. That is not weak faith.

That is a man holding on by his fingertips, which is harder than holding on comfortably and worth a great deal more.

Aisha (Allah be pleased with her) relates that the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “The most beloved of deeds to Allah Most High is the most constant of them, even if little.” [Sahih Muslim] Little and constant.

Bring the doubts to one person instead of chasing them yourself: the imam who taught the class, or any teacher who will give you five minutes.

Bring them in a weekly batch rather than as they arrive, because a doubt held until Thursday usually dissolves before then.

If there is nobody at hand, book an Office Hours session with us and we will sit with you:

Pray tonight. Once. Do not repeat it.

May Allah settle your heart and keep you firm.

records.title: Can a Father Compel His Adult Virgin Daughter to Marry?
records.question: In the Shafi’i and Maliki schools, does a guardian have the right to compel a marriage upon an adult virgin, and does her silence count as agreement?
records.answer:
If you are the young woman this question concerns, please know that Allah sees your wishes regarding your marriage and His Sacred Law honors them. Many of these rules were created to protect people in your situation.

Both schools agree that a father’s right to compel marriage for his virgin daughter continues after she becomes an adult, but there are conditions to protect her.

When asked for permission, her silence is taken as agreement. This respects her modesty, rather than forcing consent she does not give.

The Shafi’i School

The main view is that the father, and after him the paternal grandfather, can arrange the marriage of a virgin without her permission, whether she is a minor or an adult.

Seven conditions apply: there is no clear conflict between her and her father, no clear conflict between her and the suitor, the suitor is a suitable match, he can pay the dowry, she receives the standard dowry for her peers in local currency, the suitor is not someone whose company would be a hardship for her (like a blind or elderly man), and she is not required to perform hajj that year.

Of these, three affect the contract’s validity: no conflict, suitability, and the suitor’s ability to pay. Once she is mature, it is recommended to ask her permission. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin; Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj; Keller, Reliance of the Traveller, m3.13]

After she has been married and the marriage is consummated, she is considered previously married (thayyib). At that point, no guardian can arrange her marriage without her clear permission. Her silence is not enough anymore.

The Maliki School

The Maliki school has its own approach to this question.

Since SeekersGuidance does not have active Maliki faculty, it is best to ask a qualified Maliki scholar for a reliable explanation and how it applies to your situation.

The Silence Rule

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “A woman who has been previously married has a greater right to her own affairs than to her guardian, and as for a virgin, her permission is required and her silence constitutes her consent.” [Muslim]

Looking at the ruling mentioned above, the hadith makes clear how a virgin’s consent is expressed, not whether it is necessary.

In the case where a guardian other than the father or grandfather is responsible for arranging the marriage, her consent is required, and her silence is taken as consent.

If the father arranges the marriage, exercising his right of compulsion, then her consent is not required, and her silence is regarded as agreement. In each instance, Sharia treats silence leniently, on the grounds that a young woman might be too shy to speak.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The Shafi’i jurists consider compulsion to be a trust which they carry out for her advantage, and it is precisely those conditions which maintain it in that form. The basic principle is that harm shall not be caused nor shall harm be returned.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “[Let there be] no harm or reciprocation of harm.” [Ibn Maja; Malik; Daraqutni]

Khansa’ bint Khidham al-Ansariyya (Allah be pleased with her), who had previously been married, went to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) since her father had arranged her marriage against her will; the Prophet then canceled it for her. [Bukhari]

You should ask her, hear her reply, and only proceed if she is happy. In the case where a father arranges his daughter’s marriage despite her clear objection, even if he adheres to the literal meaning of the law, jurists consider this to be wrong.

When giving advice to a family, it is important to obtain their clear consent, put it in writing, and then abide by your country’s civil laws, since these laws are also intended to protect them.
references: Keller, Reliance of the Traveller, m3.13

records.title: Is Divorce Valid Under Coercion and Threats?
records.question: I had an extramarital affair, but I ended it and repented. After I ended things, the woman threatened me in public, saying she would tear off my clothes unless I divorced my wife.
records.answer:
What happened to you was extortion, and you are not the only believer who has faced this kind of situation.

The Ruling

Based on what you described, the divorce did not occur, and your marriage remains valid. In the Shafi‘i school, a divorce said under wrongful pressure (ikrah) does not count.

Why Coercion Covers What Happened to You

In our school, coercion is not just about threats to your life or safety. Imam Suyuti explains that humiliation and public shaming, like being slapped in public or having your face blackened, are also forms of coercion [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir].

Reliance of the Traveller gives the same rule: a divorce is not valid from “someone who is wrongfully coerced to do it, as when one is threatened with death, dismemberment, being severely beaten, or even mere verbal abuse or a slight beating if the person being coerced is someone whose public image is important and would thereby suffer” [Ibn Naqib al-Misri, ‘Umdat al-Salik].

A real threat to strip you in public is even more serious than these examples.

There are four conditions: the person making the threat must be able to do it, you must have believed she would, you could not get away or stop it, and the harm was about to happen.

In your case, since she had done this before and you were on a public road with no way out, all these conditions were met.

The Oath You Made Inwardly

Your private protest does not change your case. When coercion is proven, the school does not require you to have any mental reservation for the divorce to be invalid [Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj].

What matters is that you did not mean the divorce. If you had meant it in your heart, then it would have counted, because intention shows choice.

What to Do Now

Consider your marriage to be intact. You do not have to tell your wife about this; Sacred Law asks you to keep your own sins private, and telling her would only hurt her without any benefit.

The threats made against you are a crime, not just a private issue. Do not pay, do not give in, and do not meet this woman again.

Talk to someone you trust, and go to the authorities if the threats keep happening. Stay committed to your tawba, and focus your energy on your marriage and your children.

One thing to keep in mind, so you are not surprised later: if your wife ever finds out and challenges it, you would need to prove coercion with evidence, not just your own word.

That would be for a court to decide. But this does not change what is true between you and Allah, and based on what you have told me, you are still married.

Allah (Most High) says: “Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford.” [Quran 2:286] May Allah hide your faults, remove this harm from you, and bless your home.

records.title: Is My Tawaf Valid If a Few Hairs Showed Through My Hijab?
records.question: I struggle a lot with waswasa. Before tawaf, I felt a few small hairs at the back of my head under my hijab. My sister looked at me directly and said nothing was showing.
records.answer:
Your tawaf is valid, and your hajj is accepted, amin. I am going to keep this answer short, because brevity is part of the answer.

The Ruling

According to Sacred Law, hair that can only be seen by looking closely in a mirror is considered covered. What matters is what can be seen with normal vision, not by close inspection.

Even if a few strands of hair were visible, showing much less than a quarter of the head is excused, so your tawaf is valid.

Remember this important point: once an act of worship is completed, it is not undone by doubts that come up later. Certainty is not removed by doubt [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir].

During your tawaf, your sister looked at you and confirmed nothing was showing. Checking your scarf in a mirror days later does not tell you what was visible at that time, nor does it outweigh her observation.

The Key Factor

You did the right thing during tawaf. Later, the waswasa came back, and instead of ignoring it, you looked for and found something to worry about. This is exactly how waswasa works.

So here is what you should do: do not check again. Leave the scarf as it is, and let this be the last answer you look for on this issue.

When the thought comes back, and it probably will, remind yourself, “my tawaf is valid, I have been told so,” and move on without arguing with the thought.

One Next Step

If these doubts affect other parts of your worship, please talk to a doctor or therapist as well as a scholar.

If you treat this only as a fiqh issue, it can keep you stuck in a cycle. This is a health matter, and it often improves with treatment. Seeking help is also a way of trusting Allah.

You were invited to hajj, and you went, so do not let anything take that away from you. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “The accepted hajj has no reward but Paradise.” [Bukhari and Muslim]

records.title: When Does a Kinaya Divorce Expression Take Effect?
records.question: I struggle with severe OCD about divorce. I heard a speaker on YouTube say that if a man jokingly tells a friend he has “left” his wife, without meaning divorce, and when she is not present, and she later hears about it, divorce happens because the wife acts as judge.
records.answer:
No divorce has happened.

If someone uses a metaphorical (kinaya) expression as a joke, without meaning divorce, it does not count as divorce just because the wife hears about it later. Your marriage is still valid.

The Ruling

What you heard is not the view of the Hanafi school. Metaphorical expressions only count as divorce if there was a real intention to divorce, or if they were said during anger or when divorce was being discussed [Maydani, al-Lubab fi Sharh al-Kitab].

If your wife hears about a remark, it does not create an intention that was not there.

The idea that the wife acts as judge is a misunderstanding of a real principle.

There is a rule that says a woman is like a judge, but it only applies if she knows a divorce happened, either because she heard it herself or trustworthy witnesses told her, and her husband then denies it in court.

This rule means that even if the court rules in her favor, it may not settle her own conscience.

It does not apply when the husband had no intention and she only heard a report.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Allah has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

A joke made without any intention is even less serious in this case, because the school does not consider it a divorce at all.

Most importantly, remember this rule: certainty is not removed by doubt [Ibn Nujaym, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir]. Your marriage is certain. A divorce you never intended is not.

Now the Part That Matters More

You mentioned that you struggle with extreme OCD about divorce, and this is not your first message. Because of this, I will not explain when metaphorical expressions do take effect. You do not need that information. You might use it to create more questions and worries.

What you need is one clear answer, and here it is: your marriage stands.

Here are three things to keep in mind. Please take them as your answer, not just as advice.

Stop watching this kind of material. Discussions about the details of divorce rulings are not helpful for you; they only make things worse. Leave those channels, and let this answer be enough for you without looking for another opinion.

Do not go back and review everything you have said in the past. You do not need to check what you might have said months or years ago, and you should not act on doubts when you are certain about your marriage.

See a doctor. Extreme OCD is a medical condition, and it can be treated.

Talking to a psychiatrist or therapist does not mean you lack faith; it means you are using the help Allah (Most High) has given you. This will help you more than another fatwa.

You are married. Live your life as a married man, and let this worry go. May Allah remove this burden from you and give you peace.

records.title: Does Silence in Place of the Fatiha Require Sujud al-Sahw?
records.question: One answer permits standing for the length of three tasbihs in place of the Fatiha in the last two cycles, while another states that delaying a necessary act by that length requires the forgetfulness prostration.
records.answer:
Ma sha Allah, may Allah bless you for your attention to this detail. Both answers are correct, as they refer to different situations. Your prayer is valid in both cases.

The First Answer Is a Dispensation About What Occupies the Standing

According to the Hanafi school, in the third and fourth cycles of an obligatory prayer, reciting the Fatiha is considered sunna, not wajib. You can recite the Fatiha, which is best, say “SubhanAllah” three times, or stay silent for that amount of time. [Ibn ’Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

The answer you read is a dispensation for those with many makeup prayers. It is about how you spend that standing, and is separate from any instruction to pause after reciting.

The Second Answer Concerns Delaying a Necessary Act

The forgetfulness prostration (sujud al-sahw) is only needed if you forgetfully delay a necessary act for as long as it takes to say ‘SubhanAllah’ three times, without doing anything else in the prayer.

If you are reciting, remembering Allah, or even thinking about which cycle you are in, you are still engaged in the prayer, so no delay is counted. [Maydani, al-Lubab; Ibn ’Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

In the last two cycles, being silent does not cause any delay, since no recitation is required. Standing silently is a valid way to fulfill that part of the prayer.

Your Question Answered Directly

Standing silently in those cycles is not required or sunna by itself. It is just one of three valid ways to spend that time, and it is the least preferred. Reciting the Fatiha is best. Your prayer is valid either way.

The forgetfulness prostration only fixes a delay that happens by mistake. If you deliberately delay a necessary act, the prayer is still valid but incomplete, and you should repeat it within its time. [Tahtawi, Hashiyat Maraqi al-Falah]

If you are praying behind an imam, you only do the forgetfulness prostration when the imam does.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Pray as you have seen me pray.” [Bukhari] The way the prayer has been passed down gives you flexibility in the last two cycles. Choose the option that fits your situation and pray with focus.

In Summary

Recite the Fatiha in the last two cycles unless you really need to use the dispensation. Avoid adding any deliberate extra pause while standing, and let your past prayers stand as they are.

records.title: What Is the Objective Behind the Timing of Fajr?
records.question: What is the objective of the nature of Fajr’s timing?
records.answer:
The timing of Fajr, like the other five prayers, is a devotional matter. Its exact limits come from revelation, not human reasoning. The main purpose is for us to submit to Allah’s command.

The Ruling and Its Basis

Allah (Most High) says: “Indeed, performing prayers is a duty on the believers at the appointed times.” [Quran 4:103]

Those appointed times were taught to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) directly, when Jibril (Allah bless him and give him peace) led him in prayer at the beginning and end of each prayer’s time and said: “The time is between these two.” [Tirmidhi]

The start of Fajr at true dawn is based on this, and not on any human rationale, and Allah knows best.

There is a difference between the legal reason for a ruling and its wisdom. Fajr begins when true dawn appears, and this is the basis for the ruling.

We might notice some wisdom, such as starting the day with prayer before anything else, and Allah says that the dawn recitation is “certainly witnessed” by the angels [Quran 17:78].

Still, the ruling does not depend on our understanding of these reasons. When the wisdom is not clear, scholars remind us that the main point is to submit. Many say that obeying in such cases brings even greater reward because it shows trust in Allah.

The Principle and Practical Guidance

We follow Sacred Law because Allah has commanded it. Any wisdom we discover is a gift, not a requirement. Pray Fajr at its proper time, and let your acceptance of this be an act of worship.

records.title: Is It Kufr to Be Kind to Those Who Mock Islam?
records.question: Does Quran 58:22 say that loving, befriending, or showing kindness to people who have mocked Allah, Islam, or the messengers (peace be upon them) is considered disbelief, even if they are relatives? Also, what does Quran 4:140 ask of us?
records.answer:
No, showing kindness to such people is not disbelief, and neither verse says that it is.

What the Two Verses Mean

Quran 58:22 is about having loving allegiance to those who openly oppose Allah and His Messenger, meaning loving their hostility and being pleased with it. This is what goes against faith.

Natural affection for relatives, good character, giving gifts, and fair treatment are not included in this. Allah (Most High) says: “Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes.

Surely Allah loves those who are fair.” [Quran 60:8] The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) also told Asma (Allah be pleased with her) to keep ties with her mother, even though her mother was still a polytheist [Bukhari and Muslim].

Quran 4:140 is about what to do when Allah’s verses are being mocked. You should excuse yourself or change the subject, and come back when the conversation has moved on. The sin is staying and listening to the mockery without concern, but it ends once the mockery stops.

Practical Guidance

Maintain your relationships with these relatives and treat them well; this is an act of worship, not a compromise. Step away only during moments of mockery, doing so respectfully and explaining yourself if it will be understood.

Keep your closest friendships with people of faith, and think carefully about close friendships if mocking religion is a regular habit.

Dislike the act, but hope for the person’s guidance—this is the Prophetic way.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Remove Hijab to Find Employment?
records.question: I wear hijab, live in Hungary with my parents and my daughter, and have applied for over a hundred jobs without being hired, and I believe my hijab may be the reason.
records.answer:
You are carrying more than one person should have to carry, and the fear in your question is not weakness in you.

Removing your hijab to be hired is not permitted, and the financial hardship you have described, real and heavy as it is, does not reach the threshold of compulsion that would make uncovering lawful.

That threshold is narrow and concerns a person whose life or limb is genuinely under threat. You are in hardship, and by Allah’s kindness, you and your daughter have a roof over your heads tonight through your parents.

You asked whether you would be sinful. Deliberately uncovering would be a sin, and I answer plainly because you asked plainly.

But a sin committed by a frightened woman who does not want to commit it is not weighed as one committed in ease is weighed, and the door of return is never shut against you. No outcome here puts you outside Allah’s mercy.

Habib Umar Has Already Answered Women in Your Position

Habib Umar bin Hafiz (Allah preserve him) was asked about Muslim women in France, where the hijab is banned in schools and in the workplace.

He answered in a published response on Muwasala: “The real essence of the believers becomes manifest in times of hardship. Women should retain their modesty as far as possible and remain firm, show good character, and patiently bear the hardships they are exposed to, and the end result will belong to the people of taqwa.”

Asked separately about sisters afraid to wear the hijab in public, he said, in another published answer, that “they must strive to show good character, be dignified and set the best example to those around them.”

Notice that he neither licenses removal nor scolds the women asking. He tells them the pressure is itself the test, met with dignity and beautiful character.

Allah Attached a Promise to Precisely This Situation

“And whoever fears Allah, He grants him a way out of every plight, And provides for him whence he could not even guess; And whoever trusts in Allah, He always suffices.” [Quran 65:2-3; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

That was not revealed for people in comfort. It closes a passage about broken households and uncertain provision, which is where you are standing.

Trusting Allah Means to Keep Knocking, Not to Stop

Imam Qushayri (Allah have mercy on him) wrote that trust has its seat in the heart, and that outward movement does not contradict the heart’s trust once the servant has realized that the decree comes from Allah [Qushayri, al-Risala al-Qushayriyya].

Imam Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him) was blunter. Some imagine trust means abandoning work with the body and planning with the heart, collapsing like a rag thrown down; he calls this the assumption of the ignorant, since the effect of trust appears precisely in the servant’s movement and striving toward his aims [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din].

So keep looking, covered, and let your heart rest somewhere other than the outcome.

A hundred applications is a great deal of effort and a great deal of disappointment, and there may still be doors you have not been able to reach: remote and online work, translation and teaching, self-employment, employers among Hungary’s Muslim and immigrant communities, and whatever can be built alongside your husband’s business.

Ask about your legal protections in Hungary, too.

Your Husband Owes You Housing, Food, and Clothing

In the Hanafi school, maintenance (nafaqa) is a debt owed, not a kindness offered. Imam Mawsili (Allah have mercy on him) states that a wife’s food, clothing, and housing become obligatory upon her husband once she has given herself over to him in his home [al-Mawsili, al-Ikhtiyar li-Taʿlil al-Mukhtar].

He states separately that the maintenance of young children falls on the father when they have no wealth of their own [al-Mawsili, al-Ikhtiyar li-Taʿlil al-Mukhtar].

A failing business does not cancel that. It means that he must work, borrow, or accept help, and that the two of you plan this together rather than look to your covering as the way out.

And if you do find work, what you earn is yours. It does not become the household’s by default, nor does it reduce what he owes.

The hijab is not yours to trade away, as your husband says.

Say to him gently, at a calm moment, that threatening divorce over it adds fear to a wife who is already afraid, and that the ruling would stand had he never said it, because your covering is owed to Allah and not to him.

His threat is not what decides this; you are held by Allah’s command, not by anyone’s ultimatum.

You Need Someone Walking Beside You, Not Only an Answer

Do not carry the coming months alone with a written answer in hand. Find a reliable local scholar or a trustworthy teacher, in Hungary or through us, and put yourself in ongoing consultation rather than a single conversation.

Tell that person the whole picture, the money and the marriage both, and go back every few weeks. Ask them, and reliable Muslim women near you, for practical help with work and housing as well as rulings.

A situation this hard needs someone who knows your name and follows up.

Relief Comes With Distress

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said to Ibn Abbas (Allah be pleased with them both): “Know that what missed you was never to befall you, and what befell you was never to miss you. And know that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship comes ease.” [Riyad al-Salihin]

Hold fast to this supplication, which Imam Nawawi (Allah have mercy on him) records for one burdened with a debt he cannot meet from the beautiful supplications of the Messenger of Allah (peace & blessings be upon him):

اللهُم اكْفِني بحلالِكَ عنْ حَرَامِكَ، وأغْنِني بِفضلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ

“O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your grace from anyone besides You.” [Nawawi, al-Adhkar]

Ibn Allan al-Bakri (Allah have mercy on him), in his commentary on al-Adhkar, records that “suffice me” here carries the sense of holding back, that is, hold me back and guard me by what You have made lawful [Ibn Allan al-Bakri, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya ala al-Adhkar al-Nawawiyya].

That is your prayer exactly. You are not asking Allah merely to feed you. You are asking Him to guard you from being pushed toward what He has forbidden, and to make the law lawful enough.

Say it every day after your prayers, in your own language too if you wish. Allah has not overlooked you.
references: Ibn Allan al-Bakri, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya ala al-Adhkar al-Nawawiyya

records.title: Are Video Game Age Ratings Religiously Binding?
records.question: I am thirteen, and I want to know whether I may play a game rated for older players, such as a 16+ game, when the game itself contains nothing unlawful.
records.answer:
An age rating is not a ruling of the Sacred Law (Sharia), and by itself it does not make a lawful game unlawful.

A ratings board is a company or an industry body that decides what content is appropriate for which age group. That judgment can be sound and useful.

No scholar issued it, though, so it does not carry the weight of a legal ruling on you.

Two other things carry weight, and both are worth your attention.

Your Parents’ Word Settles More Than the Rating Does

Allah Most High said, “And your Lord has decreed that you are to worship none but Him; And to treat parents with grace and kindness.” [Quran 17:23; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

You obey your parents in everything that is not disobedience to Allah, and a game is squarely such a matter. So if they tell you to leave a 16+ game, that binds you. It binds you because they said it, not because the box says 16.

The reverse holds too. If they know your age, know the game, and tell you it is fine, then the rating is not standing between you and it.

What You Agreed to When You Got the Game

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “And the Muslims are held to their conditions, except a condition that forbids what is lawful or makes lawful what is forbidden.” [Mishkat al-Masabih]

Stores and online services often make age one of the account’s conditions. If you signed up by giving an age that is not yours, you broke a condition you agreed to, and you told an untruth to do so.

Where your parents set up the account or bought the game knowing exactly how old you are, the agreement is theirs and you are clear.

One more thing, said a friend. A board that puts 16 on a game usually sees something in it. Before you tell yourself the content is clean, look again and be honest about what is actually in the thing.

Take This to Your Parents

Go to them, name the game, say what is in it, and ask. You have already done the harder part by asking the right question instead of hunting for a way around the answer.

That habit will serve you for the rest of your life, and I ask Allah to keep it in you.

records.title: Do I Bear the Sin of My Mother’s Apostasy?
records.question: My mother left Islam and said it was because of my practices, like wearing trousers above the ankle, praying for a long time, lowering my gaze, and giving up music.
records.answer:
We understand how heavy this feels for you, and we pray that Allah eases your burden.

You are not responsible for your mother’s decision, and following your faith was never wrong.

Allah (Most High) says: “No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another.” [Quran 35:18] Guidance is not something you control: “You surely cannot guide whoever you like, but it is Allah Who guides whoever He wills.” [Quran 28:56]

This verse was revealed to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) about his beloved uncle, who did not accept the faith. If even the Prophet could not give faith to someone, your mistakes did not take it away from your mother.

If you truly fell short in how you treated her, ask Allah for forgiveness for that. Your repentance is sufficient for your own actions and does not extend to what she decided.

What to Do Now

Your mother’s rights over you have not changed. Be the best son you can be: help her, speak kindly to her, visit her, give her gifts, and avoid arguing with her.

Showing her patient and respectful love is the most powerful way to invite her back to Allah, and the Quran commands this even if parents oppose the faith [Quran 31:15].

Also, pray for her guidance at night, because hearts are in Allah’s hands.

May Allah bring your family back together in faith and give you peace in your heart.

records.title: How Should Muslims Regard Jews Amid the War in Palestine?
records.question: With the violence and suffering faced by Muslims in Palestine and Lebanon, should a Muslim hate Jewish people or feel glad when hatred toward Jews grows in their community?
records.answer:
No, a Muslim should hate oppression and stand against those who commit it.

Our faith does not teach us to hate an entire group of people, and being happy about such hatred spreading is the same as being happy about injustice.

The Central Verse

Allah (Most High) spoke about this situation, where believers are wronged and feel tempted to hate others without limits: “Do not let the hatred of a people lead you to injustice. Be just! That is closer to righteousness.” [Quran 5:8]

This verse does not say you cannot hate wrongdoing, but it warns against letting that feeling make you harm innocent people. “And no soul bears the sin of another” [Quran 35:18].

For example, a Jewish child in another country is not responsible for what an army does.

The Prophetic Example

Some Jews from Khaybar once poisoned the Prophet’s (Allah bless him and give him peace) food, and its effects stayed with him until his last illness. Earlier, Banu Nadir had also tried to kill him. Still, he did not respond by hating all Jews.

He continued to interact with the Jews of Medina, showed respect at a Jewish funeral, and even passed away while his armor was pawned to a Jewish merchant for barley [Bukhari].

If anyone could have justified hating a whole group, it would have been him, but he chose not to.

Practical Guidance

Turn your anger about Palestine and Lebanon into acts of worship: pray, give charity, speak out, boycott, and stand against the oppressors and those who support them. This is where your anger should be directed.

Hating Jews just because they are Jews hurts innocent people, including many who also stand against oppression. It also gives oppressors an excuse to say this conflict is about hatred, not justice.

records.title: Is It Sinful to Use Reddit Because Its Points Are Called “Karma”?
records.question: Reddit calls its reputation points “karma,” though the religious concept of karma is not recognized in Islam.
records.answer:
There is no issue. Using Reddit is permissible, and the name of its points system carries no religious weight.

Names Are Judged by Their Intended Meaning

Words take their meaning from convention and usage, not from their origins. Scholars express this in the principle that there is no quibbling over terminology (la mushahhata fi al-istilah): once the intended meaning is sound, the label does not matter.

Reddit’s “karma” is simply a tally of upvotes; neither the platform nor its users intend the doctrine of rebirth and cosmic recompense, and no one using the app is affirming it.

Our own everyday speech is full of words with pagan origins, such as the names of the days and months, and the Sacred Law has never taken issue with their use.

What Islam rejects is the belief itself: that an impersonal system rewards deeds across lifetimes.

Reward and recompense belong to Allah alone, and the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Actions are only by intentions.” [Bukhari and Muslim]

Your intention in pressing an upvote is to approve a post, and that is all it is.

Practical Guidance

Use the app without hesitation on this account, and let your care go instead to what actually carries weight there: what you read, post, and spend your time on.

records.title: Is My Nikah Valid if the Witnesses Were Sinful?
records.question: I learned that marriage witnesses must be of good moral character. My two witnesses listened to music and took part in celebrations like Christmas and birthdays.
records.answer:
No. Your marriage is valid, and there is nothing to renew.

The Ruling

What the Shafi‘i school requires is uprightness as it appeared at the time of the contract, not as reconstructed by a later audit of the witnesses’ private conduct [Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj].

The sins you name are matters scholars differed over, and they do not establish the open corruption that would strip a witness of his standing.

Your marriage was contracted with certainty. Certainty is not removed by doubt [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir].

A marriage of several years is not reopened by a fiqh detail read about afterwards.

The Instruction

You told me you have OCD, so take this as the answer, not as advice. No renewal. No further research into the conditions of your own nikah. Let this be the last opinion you seek on it.

When the thought returns, say “my marriage is valid, I have been told so,” and move on without arguing with it. If these doubts reach into other parts of your worship, see a doctor or therapist alongside a scholar.

records.title: Did Two or Three Divorces Occur Through My Conditional Oaths?
records.question: I made three conditional divorce oaths. The first was if I fulfilled my desires in a haram way, the second was if I did so through pornography, and the third was if I looked at a woman on my phone with a lustful gaze.
records.answer:
The Short Answer

I cannot give you a final answer through a written question, and it would not be right for me to try.

The issue is whether your marriage is still valid with one divorce left, or if it ended earlier.

Only a qualified mufti can decide this in person, after reviewing the exact wording of all three oaths. Please visit a reliable Dar al-Ifta in Islamabad this week.

What the Question Depends On

In the Hanafi school, a suspended divorce is considered an oath. When the condition is met, the divorce takes effect, and the oath is fulfilled.

Doing the same act again does not trigger another divorce, unless you used the word “whenever” (kullama) [Ibn ’Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar].

Your three oaths are separate, and each can only take effect once. This means that continuing the habit afterward did not add to the count, which is one clear point of relief I can offer.

Your first oath was fulfilled. Your second oath specifically mentioned pornography, and it also appears to have been fulfilled. This is why your local scholar counted two divorces.

The third oath is especially important. You swore not to look at a woman on your phone with a lustful gaze.

Whether choosing a video from a list counts as breaking this oath depends on your intention, because in our school, oaths are judged by what the person meant and by common practice, not just by the words used [Mawsili, al-Ikhtiyar].

There is also a legal discussion about whether an image is the same as the real thing. So, what you meant when you swore is a key fact, and only you can explain it to a mufti in person.

There is another important detail the mufti will need. If a divorce took place, taking your wife back, even by resuming relations, counts as revocation (raj’a) in our school and keeps the marriage valid.

If you let the waiting period end without doing this, the marriage ends. So, what happened after each event is just as important as the number of divorces.

Why This Cannot Be Settled in Writing

When the count is two, your marriage will continue, and one divorce will still be possible; but if the count is three, the separation will be final, and you will not be able to remarry under ordinary circumstances.

Since the consequences in these two situations are so serious, they cannot be decided upon without personally knowing all the relevant facts.

What to Do in Order

Start by writing down precisely the exact words you used in each of the three oaths and also what at the time you thought you were committing yourself to.

Then, set out the account of the events as well as you remember, specifying what took place, when it occurred, and whether you and your wife remained husband and wife after that.

Take both sets of notes to a trustworthy mufti in person this week, and until he has given his ruling, it is best to refrain from intimacy.

Take someone you can trust and go with them so you won’t have to go through this all by yourself, and make sure you don’t let this situation cause you to fall back into your old habits. The fact that one has stopped is a kindness from Allah, and keeping count of oaths does not take that away.

Allah (the Most High) says: “And for whoever remembers Allah, He will provide a way out for them.” [Quran 65:2]

records.title: Can Muslims Respectfully Refer to Other Religions and Their Deities?
records.question: Can one respectfully use the religious titles or names of deities and figures from other faiths when speaking with followers of those faiths?
records.answer:
No, it’s not permissible to refer to the deities of other religions as Lord and Mother and other terms you have referred to. This isn’t difficult, as Christians themselves refer to Mary as Mary and to Jesus as Jesus.

If the figure is someone Islam recognizes as special, refer to them with the Islamic honorific fiqh and make a prayer for them, such as “peace and blessings be upon them.”

If one did refer to these figures with the honorifics other religions gave, as long as it wasn’t done with the belief that these honorifics, such as the Son of God in reference to Jesus, are true, it’s not disbelief.

This is something no believer does because no believer considers Mary to be the mother of God and Jesus to be God or the son of God. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

The appropriate inward etiquette would be to hate the deification of any besides Allah in one’s heart.

It is also important not to insult any of their religious figures, especially if they are revered in our religion, because Allah has forbidden it:

˹O believers!˺ Do not insult what they invoke besides Allah, or they will insult Allah spitefully out of ignorance. [Quran 6:108]

One may note that other religions promote what are considered universal moral and ethical principles and good actions.

Such as kindness to one’s neighbor and parents, speaking the truth, avoiding lying, and other such matters. I would say, if you do quote their scriptures, also quote the Quran.

It wouldn’t be appropriate to quote their scriptures on a matter that Islam considers to be sinful or inappropriate, unless it’s to mention a comparison in which the teachings of the Quran are shown in a positive light.

records.title: Does Comparing My Wife to a Divorcee Count as Divorce?
records.question: Soon after our wedding, my wife planned to stay at her parents’ house, and I said in jest, “Why are you sleeping alone at your parents’ house?
records.answer:
There was no divorce, nor was a conditional divorce granted. Your marriage is unaffected. Let this matter rest, and do not worry about it anymore.

Why These Words Do Not Affect Divorce

Words that effect divorce are of two kinds. Plain words (sarih) expressly pronounce divorce upon the wife, and these take effect whether one intends divorce or not.

Allusive words (kinaya) hint at severance, “you are free,” “you are separated,” “go back to your family”, and these take effect only when the husband intends divorce by them. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin; Misri, Umdat al-Salik]

Your words were neither a direct nor an indirect way of pronouncing divorce. You did not say she was divorced, nor did you suggest she was separated from you. You only made a comparison about behavior, not about her as a person.

Even if your words were seen as a weak hint, it would not matter without the intention to divorce, and you have clearly said you had no such intention. Your statement about your intention is accepted. [Nawawi, al-Majmuʿ Sharh al-Muhadhdhab]

A conditional divorce only happens if someone clearly says something like, “if you do this, you are divorced.” You did not say anything like that. No condition was made, so her staying at her parents’ house does not affect your marriage.

Joking in Divorce

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Three things are always taken seriously whether said seriously or in jest: marriage (nikah), divorce (talaq), and taking back (raj‘a).” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi; Ibn Maja]

The hadith states that if a man actually utters words of divorce, he cannot afterward say that he was only joking; it does not mean that a statement which is not a divorce becomes one. As you never said any words of divorce, the hadith does not apply in your case.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The rule is that a marriage which has been definitely established remains even if there is any doubt about it; since nothing at all has taken place that could be described as a divorce, no change has occurred.

There are two things you should do. First, let this issue go. Do not go over your words again, do not repeat them to see what happens, and do not look for another opinion just to ease a worry that has no real reason.

This only leads to unnecessary doubts (waswasa), and the best way to deal with them is to ignore them completely. Second, since you meant to say you prefer being together, tell your wife that directly. It will express your feelings better than a joke.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Watch Calisthenics Videos in Which the Awra Is Exposed?
records.question: There is a brother who would like to take up calisthenics. At present, he cannot afford a personal trainer.
records.answer:
Congratulations on taking this important step towards improving your health and well-being.

The Prophet (May Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, “There are two blessings that people are negligent of, health and free time.” [Bukhari]

It is not permissible to watch videos in which the nakedness (awra) is exposed.

This includes a male looking at a female’s nakedness (awra). According to the relied-upon view (mu’tamad) in the Shafi’i School, this prohibition includes looking at the face and hands, despite the absence of desire and cause for strife (fitna). [Dimyati. I’ana al-Talibin.]

It is likewise not permissible to look at the nakedness of a male, which is the area between the navel and the knee. [Ibid.]

Even though women may be fully clothed in these videos, their clothing is typically very tight-fitting, exposing the contours of the body.

This demonstration falls under the ambit of the Prophetic statement, “And women who are clothed yet naked, who incline others and are themselves inclined”. [Muslim]

Action without knowledge is impossible. It is thus admirable that you seek to educate yourself before beginning to practice.

I am confident that you will find calisthenics learning materials that are free from Shariah prohibitions.

The principle of “Be Allah-conscious all you can” [Quran, 64:16] requires us to exhaust all permissible means at our disposal.

records.title: Is Helping My Parents Pay a Riba-Based Loan Impermissible?
records.question: My parents took out a home loan. My father transferred money to my account, and my mother asked me to withdraw it and accompany her to the bank to pay an installment on the loan.
records.answer:
Withdrawing your father’s money and handing it over to your mother is not considered impermissible assistance, due to the degree of separateness. By withdrawing the funds, you are merely returning money that has been entrusted to you.

Since you are not party to the usurious contract in any way, you are not morally responsible. Allah says, ‘And no bearer of burdens will carry the burden of another’. [Quran, 35:18]

This is a unique opportunity for you to advise your parents to free themselves from this usurious loan. With goodwill, tact, and wisdom, advise them to abandon whatever remains of usury. [Quran, 2:278]

Please consult a local shari’a expert who can provide practical guidance and help facilitate a transition from an interest-based loan to a shari’a-compliant alternative

And with Allah alone is our success.

records.title: Is a Degree Obtained Through a False Disability Certificate Valid?
records.question: A friend secured university admission under a disability quota with lower merit, then completed the degree through his own study and effort. The disability certificate was difficult to obtain, so a reference (connection) was used to obtain it.
records.answer:
Fabricating a status that a person does not possess is impermissible. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever deceives us is not one of us.” [Muslim]

Utilizing a reference to cut through bureaucracy in order to secure something to which a person is entitled is permissible. [Suyuti, Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir]

A degree earned through genuine study and examination is considered valid, regardless of how admission was obtained. This is akin to performing ritual ablution (wudu) with water that has been usurped. [See Khatib, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

If a person fishes with a usurped net, the fish belongs to him. The same applies to hunting with a usurped bow and arrow. This is because the catch or prey is directly the result of his own effort. [Khatib, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

Similarly, the acquisition of the degree is independent of, and extraneous to, the question of eligibility. And Allah knows best.

Consequently, earnings derived from the degree are lawful, just as a prayer performed after ablution with usurped water remains valid, despite the sin involved in the usurpation.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.” [Bukhari]

Cautious piety demands that we do our utmost to be truthful in all our endeavors.

The least level of truthfulness is the congruity between our inward and outward states. With Allah alone is success.

records.title: What Should I Do if My Husband Neglects My Needs?
records.question: My husband spends most of his time alone, either playing games or watching television. He provides for me financially, but he ignores my emotional, physical, and mental needs. We have been married for four years, yet he has never considered my feelings or desires.
records.answer:
The emotional needs of a spouse are indeed an obligation of propriety and legal dignity (muru’aa), not to mention spirituality. These are the higher levels of Islamic guidance.

A woman is the Muslim’s mother and his sister; then she is his wife and his daughter. If a woman encompasses all of these roles under her wings, then who could be more cherished than her? [Abd al-Halim, Tahrir al-Mar’a]

Anti-Social Behavior

Your husband’s destructive antisocial behavior needs to be addressed head-on, albeit with wisdom. Wisdom is righting the wrong while maintaining the relationship without harm to oneself.

Impress upon him that addictions of whatever nature impair relationships.

Allah says, ‘And those from idle words are invariably turned away. [Quran, 23:3]

Ibn Ashur explains, ‘Turning away from all forms of idle talk and nonsense is a mark of seriousness and resolve. Whoever adopts seriousness in all their affairs will perfect their soul, and nothing but beneficial actions will proceed from them’. [Ibn Ashur, Tahrir]

Conselling

If you struggle to communicate your emotional and mental needs calmly and effectively to your husband, then I suggest that you both see a qualified and culturally sensitive marriage counselor.

If your husband becomes very defensive when you bring up the possibility of marriage counseling, please stay calm. His response is a common one.

Allah

There is a space in your heart that belongs solely to Allah. Your husband, and no human being, can fill that. Reflect on this.

Wake up before the entry of Fajr and pour your sorrow out to Allah. Perform the prayer of need and beg Allah to nourish your marriage, and to comfort you.

Commit to daily Qur’anic recital. Commit to a regular study practice.

Make your heart and your life full of love, compassion, and service, and I pray that your husband will learn from your good character.

records.title: Is a Fixed-Fee Cash Advance Considered Riba?
records.question: I sell card machines to businesses and could also sell a cash advance product.
records.answer:
It is not permissible for you to sell the above-mentioned cash advance product. Facilitating or assisting in an impermissible transaction is itself impermissible. Allah says, ‘And aid not one another in sin and transgression’. [Quran, 5:2]

Charging a fixed amount in exchange for lending money constitutes interest (riba) and is, therefore, impermissible. Interest is any stipulated positive return on the principal amount of a loan. The ruling is that interest is prohibited, whether the return is fixed or variable. [See Khatib, Mughni]

Whether the repayment amount is linked to prevailing interest rates or to the Bank of England base rate has no bearing on the underlying arrangement.

We appreciate your concern in seeking to ensure that your livelihood is lawful.

Whoever leaves something for the sake of Allah, Allah will replace it with something better. Allah is the best of providers for those who seek it through lawful means.

And with Allah alone is our success.

records.title: Where Does the Ankle Begin and End for Washing the Feet in Wudu?
records.question: Where exactly does the ankle begin and end for the washing of the feet in wudu, and is it the same for men and women?
records.answer:
In the Hanafi school, the ankle (kaʿb) in wudu is the protruding bone on either side of the foot —the raised knob at the joint, one on the inner side and one on the outer.

Wash both in full, along with the rest of the foot. Wash this, and go a little beyond, and then don’t investigate nor listen to any doubts or misgivings.

This ruling applies to men and women alike. May Allah reward your care for your prayer.

What Counts as the Ankle

Ibn Abidin gives it plainly: the two ankles are the two bones protruding from either side of the foot—the raised ones. He notes that this is how al-Mughrib defines them, and that al-Hidaya and others declared the definition correct. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Ibn Nujaym and Zaylaʿi say the same. [Ibn Nujaym, al-Bahr al-Raʾiq; Zaylaʿi, Tabyin al-Haqaʾiq]

Run your finger up the inside of your foot until you feel the bony knob at the joint. That is your ankle. The same bone sits on the outside. Make sure water reaches both, and everything below.

The Ankles Are Washed, Not Just a Boundary

This matters in practice. Shurunbulali lists the third obligation of wudu as “washing his feet together with his ankles.” [Shurunbulali, Nur al-Idah]

Ibn Abidin explains why the texts chose “with” (maʿa) over “up to” (ila): “up to” leaves it open whether the ankles fall inside the washed area, while “with” says outright that they are washed too. He adds that consensus formed on their inclusion. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

The warning attached to this comes from the Prophet himself (Allah bless him and give him peace). Seeing men who had rushed their wudu with their heels still dry and gleaming, he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire. Perform wudu completely.” [Muslim 241; Bukhari 165]

Imam Muslim placed the narration under a chapter heading on the obligation of washing the feet in their entirety. The ankles and heels are exactly where a hurried wudu leaves dry patches.

Men and Women Are the Same in This

There is no difference between men and women here. Imam Muhammad al-Shaybani was asked whether the two are equal in the ritual bath, wudu, and wiping over leather socks. He answered that they are equal in all of it, and in wiping the head as well. [Shaybani, al-Asl]

Imam Quduri gives the reason: they generally do not differ in the rulings on purification. [Quduri, Sharh Mukhtasar al-Karkhi]

In Practice

Pour water so it flows over your whole foot and past the ankle bones. Use your hand to guide the water over your heel, the sides, and between your toes.

This is all that is required. When the water has reached every part, you have completed the washing. Do not return to it out of doubt.

records.title: Is My Income Unlawful Because of How My Workplace Handles Food?
records.question: I work on a dessert truck. The cheesecake is left out for the whole shift instead of being refrigerated, and I have been trying to move it to the freezer against my coworkers’ objections.
records.answer:
Your income is lawful. What you described does not make it otherwise. You have carried this worry longer than needed. May Allah give you ease and peace of mind.

Three Things Are Being Confused Here

First: unrefrigerated cheesecake is a food-safety matter, not a matter of lawfulness. Food left out too long may be unpleasant, or unwise to sell, or a health-code problem.

None of that makes it unlawful. There is no ruling in the Sacred Law that turns a permissible food into a forbidden one because it sat at room temperature.

So the premise underneath the whole worry does not hold, and once it goes, most of the distress should go with it.

Second: your wage attaches to your work, not to your employer’s judgment. The principle in the Hanafi school is settled and clean.

Ibn Abidin, discussing hire for carrying something a person may later misuse, states it: the hire is on the carrying, which is not itself a sin nor a cause of one— the sin only comes about through the act of a freely choosing agent, and its attribution is severed from the one hired. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Elsewhere in the same discussion: “because there is no sin in the substance of the work itself.”

You are paid to serve dessert, and that is lawful work. If your manager handles the food poorly, that is his responsibility, not yours. Your pay remains clean.

Third—and this is the one I most want you to hear: the suspicion itself is the greater danger. Imam Ghazali is severe on this, and I do not think he would be gentler with you.

Writing on precisely this kind of anxiety, he says that guarding against something on the strength of a bare imagining with no evidence behind it is baseless misgiving (waswas).

He gives the whole genre a name: “the scrupulosity of the obsessive.” [Ghazali, Ihyaʾ Ulum al-Din]

Then Imam Ghazali presses harder, in a passage that inverts the whole calculation. If you refuse a Muslim’s food or trade because “corruption is widespread among people,” that is misgiving and ill opinion of this particular Muslim, and some suspicion is sin.

He concludes: if you think ill of him because you saw corruption in someone else, you have wronged him and sinned by it immediately and certainly—whereas had you taken the property, its being unlawful would only have been doubtful. [Ghazali, Ihyaʾ Ulum al-Din]

The fear is doubtful, but the suspicion is certain. Avoiding a small risk, you have taken on a greater one. Let yourself step back from this.

Real Scrupulousness Leaves the Matter Alone

Ghazali gives the rule in one line: the path of scrupulousness is leaving, not spying. And where eating, or working, is unavoidable, the scrupulous course is to proceed and to think well.

That, he says, was the settled practice of the Companions (Allah be pleased with them), and whoever outdoes them in scrupulousness is astray and an innovator, not a follower. [Ghazali, Ihyaʾ Ulum al-Din]

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between the two are ambiguous matters that many people do not know.” [Bukhari 52; Muslim 1599] Notice what the hadith does not say.

It does not tell you to investigate the ambiguous; it tells you to leave what is genuinely doubtful, and this is not that. And the governing maxim of our law stands behind you: certainty is not removed by doubt, and what was established remains as it was until evidence establishes otherwise. [Majalla, arts. 4 and 5]

The Prayer Is the Real Question

The real concern here is not the cheesecake, but your prayer. You said you might lose your job if you took time to pray. This deserves your attention more than the food handling.

Prayer at its time cannot be left. An obligatory prayer takes only a few minutes. Ask your manager for a short break.

Most employers will allow this if you ask clearly, and many must do so. If it helps, combine it with a meal or bathroom break.

If you are refused and cannot pray, start looking for other work. Do not assume the answer is no before you ask. Often, the fear is greater than the reality.

Move the cheesecake if you can do so without conflict. If someone else prevents it, leave it. This is not your shop or your burden. Your standing with Allah depends on your prayers, not on the cheesecake.

records.title: What Should I Do After Seeing Family Members in an Intimate Situation?
records.question: I opened a door and saw what I think was two family members in an intimate situation—I am not certain what I saw, and I left at once. Something similar may have happened once before. Am I sinful? Am I sinful for picturing it again to write this question? And must I ask their forgiveness, though it is not something the family would ever discuss?
records.answer:
You have not sinned, and you owe no apology. I will answer your questions one by one, then add a word of advice.

The First Glance Is Excused

The involuntary first glance is excused. Jarir ibn Abdullah (Allah be pleased with him) said: “I asked the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) about the unintended glance, and he ordered me to turn my gaze away.” [Muslim 2159]

And the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said to Ali (Allah be pleased with him): “Do not follow a glance with a glance — the first is yours, the second is not yours.” [Abu Dawud 2149]

Imam Jassas gives the reasoning: the first is yours because it is a matter of compulsion, and the second is not yours because it is chosen. [Jassas, Ahkam al-Quran]

Khadimi: “the first is involuntary and pardoned, and the second is voluntary and held to account.” [Khadimi, Bariqa Mahmudiyya]

And Ibn al-Malak, glossing the hadith: “there is no sin upon you in the first glance if it came suddenly, without intent.” [Ibn al-Malak, Sharh al-Masabih]

You opened the door, saw something, and left at once. This is the exact situation the ruling excuses. There is nothing here to repent.

Recalling It to Ask Is Not Sinful

This is not a sin either. You had to remember what happened to ask your question. No one is blamed for recalling something in order to seek guidance.

Now that you have asked, let it go. Do not revisit the memory or test yourself about what you saw. Turning it over in your mind gives it weight it does not deserve, and this is how baseless misgivings take root.

You Owe Them No Apology

No. You wronged no one, so there is nothing to seek pardon for. The duty running in the other direction is the one that binds you: concealment.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “No servant conceals another in this world but that Allah conceals him on the Day of Rising.” [Muslim 2590]

And: “Whoever conceals a Muslim, Allah conceals him in this world and the next.” [Muslim 2699; Bukhari 2442]

Bringing this up would only uncover what Allah has covered and cause pain to people close to you. Do not mention it. Do not hint at it.

When asking for pardon would harm someone, repentance before Allah is enough. In your case, you have nothing to repent.

Assume the Better Interpretation, and Knock

Let the uncertainty remain. You are not sure what you saw, and doubt does not remove certainty.

You cannot judge others based on a moment you cannot confirm. Assume the best. This is not wishful thinking; it is the ruling.

In practice, knock before you enter a room and wait for a reply.

This is the Prophetic way of seeking permission. It protects you and others from situations like this.

If you have reason to think someone in your home is being harmed, or something wrong is happening, that is a different matter.

Ask about it directly and in confidence. But if it is as you described—a glimpse and nothing more—close the door on it and do not carry it further.

records.title: How Do I Hold to a Boycott When Close Relatives Ignore It?
records.question: We steer clear of some products and firms, whereas our close relatives do not.
records.answer:
Stick to the boycott in your own home; don’t attempt to control your relatives, and don’t let this matter cause distance between you.

That is the key point; the rest is merely about the means of achieving it.

Ease the Tension

It is a personal decision rather than a religious obligation. It is correct to avoid indirect support of oppression, and scholars back this view.

However, those with a strong faith may still differ as to its extent, who it should apply to, and whether it is effective.

The situation is unlike that of pork or interest, where the rule is clear and applies to all.

This settles most of your worries, since your relatives are not engaging in any sin you need to remedy; they are merely making a different choice about something optional.

Your Responsibility Ends with Your Own Choices

Allah (Most High) says, “No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another.” [Quran 6:164] And He says, “O you who believe, take care of your own souls.

The one who goes astray cannot harm you when you are guided.” [Quran 5:105]

If you haven’t already, offer gentle advice once, then let it go. You should not try to stop something if it will cause more harm, and a voluntary boycott is not important enough to risk family tension.

Correcting elders again and again about something they are allowed to decide for themselves is actually the mistake to avoid.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young and honour our elders.” [Tirmidhi; Abu Dawud]

Shared Purchases and Hospitality

You are not responsible for what others buy. Eating what your relatives serve in their home is not a sin, and turning down an elder’s hospitality because of a brand is disrespectful compared to any small benefit you might gain.

Bring alternatives to family gatherings yourself so the family has them without anyone feeling targeted.

Teaching the Children Without the Contempt

Don’t tell your child that what their grandmother does is forbidden. If you do, they will either look down on someone they should honor, or think that what you taught them isn’t really true.

Instead, explain the difference to them in simple terms. Some things are always forbidden by Allah, no matter where or who you are. Other things are choices families make to do extra good, and good people can make different choices and still be good.

This is what our family has chosen. Their grandparents love them, and honoring them is always required.

A child who learns this difference at a young age will benefit from it throughout their religious life. But if a child learns to see relatives as wrongdoers, it will harm them in the long run.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The main principle is that everyone is responsible for their own choices, and you should never pursue an optional good if it means giving up something required. Keeping family ties and honoring elders are required.

So, keep the boycott in your own home. Don’t check what others buy. Accept hospitality with gratitude. Bring alternatives yourself.

Teach your children the difference between what Allah has forbidden and what your family has chosen. Most importantly, keep your intention sincere for Allah, because that is where the real reward lies.

records.title: How Should Muslim Women’s Hair and Hijab Be Depicted in Animation?
records.question: I am working on a 2D animation that does not depict real people, and I want to ensure my depictions are accurate.
records.answer:
One: All the Hair, Before Non-Mahram Men

A free woman’s nakedness (awra) before non-mahram men is her whole body except the face and the hands, and the feet also, on the strict view of the school.

The hair is included without exception. There is no allowance in the Shafiʿi school for a few visible strands. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin; Ibn Hajar, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj]

Some people mention a leniency allowing less than a quarter of the hair to be uncovered, but this is a Hanafi rule and applies only to whether a woman’s own prayer is valid.

It does not apply to what non-mahram men may see, so it is not relevant to your question in either school.

Allah (Most High) says: “And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and not to display their adornment except what ordinarily appears, and to draw their head-coverings over their bosoms.” [Quran 24:31]

For your animation, if an adult woman is shown with non-mahram men, her hair should be completely covered. Showing loose strands would not reflect the standard practice.

Two: Covering Begins at Puberty

The requirement to cover applies to a woman once she reaches puberty (bulugh). Before puberty, a girl is not legally responsible for this herself; instead, her guardian is responsible for teaching her.

Scholars use the example of teaching children to pray at age seven as a guide for this training.

In our school, there is one important exception: if a girl becomes someone men might desire, she should cover like an adult, even if she has not yet reached puberty. [Bajuri, Hashiya ala Sharh Ibn Qasim]

In your animation, it is accurate to depict young girls without head coverings.

Girls who are close to or have reached puberty should be shown with their hair covered.

It is also accurate to show a girl of six or seven wearing a scarf, since many families start this practice early. Both options reflect real Muslim practices.

Three: Among Women and Mahrams

In front of Muslim women of good character, as well as mahram men, a woman’s awra is between the navel and the knees. Hair may be shown uncovered and may be styled. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin]

There are two important limits to know.

First, it is not allowed to join human hair to your own. The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) cursed both the woman who joins hair and the one who has it joined. [Bukhari; Muslim]

However, in the Shafiʿi school, using extensions made from permitted animal hair or synthetic material is allowed as a way to beautify oneself for one’s husband. [Ibn Hajar, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj; Ramli, Nihayat al-Muhtaj]

Second, the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) described women “whose heads are like the humps of camels, leaning to one side,” as among those who will not enter Paradise. [Muslim]

Scholars have different interpretations of this, and no specific hairstyle has been declared forbidden because of it. The main caution is against hairstyles that are meant to attract attention outside the home.

For your animation: in scenes among women or family, hair uncovered and ordinarily styled is accurate.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The main principle is that the rules for covering depend on the situation and who is present, not on whether it is animation or real life.

Show women as they would be allowed to appear in each scene: fully covered in front of non-mahram men, and relaxed among women and family. This will make your work accurate.
references: Bajuri, Hashiya ala Sharh Ibn Qasim

records.title: Can I Role-Play With Women During Sales Training
records.question: May I attend a free online sales training event where the instructor is a woman, and I may have to role-play a sales scenario with a woman?
records.answer:
Yes, you may attend. It is allowed to learn from a woman teacher, and it is also fine to do a professional role-play with a woman, as long as you follow the usual guidelines.

The Limits That Apply

There are four main guidelines to keep in mind, and all of them can be followed in an online session.

Lower the gaze. Allah (Most High) says, “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity; that is purer for them.” [Quran 24:30]

In the Shafiʿi school, it is permitted to look at a non-mahram woman’s face and hands where there is a need, such as trade or instruction, and there is a strong position permitting it without a need, where there is no desire and no temptation.

Looking beyond that, or looking with desire, is not permitted.

Avoid seclusion (khalwa). An open online session with a group present is not seclusion. A one-to-one private call would be a different matter, and should be avoided.

Keep your speech professional. Allah (Most High) says, addressing the Prophet’s wives, “Do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet.” [Quran 33:32]

Speak as you would to a colleague: clearly and focused on the work.

There should be no physical contact, and nothing in the role-play should involve acting out intimacy or flirtation.

Some sales training may encourage building rapport in ways that become flirtatious. If that happens, excuse yourself from the exercise.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The main principle is that a legitimate need permits interaction, but it should be limited by the scope of the need.

This is governed by how you look, speak, and avoid being alone together. Attend the session and keep things professional; if you feel emotionally involved, it is best to step away.

I would like to share one more thought, as a brother. You have asked several similar questions, and each time the same four principles apply. It might help you more now to take a short course on interacting with the opposite gender and on the fiqh of the gaze.

This way, you will understand the rules and be able to apply them yourself in new situations, rather than needing to ask for a ruling each time.

records.title: Can I Use Surah al-Rahman as a Treatment for Mental Health?
records.question: I would like to know whether this “Surah Ar-Rahman therapy”—listening to Qari Abdul Basit, then drinking water while saying “Allah” three times—is permissible for mental health issues, alongside treatment from a psychologist.
records.answer:
I have not come across any basis for this form of therapy, and I’m pretty sure it’s not something from any of the classical sources.

There is no harm in trying it, as it does not involve anything impermissible, but do not let anyone pass this off as Islamic therapy.

Usually, the means of healing from a particular illness are the standard conventional means that Allah has given us.

The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, said, “Allah has not manifested an illness except that He has manifested for it a cure.” [Bukhari]

If you do have long-standing physical or mental health issues, go to a professional. It’s better than putting your hopes in the hands of a charlatan who uses the religion as the basis of his authority in a field he is not qualified to comment on.

There is a reason why doctors have something called peer review. This prevents wild and lucky claims about X, Y, and Z being a miracle cure. Approaches are tested systematically, and something that falls short doesn’t become mainstream medicine.

Even alternative medicines such as traditional Chinese medicine and homeopathy fall into this bracket of systematically tested approaches. Consider one of these if medication or therapy doesn’t work.

records.title: What Should I Do About Old Sinful Messages After Repenting?
records.question: What should I do about old sinful or irreverent messages I posted on Discord in the past, when I have sincerely repented and deleted what I could, but cannot access or remove the remaining messages? What is the general rule?
records.answer:
All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all beings, and may peace and blessings be upon our master Muhammad (Allah bless him and give him peace)

No, you’re not obliged to go back into those environments to delete your old messages and words. Generally, with online chatter, things move on very fast, so it will be in the past.

However, if your words were something that is being used repeatedly, such as an article that you wrote that promotes a sin or something like this, then you should go back and delete it to prevent others from sinning through your past activity. This would be under the general framework of not assisting others in sin. (Maydani, Lubab)

In general, however, if you’ve repented, you don’t need to do anything further. Repentance, according to Imam al-Nawawi in Riyadh al-Saleheen, entails:

If you’ve done the above, you can assume that those words are forgotten and not go back to that environment. That would be bad for you.

records.title: Is It Necessary to Disclose a Previous Marriage and Children?
records.question: Must a man disclose an existing marriage to a woman he is proposing to as a second wife?
records.answer:
This is a painful situation, and the answer has two halves that must be kept apart: what he owed her, and what she can now do.

He was obliged to disclose it. Concealing it is deception and a sin. But the marriage contract is valid, and concealment does not by itself give her an automatic right of annulment in the Shafiʿi school.
