Her route out, if she wants one, runs through him or through a judge.

Disclosure Is Obligatory

An existing marriage is not a private detail. It determines how she will live — her nights, her home, her husband’s income, her children’s place in a larger family. A woman consenting to marriage is consenting to a known thing, and this is among the most consequential facts she could be given.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever deceives us is not of us.” [Muslim]

Her not asking does not transfer the duty to her. A man who knows that a woman is proceeding on a false assumption and who lets her has deceived her as surely as if he had denied it outright.

The same applies to concealing children from the earlier marriage.

What She Can Do Now

Here the law is narrower than the ethics, and it is important to be exact.

The contract is valid, and his concealment does not nullify it. Nor is this among the defects (uyub) for which the Shafiʿi school grants a right of annulment (faskh) — that list is short and specific and does not include misrepresentation of this kind. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin]

Her actual options are three. She may ask him for a divorce. She may seek a release in exchange for compensation (khulʿ). Or she may petition a Muslim judge or a recognised Islamic judicial body, which can dissolve the marriage where a husband has wronged his wife and refuses to release her.

Where you are, a local mufti or Sharia court should be consulted, since the third route depends on the authority available.

A note for anyone reading this before a marriage rather than after: a condition may be stipulated in the contract itself.

The Hanbali school gives binding effect to such conditions, and where a court applies them, the woman has a solution that the Shafiʿi school does not. This is a cross-school matter and should be arranged with a scholar in advance.

Allah (Most High) says, “If you fear you will not deal justly, then one.” [Quran 4:3]

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said that a man with two wives who inclines to one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides hanging. [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi; Nasaʾi]

A polygamous marriage that starts with secrets is already at a disadvantage. The only way to fix this is to be completely honest now with both wives, to sincerely repent, and to be very fair in time, support, and treatment from now on.

His children’s rights to support and inheritance are not affected by his hiding them; those rights were never his to take away.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The main principle is that a contract is not canceled because of deception; the person who deceived is responsible, and a wronged wife still has options.

To her: Do not make a decision while you are still in shock. Talk to a trustworthy scholar and a counselor before deciding whether to leave or try to fix things. Both choices are valid, and you are not required to do either.

If you stay, do so after clearly stating what he did and asking for what you deserve, not by ignoring what happened.

To him: tell both wives everything now, without waiting to be forced. Ask for their forgiveness. Then be fair and consistent for as long as the marriage continues.

records.title: Is Working on Animation With Unlawful Content Permissible?
records.question: I have been hired for a small animated series, and it appears the two main characters are gay. Should I avoid only those scenes, or leave the project?
records.answer:
Animation as a craft is, in itself, permissible. What is not permitted is to work directly on material that portrays what is unlawful as good or acceptable.

It is important to recognize the wrong inwardly, avoid direct involvement, and know that the higher path—if you are able—is to leave the project entirely.

May Allah reward you for pausing to seek guidance before proceeding. This concern is more valuable than any contract.

The Trade Is Lawful; the Specific Work May Not Be

Let us begin with what is clear. Animation and 3D modeling are, in principle, lawful professions within the guidelines our scholars have outlined for the depiction of animate life. The craft itself is not the issue.

The problem is cooperation.

Allah Most High says: “And aid one another in devotion to your Lord in every good and godfearingness, and do not aid one another in sin and transgression; And fear Allah: Verily Allah is unsparing in reprisal.” [Quran 5:2; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Distinguishing Between Direct and Indirect Assistance in Sin

Our scholars have explained that this command distinguishes between direct and indirect assistance in what is wrong. Animating the two main characters in scenes that establish or promote their relationship is direct involvement.

Tasks such as modeling a building, lighting a corridor, or working on background elements are not direct participation.

The first is direct involvement in the impermissible; the second is general work on a project that may contain some impermissible elements, and its ruling is lighter.

Therefore, your choice is not necessarily all-or-nothing. You may request that your supervisor assign you to scenes involving the relationship. Studios often reassign tasks, and such requests are usually manageable.

If they accommodate your request, you may continue with the permissible work. If you are required to animate those scenes, then it would be best to step away.

Regardless of your decision regarding the work, it is essential to maintain clarity in your heart.

What the series promotes is not permissible, and it is important to recognize this inwardly and not become desensitized to it. Prolonged exposure can affect one’s judgment.

What Is Lawful, and What Is Better

There is a higher course, and I encourage you to consider it. What is permitted is not always what is best.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.” [Tirmidhi; Nasaʾi]

You reached out because you felt uneasy about this matter. This unease is what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was referring to. Do not dismiss this concern as mere scrupulosity.

It is a sound instinct about the nature of this work, and the Prophetic guidance is to follow such caution rather than to reason it away.

Reflect also on what you are presenting to Allah.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure,” and then described the man who travels long, disheveled and dust-covered, stretching his hands to the sky, “O Lord, O Lord!” while his food, drink, and clothing are unlawful. “So how could he be answered?” [Muslim]

What you earn from this project becomes your sustenance and clothing and may affect whether your prayers are answered. This is something to weigh carefully.

Leaving Costs Less Than It Looks

If you choose to leave, do so with contentment and trust in Allah. No one loses by leaving something for the sake of Allah, regardless of what the immediate outcome may seem.

You are at the start of your career, and you have realized that you do not wish to build it on anything questionable. This is a blessed beginning.

records.title: Is Working in a Bookstore or Library Permissible?
records.question: Is it permissible to work at a bookstore or library as a shopkeeper or librarian, given that I have no control over which books are stocked or sold?
records.answer:
“Allah wants ease for you and does not want unbearable hardship for you”.

It is permissible for you to work at such a bookstore, despite the possibility of serving as an agent in the sale of impermissible books.

The same applies to working as a librarian. This is due to the general affliction and necessity, in accordance with the principle, “Necessity renders permissible that which is otherwise impermissible”. [Suyuti, Ashbah]

That said, you should make every effort to avoid selling content contrary to Islamic teachings. Imam Nawawi, citing the Shafi‘i scholars, stated that it is not permissible to sell books of disbelief because they contain no permissible benefit; rather, they must be destroyed.

The same applies to books on magic, astrology, sorcery, and philosophy. [Nawawi, Sharh al-Muhadhdhab]

Where this is unavoidable, you should feel discomfort in your heart at doing so, for loving what Allah loves and disliking what Allah dislikes is part of true faith.

Bookstores often present situations where customers seek the shopkeeper’s advice or recommendations.

This can be a valuable opportunity to encourage what is good and discourage what is wrong. Such guidance should be offered wisely and tactfully, without placing yourself in an unnecessarily compromising position.

And with Allah alone is our success.

records.title: Why Were Fifty Prayers Reduced to Five During the Miʿraj?
records.question: During the Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Miʿraj), the obligation was first set at fifty prayers and then reduced to five after the counsel of Musa (peace be upon him). If Allah already knew what His servants could bear, why was it set at fifty?
records.answer:
Allah Himself does not change. What changed was the command, and that change was always known and always willed.

“Allah changed His mind” is not just imprecise. It describes a belief that Sunni theology rejects. Some retellings miss this point and can mislead. Choose your teachers with care.

The tradition answers in four steps: first, the narrations; second, the commentators; third, the Sira; fourth, the theologians.

One. What the Narrations Say

Two phrases in the hadith seem to pull in opposite directions. They fit together once you see their meaning.

The first comes at the end of the exchange. After the final reduction of the number of prayers, the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) reported what he was told: “He said: They are five and they are fifty. I did not change the word. [Bukhari]

The second comes as he departs: “When I had passed on, a caller called out: I have put My obligation into effect, and I have lightened it for My servants. ” [Bukhari, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa; and Bukhari, which adds: “and I reward a good deed tenfold”]

The first phrase matters. At the last reduction, the Divine Speech says the word does not change. The tradition itself rejects the idea you were concerned about.

In his commentary on Sahih Bukhari, Imam Ibn Hajar (Allah have mercy upon him) explains it as marking the difference between the earlier exchanges and the last one: the repeated petitioning shows that the Prophet understood the command on each occasion was not by way of binding imposition, unlike the final time, whose wording indicates that it was. [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari]

And note what “five and fifty” means. Ibn Hajar: five in number with respect to performance, fifty in reckoning with respect to reward. [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari]

The fifty prayers were not taken away. They moved from your actions to your record.

Two. What the Commentators Made of the Difficulty

The scholars did not ignore the difficulty. They disagreed, and their disagreement teaches us.

One position, from Imam Khattabi (an early commentator), is that the fifty were never definitively binding at all, because the petitioning for relief issued from two Prophets, and what is definitively obligatory does not admit of lightening.

However, Mulla Ali al-Qari rejects this: what is not obligatory needs no request for lightening in the first place. His conclusion: “The correct view is that He first made fifty obligatory, then had mercy on His servants and abrogated them with five.” [Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih]

The Fifty Were a Real Obligation

The fifty prayers were a real command. The question is: for whom, and when were they lifted?

This is where Ibn Hajar does the decisive work. Ibn Battal had said the fifty were abrogated by the five before they were ever prayed.

Ibn al-Munayyir objected that all parties—those who permit abrogation before the act and those who deny it—agree that abrogation is inconceivable before promulgation, and here the change came before promulgation, so the problem defeats everyone. Ibn Hajar answers:

If he means before promulgation to anyone, that is not granted. If he means before promulgation to the community, that is conceded—but then with respect to them, it is not abrogation at all.

It is an abrogation with respect to the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace), because he was definitively obligated to it, then it was abrogated after it had been conveyed to him and before he acted. [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari]

That resolves your question. The fifty were a genuine obligation— upon the Prophet, in that assembly. They never reached the community as a standing duty, so for us there was no abrogation at all; only the five ever arrived.

What occurred was abrogation before the act, which Imam Nawawi records as permissible and as the very point this hadith is cited to prove. [Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim]

Imam Bulqini sharpens it with the technical vocabulary: the lightening from fifty to five is not properly called abrogation with respect to the community, because the ruling was never attached to them in an actualized way, since it was never conveyed to them.

And he adds the line that answers the theological half of your question: what is meant by the “lifting” of a ruling is the severing of its attachment to those under obligation, for the ruling in itself is eternal and is not lifted. [Sakhawi, Fath al-Mughith]

The Whole Sequence, Including the Reduction, Was Planned. The Sira Says This Plainly

Was the whole sequence, including the reduction, planned? The Prophetic biography (Sira) answers yes, and in so many words.

Imam Salihi distinguishes two registers of the decree. “The decree which He decreed together with decreeing that it not be carried into effect, by reason of an intermediary or a supplication—that is His imposing here of the fifty prayers; for when He commanded the fifty first, His will had already gone forth that it not be executed, and He made Musa’s counsel there a cause for its removal. And the decree whose execution He decreed and which no repeller repels—that is His imposing of the five; for when He commanded them and His will had already gone forth to put them into effect, Musa’s words availed nothing at that point.” [Salihi, Subul al-Huda wa’l-Rashad]

Musa (peace be upon him) was not overruling anything. He was the appointed means.

And on why the Prophet stopped asking, the same work says: the unseen disclosed that the eternal knowledge had attached to these five remaining —and that is why they remained. [Salihi al-Shami, Subul al-Huda wa’l-Rashad]

Four. What the Theologians Settled

That something should emerge to Allah which He had not previously known, or that a new opinion should arise in Him: this is badaʾ.

Imam Zarqani gives both senses and rules on both: both are impossible for Allah, because they entail prior ignorance and the origination of knowledge. He is described in pre-eternity and everlastingly with unrestricted, encompassing knowledge of all that was, all that will be, and all that is; He cannot be originated, nor can He be a locus of originated things. [Zarqani, Manahil al-Irfan fi Ulum al-Quran]

Then the formula that answers your question in one sentence: “His knowledge does not change or alter; the change is in the object known, not in the knowledge … abrogation is an alteration in the object known, not in the knowledge; a change in the created, not in the Creator; and a disclosure to us of part of what Allah’s eternal all-encompassing knowledge had already determined… it is an alteration with respect to us, but pure clarification with respect to the Lawgiver.” [Zarqani, Manahil al-Irfan]

Imam Shahrastani makes the same point as a formal argument: abrogation does not entail any change in Allah’s Knowledge (badaʾ), because He was knowing of that obligation at the time of its being directed upon the servant, and knowing of its removal at the time of the abrogation, so no newly arisen matter appeared to Him that He had not known, nor did He lift the ruling because something else appeared to Him. [Shahrastani, Nihayat al-Iqdam]

In your case, both the fifty and the reduction were always in Allah’s knowledge. Nothing was discovered.

The Objection Was Raised and Answered Long Ago

Your worry is not new. Tahanawi records the dispute precisely: “The condition of abrogation is the capacity for belief in the ruling; there is no need for capacity for the act, in our view. For the Muʿtazila, it is not valid before the act, because the purpose of it is the act; so, before the act occurs, it would be badaʾ.

Our proof is that he (Allah bless him and give him peace) was commanded on the night of the Ascension with fifty prayers, then what exceeded five was abrogated, without there having been any capacity for the act.” [Tahanawi, Kashshaf Istilahat al-Funun]

So the exact objection you raise—“that would mean Allah changed His mind”—is stated in the tradition, attributed to those who held it, and the Isra is given as the refutation rather than the problem.

Imam Iji, listing the sects, names the Badaʾiyya as a sect that permitted that Allah should will a thing and then have something become manifest to Him that had not been, “and it follows from this that the Lord would not be knowing of the outcomes of affairs.” [Iji, al-Mawaqif] That is the doctrine. It is not ours.

The Precise Distinction You Asked For

Thus, Allah’s Knowledge, Will, and Speech are eternal attributes and do not change. What stands in time is not the attribute but its relationship to created things—the address actually reaching a servant who exists and is under obligation.

When a ruling is abrogated, the attribute is untouched; what ends is the connection of that ruling to those bound by it, at a moment eternally appointed.

Allah commanded fifty, then five, and He always knew and willed both. Musa’s counsel was the means Allah chose. The night was not a negotiation. It was a disclosure of mercy, so we would see what was lifted from us and know its weight.

Fifty prayers were set so we would know that five are a gift. The reward of fifty remains. Nothing was taken away.
references: Bukhari, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa; and Bukhari, which adds: “and I reward a good deed tenfold”
Zarqani, Manahil al-Irfan fi Ulum al-Quran

records.title: Is Opening a KFH Hassad Account with a Prize Draw Permissible?
records.question: Is opening a Hassad account with Kuwait Finance House (KFH) in Bahrain, which enters depositors into a draw to win $1,000,000, halal or haram?
records.answer:
It’s commendable that you seek to ensure that your investment accounts are shari’a-compliant.

Opening an Al-Hassad Investment Account that enters depositors into a draw to win $1,000,000 is permissible. Prizes granted under the AI-Hassad Prize Program are funded by the Bank’s funds, not depositors’ funds. [kfh.com] The depositor thus stakes nothing and loses nothing.

The underlying contract is not a current account based on a loan agreement. Therefore, the principle of a loan that brings a benefit (qard jarr manfa‘a) does not apply. It is for this reason that ‘The Bank Fatwa and Shari’ah board has approved the prizes program for the investment accounts’. [Ibid]

Prizes on Investment Accounts

According to the AAOIFI Shari’a Standards,

3.5.2 It is permitted for the institution to give prizes to investment account holders on condition that:

3.5.2.1 The prizes do not come from the investment accounts, the profits, or the charity account. It may come from the bank shareholders’ account.

3.5.2.2 The giving of these prizes must not amount to guaranteeing the invested capital or part of it.

3.5.2.3 The opportunity to win must be available to all participants in the investment account or in one of its categories. [See AAOIFI]

You may open an Al-Hassad Investment Account with a clear conscience. Allah says, ‘O you who believe forbid not yourselves the fair viands of what Allah has made lawful to you: and exceed not the proper due bounds; Verily Allah loves not those who commit excess’. [Quran, 5:87]

records.title: Is Watching the Trailers and Playing the Game Final Fantasy Permissible?
records.question: I play the Final Fantasy VII series, which currently consists of Final Fantasy VII Remake and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth.
records.answer:
Revelation, as you mentioned, is sacred and reserved for the elect. Using the term ‘revelation’ in a context that draws heavily on religious and mythological imagery is misleading and should be avoided. Watching trailers and playing video games with impermissible content is likewise impermissible.

Trailers and Video Games

Watching trailers featuring impermissible imagery and playing such video games are not permissible. This is akin to entering non-Muslim places of worship, such as churches, temples, or synagogues.

In the Shafi‘i School, it is generally unlawful for a Muslim to enter such places if these places contain revered images, symbols, or figures that are forbidden in Islamic law. [See, Ibn Hajar, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj]

Ibn al-Qasim says, “Whatever is impermissible in and of itself is impermissible to view as it amounts to approval (rida)”. [Bujayrami, Hashiya]

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) refused to enter the Kaaba until the images within it were removed. [Bukhari, Sahih]

Advice

Avail yourself of the broad range of permissible forms of entertainment and steer clear of the limited range of impermissible ones. This will afford you true relaxation, peace of mind, and renewed energy.

records.title: Is Wearing Decorated Clothing for Nikah Permissible?
records.question: Is it permissible to wear decorated clothing for one’s nikah? The dress would be loose-fitting and would cover the awrah. I have always loved sparkly things, embroidery, and rhinestones, and I am quite skilled at using them to decorate fabric.
records.answer:
What wonderful news! May Allah place love, compassion, and understanding between you and your spouse. May He unite the two of you in love and harmony, as He united the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with his wives.

You may incorporate embroidery and rhinestones into your nikah dress and scarf. It is permissible to wear decorated clothing for one’s nikah, provided that the decorations do not contravene the precepts of the shari’a.

Wearing makeup for your nikah is also permissible. You should, however, avoid appearing before non-mahram men while wearing decorated clothing or makeup.

Decorated Clothing

It is permissible to wear decorated clothing for one’s nikah. Indeed, it is encouraged for a wife to adorn herself for her husband. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked, “Which women are the best?” He replied, “The one who makes him happy when he looks at her.” [Musnad Ahmad]

The decoration should, however, be moderate. Anything that exceeds its proper limits may produce the opposite of the intended effect. [See al-Khatib, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

The key element of a Muslim’s clothing is modesty. Allah Most High told us, “Children of Adam, We have given you garments to cover your nakedness and as adornment for you; the garment of God-consciousness is the best of all garments- this is one of God’s signs, so that people may take heed.” [Quran, 7:26]

Public Display

Decoration and makeup should not be intended to attract the opposite gender and should not be displayed publicly. Displaying such adornment in the presence of non-mahram men is impermissible.

Allah says, “And remain fast in your homes and make not public display of your beauty as was done in the bygone age of pagan ignorance.” [Quran, 33:33]

May Allah make this new chapter a source of tranquillity, joy, and baraka. This is achieved by following the commands of Allah as shown to us by the Prophet (May Allah bless him and grant him peace).

records.title: Is It Sinful to Divorce a Mentally Ill Wife?
records.question: I have been married for 10 years with no children. My wife struggles with mental health issues, including ADHD and Borderline Personality Disorder, causing anger, emotional outbursts, depression, and conflict.
records.answer:
I’m sorry to hear about your situation and your wife’s.

As you’ve tried supporting your wife and encouraging her and her family to seek treatment, but they refused to seek help, a last resort is a revocable divorce. You will not be sinful due to the efforts you have made.

You’ve spent a long time with her, but if you don’t feel an emotional connection now, consider ending the marriage.

The Quran states that effort should be made for a marriage to work, or for it to end amicably if rights are not fulfilled.

Honorably Retain or Kindly Let Go

Allah guides that a wife should be retained with honor or separated with grace. “The divorce that can be returned from may be pronounced up to two times, then either honorably retaining her or kindly letting her go.” [Quran, 2: 229]

Quranic Guidance

The Quranic guidance is to seek help from righteous scholars, elders, and professional mediators, then strive for reconciliation and give marriage another chance; if this second step fails, the husband may consider ending the marriage.

If considering divorce, respect each other with mutual understanding and sensitivity, and advise them to consider treatment and seek help.

If they seek help, resolve issues, and if she has renewed intent and commitment, reconsider remarriage if you mutually agree to all.

If a husband cannot maintain rights or has no desire for her, then he may divorce her [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Divorce – a Last Resort

Divorce in Islam can be a mercy if marriage fails to achieve mutual comfort.

It provides a solution to hardship, as Allah states in the Quran, “And if a man and wife go their separate ways, Allah shall enrich each from need out of His illimitable bounty; And verily was Allah ever vast of magnificence, all-wise.” [Quran, 4:130]

We pray to Allah Most High to grant a cure to your wife and make it easy for her to seek support. May he reward you for your patience. If not, after consulting your family and reliable local scholars, you may consider ending the marriage as described above.

records.title: Do Impure Splashes Count Collectively?
records.question: Regarding major impurities, impurities up to 5 cm in diameter are excused. Does this exemption apply only to a single spot?
records.answer:
This 5 cm in diameter or less excused exception applies to multiple splashes of impurity, too.

Multiple splashes of impure water will be combined in size, but it’s not necessary to combine them unless there’s an obvious excessive splashing. Assume the impurity is within the excused amount and ignore it.

The fiqh of Islam is practical. You are not expected to excessively combine impurities in this way. In general, when there is great difficulty avoiding impurity, such as splashes when relieving oneself, it is excused. An explicit example of this is small splashes of urine coming into contact with one’s body or clothes.

Allah Most High says, “Allah wants ease for you, and does not want unbearable hardship for you” [Quran 2:185; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

General Ruling

When urine comes out, it invalidates one’s wudu and, as a result, one’s prayer if in it.

If the urine or other filth is 5cm or less in diameter, it is recommended but not obligatory to remove it. It is, however, improper not to remove it unless doing so is difficult in one’s circumstances.

More than 5 cm in diameter of urine or other filth must be removed. Not removing it will invalidate one’s prayer, even if one performs wudu. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

A way is to learn the essentials of purity and prayer and apply them without worrying about minute details.

records.title: Is Selling Gold Through eBay’s Authentication Process Valid?
records.question: I sold ten grams of gold on eBay at a fixed price. The buyer paid eBay, which held the funds while the gold was sent to an authentication center and released to me about a day later.
records.answer:
Your sale is valid, and nothing is owed. You should know, though, that the position it rests on is the minority one.

Do the Rules of Sarf Apply to Modern Currency?

Everything turns on one question: is gold sold for pounds a currency exchange (sarf) or an ordinary sale? For a true currency exchange, the rule is strict and undisputed.

Imam Marghinani (Allah have mercy on him) writes that “both counter-values must be taken into possession before the parties separate,” and that “if they separate in a currency exchange before taking possession of both counter-values, or of one of them, the contract is void, because the condition, which is possession, has failed” [Marghinani, al-Hidaya].

The disagreement is over what paper money is.

One. Modern currency has replaced gold and silver.

In this view, modern currency stands in the place of gold and silver, so gold against sterling is a currency exchange, and both sides must be taken into account before the parties part. That is the position of contemporary fiqh councils and standard-setting bodies, and it is the more widely held view today. On it, your sale was defective because eBay held the price against a risk you were still carrying, and money you cannot draw on is not money you possess.

Two. Paper currency is money by cconvention—andthe rules of “sarf” don’t apply to iit—butriba does apply to it.

The second view is the one we follow, and it goes back to Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (Allah have mercy on him): paper currency is money by convention rather than by creation, and so stands in the position of fulus, the old copper coinage.

records.title: Is Ignorance of Allah’s Attributes Disbelief?
records.question: Out of ignorance, I once thought that Allah Most High has no need to be grateful to anyone, because I judged that gratitude did not befit His Majesty. I later learned that al-Shakur, the Most Grateful, is among His names.
records.answer:
No, neither you nor the person in your example left Islam. The thought that worried you came from a place of reverence, not rejection.

Let us begin with the foundations of our belief. We affirm for Allah every perfection, and we declare Him free of all deficiency. As Imam al-Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him) said, ‘He alone possesses perfection, exalted above deficiency, hallowed beyond every defect.’ The names of Allah are not just labels. Each name has a true meaning that is affirmed for Him.

Imam al-Zabidi (Allah have mercy on him) explains that every divine name either points to Allah’s very essence, to one of His attributes, to the negation of any defect, or to the affirmation of His majesty and perfection.

When a name refers to an attribute, that attribute is not separate from Allah, nor is it identical to His essence. Rather, it is inseparable from Him.

Consider your own thoughts in this light. You were trying to affirm Allah’s perfection by denying any need, indebtedness, or obligation to His creation. This instinct is correct.

What you had not yet learned is that the name al-Shakur, the Most Grateful, also negates these deficiencies. It means that Allah gives abundantly for even a small act, not that He owes anyone anything.

You did not deny anything that must be affirmed. Disbelief is to deny what is essential.

Imam al-Bajuri (Allah have mercy on him) explains that some forms of ignorance are not the opposite of faith at all, such as not knowing certain details of Allah’s majesty or attributes that are not obvious from His actions.

The Hanafis say the same: Mulla Ali al-Qari (Allah have mercy on him) says it is more correct that a person is excused by ignorance, unless it is about something every Muslim must know by necessity.

The meanings of Allah’s names are learned. Not every Muslim knows them all from the beginning.

Your second question is similar. If someone considers a hypothetical case and answers it incorrectly, they have made a mistake in understanding, not in belief.

Allah Most High says, ‘Allah’s are the most beautiful names, so call on Him by them; and leave those who heretically ill-use His names.’

Imam al-Qushayri (Allah have mercy on him) explains that misusing Allah’s names means either adding to them or taking away from them. You did neither. You simply had not learned yet.

Call on Him by Them

Do not judge yourself harshly. Instead, make this an opportunity to learn. Imam al-Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him) advises us to reflect on the meanings of Allah’s names and attributes, so that their secrets may be opened to us.

I encourage you to study the ninety-nine names of Allah with a qualified teacher, and to take your time. Remember: whatever a name means for Allah is far beyond what it means for us.

records.title: Is Disclosure of a Concealed Past Sin Required Before Marriage?
records.question: I committed a serious sin in the past, repented sincerely, and have not returned to it. Allah concealed it. A prospective spouse has strict criteria regarding a woman’s past and is asking me directly for a yes-or-no answer.
records.answer:
Striving for this balance is itself a sign of faith and sincerity.

You are not required to disclose what Allah has concealed, and choosing not to answer is not considered deception.

What Allah has concealed, you are commanded to keep concealed, of yourself first of all. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “All of my Community will be pardoned except those who flaunt their sins.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

Imam Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him) counts retelling past sins among the harms of the tongue: it tears the covering Allah drew over you and spreads what should stay buried. [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din]

Your past, which Allah has covered, is not something a prospective husband has a right to know. What concerns him is your present state, your religion, and anything ongoing that would affect the marriage. A sin that is over, sincerely repented from, and concealed by Allah is not among these matters.

What You May Say

Tell him plainly that you do not discuss your past, that it is a matter between you and Allah, and that you will not lie to him about it either way. That is honest and complete.

You are not hiding a fact about your present; you are declining to publicize what Allah has hidden, which is exact.

Do not deny the sin outright, as lying is neither necessary nor permitted. The way forward is to uphold truthfulness while maintaining the covering of Allah.ay out of this, and it is not needed.

If He Cannot Accept That

If he chooses to step back, allow him to do so. You are not required to withdraw first, nor to purchase the marriage by disclosing what Allah has concealed. If someone insists on uncovering what Allah has covered, this may indicate how he would approach your past within the marriage.

Trust that Allah may be protecting you from harm.

Repentance Closes the File

Sincere repentance erases what came before, and Allah does not ask you to bring it forth again. Maintain the good opinion of Allah that led you to repent, and ask Him to grant you a spouse who will honor what Allah has honored and covered.

records.title: Can a Convert Leave More Than One-Third to Non-Muslim Family?
records.question: I am a convert to Islam, and I have no Muslim relatives. May I leave more than a third of my estate to my non-Muslim family?
records.answer:
Yes. With no Muslim heirs, you may leave your non-Muslim family more than a third, and indeed the whole of your estate. Here are your three questions, in order.

One: The Third Limits Bequests Only Where There Are Heirs

Non-Muslim relatives do not inherit from a Muslim, so anything your family receives from you passes by bequest (wasiyya), not by inheritance. The one-third limit on bequests exists to protect the heirs.

When the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) limited Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (Allah be pleased with him) to a third, calling even a third much, he gave the reason himself, in meaning: it is better to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor, asking of people. [Bukhari; Muslim]

Where no one holds that right, the limit does not bind. Ibn Abidin states the principle plainly: preventing more than a third is for the heirs’ sake, so where there is no heir, there is no prevention. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar, 2.424; 6.765]

The school goes further for someone in exactly your position: the Hawi al-Qudsi counsels that one who has no heir and no debt does well to bequeath all of his wealth. [Radd al-Muhtar (Takmila), Kitab al-Wasaya]

A word of caution: this ruling depends on you having no Muslim heirs at all. If, at the time of your passing, any Muslim relative exists—even a distant one—the situation changes.

If anyone in your family embraces Islam, review your will to ensure it remains valid. In this, consult a qualified Muslim scholar directly–or reach out to us.

Two: The Quranic Shares Do Not Govern Your Bequest

The fixed shares in the Quran apply to inheritance among Muslim heirs. Since your family will receive by bequest, these shares do not apply.

You may allocate to each person as you see fit, with wisdom and kindness. Many are surprised by this: the division is truly yours to decide.

Three: Witnessing Is About Proof, Not Validity

The requirement for two Muslim male witnesses relates to proving a bequest if it is disputed. It is not a condition for the validity of the will itself. What matters most is that your will can be carried out where you live. A Quebec notarial will is valid.

If you are able to have two upright Muslims witness it, that is better. If not, there is no harm.

A Will Is Worship

Writing your will with care is itself an act of worship. Showing generosity to the family Allah has given you is a form of excellence (ihsan) that they will remember you by.

records.title: Is Marketing for a Business That Accepts Conventional Insurance Permissible?
records.question: I provide marketing, customer acquisition, and referral services for a business whose services are lawful but accept payment through conventional insurance.
records.answer:
Yes, this work is permissible. Marketing a lawful service is itself a lawful service. You conclude no insurance contract: the customer chooses it, the insurer pays, and the business pays you for lawful work.

The Hanafi school looks at where the wrong occurs. When another person’s free choice stands between your work and the wrong, responsibility for the wrong attaches to their act, not to yours.

This is the reasoning the school applies to selling grape juice, which only becomes wine by another’s deed, and it runs through the discussions in the Hidaya and Ibn Abidin’s treatment of hired carriage. [Marghinani, al-Hidaya, 4.378; Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar, 6.392]

Your marketing promotes a lawful service; the insurance contract, where it happens, is the customer’s and insurer’s own act.

Answering Truthfully Is Not Participation

When someone asks whether insurance is accepted, say yes. Stating a fact about payment methods is not participation in the payment method. Truthfulness here is simply honesty in trade, and honesty in trade is beloved to Allah.

Advertising: Disclose, Do Not Induce

One distinction is worth keeping. Listing insurance as an accepted payment method is standard disclosure, and it is fine.

Making the insurance itself the selling point, urging people toward that contract, moves your speech closer to promoting the contract itself, and godfearingness (taqwa) says step back from that.

Keep the promotion on the service; let the payment details inform rather than urge.

I answered a nearby case from a recruiter at a company offering interest-based customer financing along the same lines; you may find it useful below.

Keep the Work Clean and the Heart Present

Renew your intention that this work feeds your family and serves people honestly, and be the one in the room whose word can be trusted completely.

May Allah put blessings (baraka) in your earnings.

records.title: Does One Kaffara Suffice for Multiple Broken Oaths?
records.question: Over the years, I have sworn many oaths, on different matters, many of them under compulsive misgivings (waswasa), and I broke some.
records.answer:
The way forward is simpler than you may think, and Allah has made the path to relief open and accessible.

For your situation, one expiation will cover all the oaths you actually broke. As for the oaths that arose only from waswasa, they never bound you at all, and you are not responsible for them.

Which Oaths Counted at All

An oath is only what is spoken aloud. Thoughts or worries that remain in your mind, without being uttered, do not count as oaths. There is nothing to discharge for them.

If you spoke words while truly overwhelmed by waswasa, and not in control of your speech, you are not held to those utterances.

Scholars such as Ibn Abidin have explained that such pronouncements do not take effect. If you were genuinely compelled in those moments, those words did not count as oaths.

There is an important distinction: if you spoke an oath hastily, but you were present in mind and not overwhelmed, then it does count as an oath in the Hanafi school, even if you did not intend it deeply.

The key is whether you were truly overpowered by waswasa or not. Reflect on your past moments with this in mind, decide once, and then do not revisit or worry about them again.

One Expiation for Whatever Remains

For the oaths that did count and were broken, the Hanafi school holds that if several expiations become due, they merge into one. This is the position of Imam Muhammad, as related by Ibn Abidin and others.

The ruling applies to all oaths, even if they were about different matters. What merges is the expiation itself, which is of one type, regardless of the details of the oaths.

What to Actually Do

Give one expiation now, and then consider the matter closed.

Allah Most High says: “Allah will not take you to task for thoughtlessly uttered oaths, but rather for swearing binding oaths, the expiation for breaking which is to feed ten unfortunates the usual fare you feed your own families, or to clothe them, or to free a slave; So whoever finds no means to do any of these, then to fast three days: That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn.” [Quran 5:89; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Feed ten poor people two meals each, or clothe them.

In the Hanafi school, you may also give the equivalent value in money, and a trustworthy charity can carry this out for you. If you truly cannot afford this, then fast three consecutive days instead.

Close the Account and Walk On

Once you have given the expiation, your responsibility is fulfilled. There is no need to recount or keep score; the Shariah does not ask this of you.

Allah has made this door easy so that you can move forward with peace.

Guard your tongue gently in the future, say ‘in sha’ Allah’ when you speak of what you intend, and trust your affairs to your Lord.

records.title: What Do I Do When My Husband Refuses to Acknowledge My Family?
records.question: My husband and I get along well and prioritize each other. The one recurring conflict is his refusal to visit or interact with my family.
records.answer:
What you describe is a real test: loving your husband and loving your family, yet finding it difficult to bring them together. May Allah mend this for you, and reward your patience and striving.

Your husband is right about the narrow ruling and mistaken about what it means for your marriage. He is not obliged to build friendships with your family.

He is obliged to honor you in what concerns them: to support your ties with them, to speak of them with respect, and to meet them with basic good character when occasions arise.

What the Fiqh Actually Says

The duty of maintaining kinship (silat al-rahim) binds a person to their own blood relatives; your family are not his kin in that technical sense. That much of his claim is true. But the Sacred Law does not stop at that line.

Allah Most High commands husbands: “But rather live with them graciously and reasonably.” [Quran 4:19; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Living with a wife graciously means making space for what she loves and who she loves.

He may not cut you off from your family or resent your connection to them. Keeping those ties is your religious duty, and helping a spouse fulfill her duties is part of living together with excellence.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “The best of you is the one who is best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family.” [Tirmidhi]

Excellence to one’s wife includes honoring the people she comes from.

Name the Real Issue, Gently

What you describe beneath the fiqh issue is a matter of values: weighing people by status or background rather than by character and deen. This is something to address gently and without blame, as the Quran itself addresses it first:

“Verily the greatest of you all in the sight of Allah is the most godfearing of you.” [Quran 49:13; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

From what you mention, your family’s faith and warmth are what Allah values most.

Move From Argument to Excellence (Ihsan)

Do not focus on arguing the obligation. Fiqh arguments rarely soften hearts. Instead, ask for something small and specific: a visit at Eid, attending weddings or funerals, or sharing a meal once a season.

Small steps can open big doors. If he does not respond to your request, consider seeking the help of someone he respects, such as an imam or a senior person of faith. Sometimes, advice from another can reach the heart when a spouse’s words cannot.

For Your Own Heart

His distance is not a judgment on you or your family. Keep your ties warm, even if you attend alone for now. Your duty to your family remains, and he does not have the right to take it away.

Pray for him, not about him. Allah is the Turner of hearts, and many husbands have been softened by a wife’s quiet du’a and steady dignity.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Work and Deal with Pig Leather?
records.question: I work at a leather shoe shop as a salesperson and am interested in applying for a cobbler position. However, I have a few questions regarding working with pig leather in both positions.
records.answer:
The Prophet was asked, “Which earnings are the purest?” He replied, “A man’s work with his hands” [Musnad Ahmad]. It is lovely to hear that Muslims are pursuing and developing this craft.

Pig leather is considered intrinsically impure, regardless of whether it is dry or wet. However, the impurity is only transferred if either the pig leather or the surface with which it comes into contact is wet. [Khatib, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

It is not permissible to market or sell these shoes. The Prophet (May Allah bless him and grant him peace) prohibited taking payment for dogs, and scholars have extended this ruling to pigs. [Muslim]

Commenting on this narration, Imam Nawawi states, “And since it is among the worst forms of earnings and is impure, this indicates that selling it is prohibited, that its sale is invalid, and that its price is not lawful.” [Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim]

It is not permissible for you to use pig leather to make or repair shoes.

When you become a cobbler, explore whether your employer can assign you to work involving permissible materials, or consider other opportunities within the craft that allow you to earn a halal livelihood.

These restrictions are designed to protect and help us grow. Your concern to earn a halal income is praiseworthy, and Allah is the Best of providers.

And with Allah alone is our success.

records.title: Is Claiming Pre-Judgment Interest as a Lawyer Permissible?
records.question: I’ve been practicing law for over a decade, and I’ve been considering focusing more on litigation and moving away from corporate/real estate work because of concerns about being involved with Riba-based loans and mortgages.
records.answer:
“Allah never wastes the wage of those who excel in good”. [Quran, 12:90]

Each case would have to be considered on its own merits. Prejudgment interest in a personal injury case is treated differently from money that is simply owed.

In the former, there is a basis for construing the prejudgment interest as part of the claim itself, thereby making it valid. The same, however, cannot be said of money that is owed.

Injury Case

This type of statutory prejudgment interest is not riba. Interest arises in the context of a loan contract. In the absence of a loan contract, interest does not exist. There is no loan contract between the plaintiff and the defendant that gives rise to interest.

The Sharia simply construes the above amount as part of the award. It is therefore permissible for you to negotiate settlements that take this amount into account.

The legal fiction of a loan, which gives rise to the terminology of interest, serves as the basis for determining the value of the plaintiff’s loss.

Interest is used here as a means of determining value rather than as a stipulated positive return on a loan. The resulting amount is then incorporated into the overall award.

This is analogous to the position of scholars who hold that a usurper must compensate the owner based on the highest value of the usurped goods between the time of the usurpation and the time of their destruction. [See Muqri, Rawd al-Matalib]

Money Owed

In the case of money owed, it would not be permissible to negotiate settlements along these lines, as it can no longer be construed as an increase in the award.

This applies to all cases in which a liability is established at one point in time and an additional charge is levied for time. This is the classic case of interest that the Quran prohibits. [See Misri, Riba]

Rather, it is clearly an increase in the amount due directly linked to the passage of time. In this case, only valid, directly related charges to recouping the money may be added. [See AAOIFI] And Allah knows best.

In the case of money owed, it would not be permissible to negotiate settlements along these lines, as the additional amount can only be construed as a stipulated positive return on a deferred ‘monetary’ liability.

This applies to all cases in which a liability is established at a particular point in time and an additional charge is imposed in consideration of the passage of time. This is the classic form of interest prohibited by the Quran. [See Misri, Riba]

In such cases, only valid charges that are directly related to recovering the outstanding amount may be added. This must not be disposed to the benefit of the ‘lender’ [See AAOIFI]

Practicing Caution

It is important that you consult a scholar regularly, on a case-by-case basis, to ensure that your activities remain Sharia-compliant. This will give you peace of mind and further encouragement to continue the good work your vocation enables you to do. It will also help alleviate religious anxiety.

When in doubt, consult a qualified scholar where appropriate; otherwise, avoid the matter altogether. The Prophet (May Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Leave what causes you doubt for that which does not.” [Tirmidhi]

And with Allah alone is our success.

records.title: Is Suppressing Emotions Necessary for Sincerity?
records.question: To avoid insincerity, must a person deny his emotions?
records.answer:
No. Sincerity is a matter of what you are aiming at, not of what you feel. And you do not have to flatten your feelings to be sincere. Sincerity is seeking Allah’s Pleasure through your actions and having no ulterior motives.

Given how critical sincerity is, our tradition is more careful here than a simple yes or no: not every gladness is the same gladness, and learning to tell them apart is the real work.

What Sincerity Is

Sincerity (ikhlas) is the singling out of Allah in obedience by way of the intention, as Imam Qushayri defines it. [Qushayri, al-Risala al-Qushayriyya] Notice where the weight falls: on what the act is for.

Allah Most High says: “Nor have they been commanded aught else but to worship Allah alone, making their religion sincerely His.” [Quran 98:5; Keller, The Quran Beheld] The verse points to the direction of worship and says nothing about the worshipper’s inner weather.

Imam Ghazali defines the opposite — showing off, or insincerity (riya) — in the same way: showing off is the desire to stand in people’s hearts through obedience to Allah. [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din; with Zabidi’s commentary, Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin]

A definition framed in terms of what a person wants cannot be satisfied or broken by a feeling. Showing off is a movement of the will toward creation; gladness is something that happens to you.

Gladness After the Deed

Imam Ghazali addresses your question directly. If bare gladness arises after the act is finished — gladness that it became known, without your having displayed it — the deed was already completed under the description of sincerity, and we may hope that what arises afterward does not fold back upon it.

The danger lies in the appetite to display it, and in acting on that. A group of the knowers of Allah, he notes, held precisely this. [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din; with Zabidi’s commentary, Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin]

Four Kinds of Gladness That Are Praiseworthy, and One That Is Not

Imam Ghazali sets out five kinds of joy at being discovered in an act of obedience, and four of them are praiseworthy:

One. You concealed the act and intended it for Allah, and when people came to know of it you understood that Allah disclosed it and made the beautiful in your state apparent, so your joy is at Allah’s gracious regard for you, not at their praise.

Two. Or you take His concealing your ugliness and disclosing your beauty in this world as a sign that He will do the same in the next.

Three. Or you expect that those who saw will follow you in the good, so the reward multiplies.

Four. Or you rejoice at the faith of those who saw — that they love an obedient person rather than resenting him — and the mark of sincerity in this fourth kind is that your joy at their praising someone else equals your joy at their praising you.

Five. The fifth is the blameworthy one: joy at your standing being established in people’s hearts, so that they praise you, honor you, and see to your needs. [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din; with Zabidi’s commentary, Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin]

So the question is never “Did I feel something?” It is “What was the feeling about?”

One Honest Warning

Imam Ghazali also gives the sign of hidden showing off, and it deserves saying plainly. A servant may be sincere, may hate showing off and push it away, may complete the act that way — and then, when people learn of it, feel gladness and ease and expansion, and find that this lightened the weight of the worship on his heart.

That relief is the tell. Had the heart not been turned toward people, their noticing would not have eased anything. Showing off was lying in the heart, he says, as fire lies hidden in flint, and their looking struck the spark. [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din; with Zabidi’s commentary, Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin]

Read that as diagnosis, not accusation. And note the limit he himself draws: bare gladness at people’s noticing, where the effect does not visibly reach the act, is far from invalidating the prayer, and that, he says, is what accords with the canon of fiqh as the Shafi’i jurists frame it.

He adds that those who plunged into this subject without regard for the jurists’ rules ended up voiding acts of worship over the slightest passing thought.

The Sunna Forecloses the Scruple

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) was asked about the man who does something good, and people praise him for it, and he said: “That is the believer’s glad tidings hastened forward.” [Muslim 2642]

Imam Nawawi placed it under a chapter heading: when the righteous person is praised, it is glad tidings, and it does not harm him.

Feeling in the Lives of the Prophets

If emotion were itself a defect, the Quran would not narrate the prophets’ emotions without censure.

Yaqub (peace be upon him) grieved until his sight went: “And he turned from them and said, ‘O my searing grief for Joseph!’ And his eyes grew white for very sorrow, choking back his grief.” [Quran 12:84; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Challenged on it, he neither denied the feeling nor apologized for it: “I but complain my ungovernable anguish and sorrow to Allah; And I know of Allah what you know not.” [Quran 12:86; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The anguish stands, named and owned. What the Quran regulates is where he carries it.

Aim the Heart, and Let the Feelings Be

So point the intention at Allah when you begin, and then leave your emotions alone. Do not audit them, and do not read their presence as evidence against you. Policing feeling for traces of insincerity is itself a species of misgiving, and it grows by being fed.

If you want to strengthen sincerity, do not do it by subtracting feeling. Do some good quietly, where no one will ever know. That works on the intention directly, and it is also the test the Ihya gives you: if being unseen costs you nothing, there was nothing hidden in the flint.
references: Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din; with Zabidi’s commentary, Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin

records.title: Is a Penalty Required for Mistakes During Sa‘i and Ihram?
records.question: During an umra performed while I was very unwell, I stepped outside the boundary during sa‘i, later counted fourteen circuits instead of seven, and used perfumed soap for istinja and washed my hands to the wrists.
records.answer:
What you went through was heavy, and it is a mercy that you completed the rites at all. Take the answer below as relief rather than as a reckoning.

There is no penalty for crossing the boundary, since you returned and performed the sa‘i, and no penalty for performing an extra seven circuits out of ignorance. Washing the hands to the wrists with perfumed soap does entail a penalty.

Allah Most High says, “Verily Safa and Marwa are sites of Allah’s worship. So whoever makes a pilgrimage to the Sacred House or the lesser visitation, there is no wrong or harm in making many a round between them. And whoever does more of the best than even that, Allah truly is supreme in thanks, all-knowing.” [Quran 2:158; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

Stepping Outside the Boundary

You wrote that you accidentally crossed the boundary while looking out. That alone is not enough to conclude that a penalty is due, so do not carry it.

Fourteen Circuits Instead of Seven

The sa‘i is valid where a person performs fourteen circuits rather than seven out of ignorance. Despite the additional seven, no violation of the ihram has occurred. [Shaykh Zada, Majma al-Anhar fi Sharh Multaqa al-Abhur]

Perfuming a Whole Limb

Perfuming an entire limb in one sitting does entail a penalty.

The sacrifice of a sheep must be carried out within the sacred precinct (haram) in Makka, so you may ask someone traveling from your country for umrah to discharge it there on your behalf. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

You Are Not Being Pressed for It

You are unemployed and dependent on your parents for now. As long as you intend to discharge the penalty, do not worry and take your time in doing so. An obligation you intend and cannot yet afford is not a debt hanging over your worship.
references: Shaykh Zada, Majma al-Anhar fi Sharh Multaqa al-Abhur

records.title: Can I Give Up My Right of Divorce?
records.question: I make hasty decisions when angry. I have already issued two divorces, and I fear a third. Can I give up my right of divorce, or bind myself by a contract so that it cannot be issued in haste?
records.answer:
There is no legally recognized way for a husband to relinquish his right of divorce entirely.

Even if he delegates it, or conditions it on a written statement or a binding intention, his own right of divorce never ceases and can still take effect.

Ibn Abbas (Allah be pleased with him) related that the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Divorce is the right of the husband, who has authority over the woman through marriage.” [Ibn Majah]

The one who holds the right of divorce is the husband. The wife does not hold it. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

What You Can Do Instead

The right of divorce placed in the husband’s hands carries great divine wisdom. It is a grave trust and part of your moral responsibility, and the way to honor it is to make hasty use of it harder rather than to try to sign it away.

Take a marriage course and an anger management course, so that you learn to hold your tongue in the moment. And draft a safeguard undertaking with a reliable mufti or scholar: a written promise not to pronounce divorce, and to seek mediation or consultation first.

That will not remove the right, but it will stand between you and an impulsive word.

records.title: Is a Threat of Divorce Considered Divorce?
records.question: My husband told me that if I kept up my attitude, I should stay in my country and send our child back. I asked if he meant divorce or if he was threatening divorce.
records.answer:
No divorce has taken place. Your marriage is still valid. What your husband said was only a warning about what he might do in the future, and a warning is not the same as actually declaring a divorce. And Allah knows best.

Plain and Allusive Words

There are two types of words that can cause a divorce. Plain words (sarih) clearly state divorce and take effect whether or not the husband intends it.

Allusive words (kinaya) only hint at separation, like “you are free,” “you are separated,” or “rejoin your kin,” and these only count as divorce if the husband actually means divorce by them. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin; Misri, Umdat al-Salik]

Your husband said, “If you are going to keep this stupid attitude up, then stay in your country because I will not tolerate it anymore. Send our child back and you can stay there.”

There is no mention of divorce in what he said. At most, “stay in your country” could be seen as an allusive phrase, since it talks about being apart.

But even then, it only counts if he meant divorce at that moment, and he clearly said he only meant it as a threat. His explanation about his intention is accepted. [Nawawi, al-Majmu Sharh al-Muhadhdhab]

The Tense He Used Settles it

There is another, even clearer reason. His words were about something he might do in the future, not something he was doing at that moment.

Using the future tense, like saying “I will divorce you,” is only a promise or a threat. It does not cause a divorce, even if the man means it as a threat or even if what he warned about later happens. [Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj; Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj; Bakri, I‘anat al-Talibin]

Why cannot the whole conversation you describe produce a divorce? He was not divorcing you. He was telling you what he might do if things did not change.

This is not a conditional divorce either. For a conditional divorce, there must be a clear statement linking divorce to an event, like “if you do this, you are divorced.” He did not say that. He only mentioned a consequence he would impose, not an actual divorce.

The Word “Yes” in the Exchange

There is a known ruling that when a husband is asked, “Have you divorced your wife?” and he answers, “Yes,” she is divorced even if he did not intend it. [Misri, Umdat al-Salik]

That ruling does not apply in your case because of how the question was asked. You did not ask, “Have you divorced me?” Instead, you asked, “Did you threaten divorce?” So when he said “Yes,” he was only confirming the threat, not a divorce. A “yes” only answers the question it is given, nothing more.

He also cleared up any confusion himself. When asked if he meant divorce, he said, “No. It was a threat.” His answers have been clear and consistent from start to finish.

Taking Divorce Seriously

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Three things are always taken seriously whether said seriously or in jest: marriage (nikah), divorce (talaq), and taking back (raj‘a).” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi; Ibn Maja]

This hadith means that if a man actually says words of divorce, he cannot later claim he was not serious. But it does not turn words that are not divorce into a divorce. Since no words of divorce were said, this hadith does not apply to your situation.

A Word to Your Husband

Your marriage remains valid, and that is the ruling. However, there is still something important to say about how your marriage is being handled. (Most High) says, “Do not hold them back to harm them, so that you may exceed the limits. Whoever does that surely wrongs his own soul.” [Quran, 2:231]

Keeping a wife under the constant threat of divorce, and also threatening to separate her from her child, is the kind of harm this verse warns against. Divorce is meant to be a remedy in Islamic law, not a tool to control a spouse.

A man who brings up divorce in every argument should realize that he is putting his marriage and his responsibility before Allah at risk each time.

Principle and Practical Guidance

A marriage that is certain cannot be undone by doubt. Nothing has happened that counts as a divorce, so nothing has changed.

Three things follow from that.

Let this question go. Do not keep rereading the messages looking for something you might have missed, and do not look for more opinions just to calm an anxiety that has no real basis. This only leads to unnecessary doubts (waswasa), and the best way to deal with them is to ignore them, not to keep investigating.

Ask your husband to stop mentioning divorce unless he truly means it. If he only brings it up when he is serious, most of this stress will go away immediately.

Talk to someone qualified about this pattern in your marriage. The legal question has been answered, but the state of your marriage is a different issue. It deserves proper attention from an Allah-conscious counselor and a scholar who can take the time to understand your full situation, and advise accordingly.

records.title: What Should a Couple Do After Intercourse During Menstruation?
records.question: My husband and I had a marital relationship during my period of confusion.
records.answer:
If you did not know your period started, as you mentioned, and had a marital relationship, you would not be sinful. However, you should both seek forgiveness and repent to Allah Most High.

Allah Most High says, “And they ask you about menstruation; Say: it is foul, so leave off from women while in their menses, and approach them not until again pure. [Quran, 2:222]

Abu Dhar (Allah be pleased with him) reported: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Verily, Allah has pardoned my nation for their mistakes, their forgetfulness, and what they are coerced into doing.” [Ibn Majah]

It is also prohibited for the husband to touch the area between her navel and knee with skin-to-skin contact, regardless of whether sexual desire is present or not. The back, hips, and thighs are all included in this prohibition.

Skin-to-skin contact with all other areas of the body is permissible, like the chest, back, arms, and calves. [Shurunbulali, Maraqi al-Falah]

Since it was a genuine accidental fall into something prohibited, don’t fall into guilt; just seek forgiveness, as this will suffice.

records.title: Is a Secret Nikah Without My Father’s Consent Valid?
records.question: When I was younger, I entered into a secret nikah online. A Hanafi shaykh acted as my wali, even though my father was alive and unaware. Later, my parents refused the marriage.
records.answer:
You are single. Both the view you follow and the one under which the contract was made lead to the same outcome, and you handled the situation correctly in both cases. You owe your former husband nothing, and you do not have to tell a future suitor about this unless he asks you directly.

The Position You Follow: There Was Never a Valid Contract

In the Shafi’i school, and in the position of the majority, which you sincerely hold, the presence of a valid guardian (wali) is a condition for the validity of a woman’s marriage contract.

The father is the primary wali, and where he is alive and reachable, his consent cannot be bypassed. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin]

Our mother Aisha (Allah be pleased with her) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Any woman who marries without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is void, her marriage is void, her marriage is void.” [Ahmad; Tirmidhi; Abu Dawud; Ibn Maja]

A shaykh can only act as a wali if there is no wali, if the wali cannot be reached, or if the wali refuses without a valid reason, and a judge steps in.

None of these applies to your situation. Your father was alive and available, and had neither refused nor appointed anyone else, since he did not know about the marriage. The shaykh, therefore, had no standing to act as your wali.

Accordingly, no valid marriage took place. There was nothing to end, and nothing more needs to be done.

The Hanafi Reading: A Valid Contract That Khula Ended

Because the contract was done by a Hanafi shaykh and the man followed the Hanafi school, it makes sense to consider the situation from that perspective as well.

In the Hanafi school, a woman of sound mind who has reached majority may contract her own marriage, and the contract is complete with a proposal, an acceptance, and two Muslim male witnesses or one male and two females. Contracting it without the guardian’s involvement is prohibitively disliked (makruh tahriman), but the contract itself stands. [Maydani, al-Lubab fi Sharh al-Kitab]

The guardian is not left without recourse in that school. Where the husband is not a suitable match (kafa’a), the father retains the right to seek annulment. [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

From this perspective, you were married, and then you asked for a release (khula) in exchange for compensation, which he accepted. Khula results in a final separation, and once you have completed your waiting period, the marriage is over.

Both Roads End in the Same Place

If the marriage was not valid, you were never married and are now single. If it was valid, it ended with khula and your completed idda, so you are also single now. There is no other possibility, and no situation where you are still connected to this man.

You were right to resolve the matter according to both his school and your own.

Scholars recommend this kind of caution in situations like yours, and it means your position is clear from every perspective.

If the marriage was consummated, your idda was necessary, not just a precaution, because a waiting period is required after intercourse that was believed to be lawful. You did exactly what was needed.

What You Owe Him

You don’t owe each other anything because of the marriage. There is no remaining waiting period, financial support, need to return to him, or anything that requires his permission, either.

There are just two small financial matters to check and finish. If your khula included returning a dowry or a specific amount and any part is still unpaid, make sure to settle it as soon as possible.

If you were owed a dowry that was never paid, you can choose to waive it, which is easiest if you do not want further contact. Other than that, nothing remains.

Telling Your Parents, and Telling a Future Husband

Your parents already know about the marriage. They found out, refused it, and the issue was settled. Whatever obligation you had to tell them is now fulfilled. You do not need to bring it up again or give them more details than they already have.

For a future husband, a past marriage that has ended does not have to be shared unless asked. You only need to disclose a marriage that is still ongoing, and hiding that would be deception and a sin. This does not apply to you.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever deceives us is not of us.” [Muslim]

Deception means actually giving a false impression. Choosing not to share your past is not the same as creating a false impression. You do not have to bring this up with a suitor.

If he asks you directly if you have been married before, answer honestly. You can keep your answer brief, saying a nikah was contracted and later ended. You do not have to give details, reasons, or names. You do owe honesty, but not full disclosure.

Still, be aware that he may not be fully satisfied with a brief answer, and he is free to decide on that basis.

Allah conceals what He conceals for a reason, and you are not asked to lift that covering from yourself.

On Your Regret

You were young and did not know better, and you trusted a religious authority you had every reason to believe. That is important.

Allah (Most High) says, “There is no blame on you for what you do by mistake, but for what your hearts intend.” [Quran, 33:5]

Since then, you have learned the ruling, accepted your parents’ decision, properly ended the relationship in accordance with both schools, and repented.

This is a full response, and more than many people do. Regret that leads to correction has served its purpose, and Allah does not expect you to keep feeling guilty for something that has already been resolved.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The principle is that certainty is not lifted by doubt. Your marriage ended, definitely, and doubt cannot restore a contract that has been closed twice over.

Think of this matter as closed. Do not keep thinking about the nikah, searching for details that might change the ruling, or looking for more opinions to ease your worries. This only leads to unnecessary doubts, which should be ignored.

Keep no channel open with him. Since nothing remains between you, contact serves no lawful purpose now.

When you marry in the future, do so properly and openly, with your wali, witnesses, and your family present.

The public marriage that the Sunna encourages is not just a formality. It is a protection you did not have before.

records.title: How Do I Calculate Missed Prayers When I Do Not Know the Number?
records.question: I am trying to estimate the number of missed obligatory prayers from 2 October 2014 to 27 June 2026, which comes to about 21,435 prayers if I missed every one.
records.answer:
Just deciding to face such a large number is an achievement in itself. Many people never even get to this stage.

In short, estimate on the higher side and use that as your target. Only lower the number for periods you are sure about. Praying ten make-up prayers each day, along with your five daily prayers, is allowed.

At that pace, it will take years, not months. I will answer your nine questions one by one.

1. Calculating when you do not know the exact number. If you cannot be sure, go with what seems most likely. Certainty is not removed by doubt: you know the prayer was required, but you are not sure if you prayed it, so you still need to make it up. [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza‘ir]

2. Is a reasonable estimate acceptable? Yes, after so many years, estimating is what you are expected to do. No one in your situation can do better than that. Your estimate should be on the higher side.

3. If you are unsure whether your estimate is too high or too low, choos e the higher number. A clear obligation is not removed by an uncertain effort, and any extra prayers you do will not harm you.

4. Using 21,435 as your starting target. The total of 21,435 is correct for that time period. Only subtract days you are sure about. Since you are not certain about the 150 days, keep them in and start with 21,435. If you were sure about all of them, the number would be 20,685. Lower your target as you go along.

5. Adjusting if you later recall praying. If you remember praying on certain days, subtract those prayers. Reducing the number because of a genuine recollection is essentially an accuracy adjustment.

One thing to note: if you are not sure when you reached puberty, use the latest possible date. The strict rule applies to whether you prayed, not to when you became responsible for prayer.

6. Prayers missed deliberately. Be clear-eyed here without being crushed. Prayers left without a valid excuse are a grave matter calling for sincere repentance, and the relied-upon position is that they must be made up immediately, meaning in whatever time is not taken up by necessity.

Ibn Hajar al-Haytami (Allah have mercy on him) holds that a person in this position may not spend his time on anything else, optional prayers included, beyond what he is genuinely compelled to do. [Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj]

If you take the rule literally for 21,435 prayers, it would be impossible for anyone to keep up, and the scholars do not expect that.

Imam Abdullah al-Haddad (Allah have mercy on him) gave a fatwa allowing people to make up missed prayers at their own pace when the strict approach is too hard. [Abd al-Rahman al-Mashhur, Bughyat al-Mustarshidin]

Use this permission, make a plan you can stick to, and keep following it.

7. The intention. Intend as you would for a prayer performed on time: that you are praying, that it is obligatory, and which prayer it is. Form the intention in your heart, it is an act of the heart, not of the tongue, at the moment you say Allahu akbar.

You need not specify the number of cycles, nor that it is a make-up rather than a current prayer, though specifying is better, and you need not identify which day’s Dhuhr it was. [Nawawi, al-Majmuʿ]

8. Ten make-up prayers a day, along with the five daily prayers. This is allowed and is a good plan. There are two things to note. A make-up prayer has a reason, so you can pray it at any time, even during times when voluntary prayers are usually disliked.

Also, it is recommended but not required to pray your make-ups in their original order, such as Fajr before Dhuhr. If you break the order, it does not affect the validity. [Misri, ‘Umdat al-Salik]

What does this mean in practice? If you do 10 prayers a day, 21,435 prayers will take about 5 years and 10 months. If you do fifteen a day, it will take about three years and eleven months. Pick a pace you can keep up with even after four years.

Keep a basic written record, as seeing your progress helps you stay motivated over time in sha Allah.

9. Reliable sources. In English, Reliance of the Traveler [Umdat al-Salik, translated by Shaykh Nuh Ha Mim Keller] is the essential reference and treats missed prayers at length, and al-Maqasid of Imam Nawawi, also in Shaykh Nuh’s translation, is the standard short primer.

In Arabic: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami’s Tuhfat al-Muhtaj, Abdullah al-Jurdani’s Fath al-Allam bi Sharh Murshid al-Anam, and Abd al-Rahman al-Mashhur’s Bughyat al-Mustarshidin.

Better than reading alone, study this material with a teacher in our Shafiʿi fiqh courses.

Principle and Practical Guidance

The main rule is that a clear obligation is not removed by an uncertain effort, so estimate on the higher side. Also, Allah does not give anyone more than they can handle, so pick a pace you can keep up for years.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

Do not let the large number stop you from starting. Each make-up prayer you do pays off a debt and is a step toward repentance.
