Allah has kept the door open for you all this time. Start tonight with one set of five prayers, and begin keeping your record tomorrow.
references: Umdat al-Salik, translated by Shaykh Nuh Ha Mim Keller

records.title: Is a Plush Doll That Plays Quranic Verses Permissible?
records.question: I have started creating a product for toddlers/kids: a plush doll you can sleep with or bring with you for comfort. The doll has a sheep head and a little blanket on it. There are no open eyes; the eyes are closed, as if it’s sleeping.
records.answer:
Yes, such a product would be permissible. It is important to teach children the significance of our religion in their lives, and a bedtime routine is an excellent way to do so.

Also, children need something they can engage with, such as cute toys and interesting stories to learn from.

Your pursuit of this would be permissible, and we have descriptions of the children of the Sahaba also playing with dolls [Bukhari]. That will add to the permissibility of what you are doing.

Children’s toys are not something that’s honored and therefore not considered the same as images that are honored by being placed on the wall, for example.

It’s permissible to make them and even pray in the room where they’re on the floor, just as with a rug with an image that one stands on. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Allah bless you, the best of both worlds.

records.title: How Can Different Qiraat Preserve the Same Statement?
records.question: Across the qirat, there are 4 readings for 40:26.
records.answer:
The general rule with the canonical variant recitations is that all of it was said by the people quoted. However, Allah Most High quotes certain aspects or certain parts of their statement in one surah, for example, or in one variant recitation, and others in another.

The purpose here is to focus on what is relevant and to explore the meanings the Quran conveys through other recitations.

In the verse you mentioned, it seems like Pharaoh initially told these people that he was Afraid Musa would change their religion, or that corruption would spread in the land, and then he changed it to a decisive statement that corruption would spread in the land.

This would be through people following him, and that, in and of itself, would be seen as corruption by the Egyptians. [Ibn Ashur, al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir]

This suits the context of the verse, seeing as he was a coward and he wanted their support and permission in his plan to kill Musa, peace and blessings be upon him.

records.title: Can I Pray for Someone I Have Backbitten?
records.question: I backbit about someone with fragile mental health and fear that learning of it may severely hurt her. I also previously prayed that my backbiting would be exposed to her, God forbid.
records.answer:
Yes, you can make these prayers for her, and you should. If someone is sensitive and hearing about your backbiting will hurt them more than anyone else, it’s more of a reason to avoid it.

The guilt you’re feeling is something that can be used as a means of drawing closer to Allah.

It’s not a good feeling, so do your best to avoid these situations and avoid saying things like this. You’ll be okay, inshallah, in the future.

One thing you can do to compensate for it is to regularly do some good deeds and donate the reward of them to her and ask Allah to make her happy beyond measure, like you were intending.

That way, if she comes to you on the Day of Judgment, you will have already compensated her. (al-Shar’ani, al-Kawkab al-Shahiq)

records.title: What Are My Financial Duties Toward My Parents and Sister?
records.question: My father became involved in a scam, neglected my mother and disabled sister financially, and is now seriously unwell. I forgive him and want to support him, but my mother and sister have greater financial needs.
records.answer:
May Allah give you ease and well-being. This is a very difficult test.

Allah has commanded us to be kind to both parents in a way that everyone would recognize as being good.

This is the explanation of the term ma’ruf in the Quran in this context. The Quran says, “We have commanded people to honor their parents.” [Quran, 29:08]

As for the injustice your father did to your mother, Allah will deal with that. If your mother forgives him, you should try to look past it as well. However, if your mother is in greater financial need, then do what you can to support her.

If you can periodically spare something to say to your father, do so. At this time, he might be more in need of your understanding and your compassion than finances. Try to reach out to him periodically and see what you can do to maintain that relationship as best you can.

It is a difficult situation, and Allah sees it. So now you’ll be rewarded tremendously, and perhaps Allah will facilitate the means for everyone to be cared for without difficulty.

records.title: Can an Oath or a Vow Make the Stronger Opinion Binding?
records.question: Suppose a man utters a conditional formula about marriage and unbelief. He then adds a second undertaking: he swears by Allah, or vows, that in this very question, whichever of the two positions, that of Imam Abu Hanifa or that of Imam Shafiʿi, is stronger in evidence shall be the one binding on him.
records.answer:
Amin.

No, neither an oath nor a vow can do that. Oaths and vows affect your own actions, not how your actions are judged.

They cannot turn an issue that Sacred Law allows different opinions on into something you must follow in only one way.

If you act on a reliable opinion from your school, it does not become invalid just because you made an oath or vow. Allah knows best.

What an Oath Is, and What a Vow Is

An oath is a solemn statement to do or refrain from something, or that something is true, so if things turn out otherwise, the swearer must make an expiation (kaffara). [Misri, ʿUmdat al-Salik]

An oath is when you say, “By Allah (WAllahi)…”. A vow is when you make a recommended act of worship (sunna) obligatory on yourself by saying, “for the sake of Allah” or “due to Allah.” Vows are often linked to something happening. For example, “If Allah cures my son, I will fast for twenty days.”

Please note: if you do not mention Allah by His names, it usually cannot count as an oath or a vow. So, the first thing to ask about your second statement is not what it does, but whether it is even an oath or a vow.

A Vow Takes Hold of an Act of Worship, Not of a Legal Determination

In the Shafiʿi school, what a vow takes hold of is an act of worship you undertake yourself, such as fasting, giving charity, or praying.

What you described is not an act, but a legal judgment, deciding that one imam’s evidence is stronger than the other’s. This kind of decision is not something you can perform or control.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey Him, let him not disobey Him.” [Bukhari]

And he said, “There is no fulfilling a vow in disobedience, nor in what the servant does not own.” [Muslim]

The second part of the hadith is most relevant to your question.

It’s plain-sense concerns property that a person does not own, so using it in legal judgments is an analogy rather than a direct ruling. But the main point is the same: a vow only applies to what you can actually give. Deciding which imam has stronger evidence is not something you can give.

An Oath Binds Your Conduct; It Does Not Invalidate Your Acts

Let’s say your second statement was a valid oath. An oath is about obligation, sin, and making up for breaking it. Allah Most High says:

Allah will not take you to task for thoughtlessly uttered oaths, but rather for swearing binding oaths, the expiation for breaking which is to feed ten unfortunates the usual fare you feed your own families, or to clothe them, or to free a slave; So whoever finds no means to do any of these, then to fast three days: That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. [Quran 5:89; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The verse mentions a penalty for breaking an oath, without stating that the oath is invalidated.

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said, “If anyone has taken an oath and then sees that something else is better, let him offer expiation for the oath and do the better thing.” [Muslim]

So even if an oath is binding, you still have another choice.

If you break the oath, you must make up for it, but your action is not invalid. An oath does not affect whether a prayer, marriage, or transaction is valid.

Our school draws this very distinction in its own chapter on following a scholar. Among the conditions is that one not go about collecting the easiest ruling from each school to slip the collar of legal responsibility from his neck.

Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami held that a man who does so is thereby a transgressor; Imam Muhammad al-Ramli held that he is not, though he sins.

Then Sayyid ʿAlawi al-Saqqaf’s own words: this is not a condition for the validity of following a scholar, as the later scholars stated explicitly, but a condition for averting sin, like the prohibition against praying on usurped land. [Saqqaf, Mukhtasar al-Fawaʾid al-Makkiyya, 40–41; ed. Yusuf al-Marʿashli, Dar al-Bashaʾir al-Islamiyya, 1st edn, 1425/2004]

Think about that comparison, because it gives you the answer. A prayer offered on stolen ground is a sin, but it is still a prayer. Sin and validity are two separate things. At most, an oath affects the first, but not the second.

You Were Never Asked to Weigh the Evidence

Begin with the assumption underneath your question. You have taken it that the stronger opinion is the one you owe.

Our school does not say so. Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami records that the well-known position, which Imam Rafiʿi and Imam Nawawi both held to be preponderant, is that it is permitted to follow the less preferred opinion while the more preferred one exists. [Saqqaf, Mukhtasar al-Fawaʾid al-Makkiyya, 43]

So the duty your oath tried to create is not something Sacred Law ever required. This is important because it means your worry has no real basis.

Following the “strongest position” is not really how the schools of thought work. Each of the four recognized schools is considered strongest in its own way of interpreting Sacred Law from the Quran, the Sunna, and other sources.

Even if someone tried to rank the schools by the authenticity of the Prophetic narrations they use, it would require scholarly expertise most people lack, and there would still be differing opinions.

What is asked of you is something else. Allah Most High says, “Ask those who recall if you know not.” [Quran 16:43] By the consensus of scholars, this verse is the evidence that someone who does not know a ruling or its proof follows someone who does. [Buti, al-la Madhhabiyya]

Your commitment would make you responsible for weighing evidence, but Sacred Law never required you to do so. A personal promise cannot create an obligation that the Lawgiver did not make.

Acting on a Relied-Upon Position Remains Sound

Imam Nawawi (Allah have mercy on him) cites Abu al-Fath al-Harawi: “The opinion of the majority of our companions is that a particular legal school does not bind the non-scholar. If they find a mujtahid Imam, they follow them…” [Nawawi, Rawdat al-Talibin wa ʿUmdat al-Muftin]

Our own manuals put it plainly. There is no harm in following someone other than the imam of the school you have committed to on individual matters, so long as that school is recorded and its conditions are known.

It is likewise permitted to follow the scholars who made their own selections within the school, such as Imam Nawawi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Imam Suyuti, because in the issue selected, they are mujtahids.

And moving from one recorded school to another is permitted, even out of mere inclination, provided no contradictory combining of opinions (talfiq) follows from it. [Saqqaf, Mukhtasar al-Fawaʾid al-Makkiyya, 39]

Talfiq is the one real limit, and it is worth knowing where it bites. The combining that vitiates occurs only within one and the same matter.

Al-Bulqini’s example, as Ibn Ziyad transmits it: a man performs his ablution following Imam Abu Hanifa on touching the private parts, and Imam Shafiʿi on bloodletting, and his prayer is void, because both imams agree his purification failed.

Where the two rulings belong to two separate matters, that is not vitiating. [Saqqaf, Mukhtasar al-Fawaʾid al-Makkiyya, 42]

So we advise you not to switch between positions as a habit, and not to combine two opinions in one act as described above. Other than that, you are on firm ground.

One Word Beyond the Ruling

You have written to us with an oath about an oath, a vow about what happens after an oath, and careful limits on the situation. We have seen this before, and it is usually caused by scrupulous doubts (waswasa), not by a real legal problem. Waswasa is not solved by more rulings; it is solved by letting go of the worry.

So let go of this worry. You do not need to decide which imam is stronger. You are not doing anything wrong by following a reliable opinion from your school. Do not repeat the statement, do not test it, and do not look for another ruling about it.

Because of these points, we encourage you to speak with trustworthy local scholars about your specific situation, and to keep the details out of writing.
references: Saqqaf, Mukhtasar al-Fawaʾid al-Makkiyya, 40–41; ed. Yusuf al-Marʿashli, Dar al-Bashaʾir al-Islamiyya, 1st edn, 1425/2004
Nawawi, Rawdat al-Talibin wa ʿUmdat al-Muftin

records.title: Is Conquering Non-Muslim Lands Permissible?
records.question: Is it allowed for a Muslim ruler to conquer a non-Muslim land? Someone heard that a true caliph might do this, and history shows that many lands were taken, including Constantinople, Sicily, Spain, southern France, Egypt, and Persia.
records.answer:
Amin.

No. In the Sacred Law, fighting answers aggression, the breaking of treaties, and the forcible barriers that powers place between people and a free hearing of the message.

It never answers a person’s refusal to believe, and having the means to attack has never been a reason to attack.

Allah Most High prescribes both the cause and its limit: “Fight in the cause of Allah ˹only˺ against those who wage war against you, but do not exceed the limits. Allah does not like transgressors.” [Quran 2:190; Khattab, The Clear Quran]

Your message contains three questions, and each has a different answer. One is about Islamic law, one is about history, and one is about what a hadith can prove.

Regarding the law, classical texts on warfare discuss a legitimate ruler who leads a functioning state, and they set conditions at every stage. Appointing qualified leaders is a communal duty, but their role is to keep order, ensure justice, and protect the religion, not to gain territory.

Even if a ruler has the power, using warfare to establish authority is not required. [Mawardi, al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya wa al-Wilayat al-Diniyya]

Physical struggle must be reviewed by qualified traditional scholars and leaders. This means that no individual, group, or movement today can take on this responsibility alone.

These conditions are important and must be followed.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) told every commander: “Fight, but do not embezzle the spoils, do not break faith, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child. When you meet your enemy among the idolaters, call them to three things; whichever of them they answer you with, accept it from them and hold off from them…” [Muslim]

Before fighting, there is a call, which the schools discuss at length, and fighting must stop as soon as the terms are accepted. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) also said, “O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

He also forbade killing women and children. [Bukhari; Muslim] Treaties must always be honored: “If the enemy is inclined towards peace, make peace with them…” [Quran 8:61]

If someone only looks at the permission to fight and ignores these rules, they misunderstand the law. This is the reading your brother has been handed.

As for history, numerous empires came into being and expanded, one of them being the early Muslim state. Not all the actions of all armies were in accordance with Sacred Law. Being honest about history does not damage the faith.

The greatest error is to confuse what states have done with what the religion teaches. Some of the campaigns were responses to aggression or broken treaties; others were driven by political relations between empires, and some were simply cases of ordinary expansion.

None of these situations justifies attacking people simply because they are not Muslim. The Quran states this clearly: “Let there be no compulsion in religion, for the truth stands out clearly from falsehood.” [Quran 2:256]

It is not true faith to force people to believe, and historians point out that forced conversions were, in fact, very rare.

About the hadith: A narration that predicts the conquest of Constantinople or praises the army that achieves it is describing what will happen and the reward for it. It does not give permission for action.

Prophecy and legal rulings are different things, and no jurist allows something just because it was predicted. It is this misunderstanding, not the reports themselves, that needs to be addressed.

Muslims are not limited to only defending themselves in every situation, but nothing in that permits what you were asked about: no ruler is allowed to attack just because he has the power. Islam aims for truth, peace, and justice for everyone. Any struggle must have these goals to be considered legitimate.
references: Mawardi, al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya wa al-Wilayat al-Diniyya

records.title: Is a Mixed Gym Permissible If I Lower My Gaze?
records.question: Most gyms in my city are mixed. Some people say men should not go because of this.
records.answer:
Before considering the two arguments, it is important to clarify the main point.

A gym is just a place, and legal rulings apply to what people do there, not to the building itself. So, both you and your friends have valid points, and the disagreement becomes clearer when the question is framed properly.

Rulings Attach to Actions, Not to Buildings

Scholars explain that a legal ruling (hukm) is “the communication from the Lawgiver concerning the conduct of the duty-bound person (mukallaf), which consists of a demand, an option, or an enactment.” [Zuhayli, al-Wajiz]

Since a gym is just a place, what matters is what people do there. This is why saying that all gyms are impermissible is inaccurate.

Four Distinct Obligations, of Which the Gaze Is One

There are four main concerns in a mixed gym. First, look at what is not allowed.

Allah says: “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. That is purer for them.” [Quran 24:30]

Second is covering your own nakedness (awra). Wearing tight or short gym clothes that show skin or the shape between the navel and the knee is not allowed for men in public, though many think this rule applies only to women.

Third is avoiding seclusion (khalwa) and unnecessary mingling, including speaking softly or in a flirtatious way with women you could marry.

Fourth is the music. Scholars differ about music in general, but there is broad agreement that many modern forms are not allowed, and those are exactly the forms most gyms play.

Why the Gaze Argument Is Incomplete Rather Than Wrong

Lowering the gaze is required everywhere, whether on the street or at work. This is the basic expectation for a Muslim, not a special permission to enter any place.

It only addresses the first concern. It does not cover how you dress, what happens in changing rooms, saunas, or showers where men may expose themselves to each other, or the issue of music.

If the environment makes it too hard to lower your gaze for the entire session, then the setting itself becomes a problem, because Sacred Law also blocks the paths leading to what is forbidden.

If you can truly manage all four concerns, and your friends might be talking about a gym where this is possible, then there is no reason to say attending is not allowed.

The University Comparison Does Not Establish a Double Standard

The rules for a lecture hall are the same as for a gym: lower your gaze, cover your nakedness, avoid seclusion and unnecessary mingling, and avoid listening to what is not allowed. Neither place is always allowed or always forbidden.

The difference is in how much hardship a person is expected to bear. Education is a real need in a way that fitness is not, since you can exercise at home, outside, or in a men-only gym, but you cannot easily get a degree elsewhere.

So, a Muslim might have to put up with some difficulty in a classroom that he does not have to face in a gym. This is about what is tolerated, not about having two different standards.

Principle and Practical Guidance

Try to find a men-only gym or class first. If that is not possible, go during the quietest times to avoid seeing things you should not. Make sure your clothing covers the area between your navel and knees, both in shape and skin.

If you can, ask for the music to be turned down, or use noise-canceling headphones and listen to something good. If none of these options work, training at home or outdoors is a good alternative.

Allah says: “And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them, and provide for them from sources they could never imagine.” [Quran 65:2]

Stay true to your faith, but do not judge others harshly for having a gym membership.

For a fuller treatment, see The Strong Believer, Article Four: Muslim Gym-Etiquettes, and Is It Impermissible to Go to a Mixed Gym?.

records.title: What Happens If Ghusl After Menstruation Was Too Early?
records.question: I bled on days one to three, was dry on day three, saw blood on days four and five, then took my ghusl, believing my period had ended, and prayed for the following week.
records.answer:
You acted on what you understood at the time, and you have since sought the correct knowledge. That is exactly what is asked of a believer. No make-up prayers are due from you. Your prayers that week stand as valid.

How Purity Is Recognized

Menstruation comes to an end when the bleeding ceases, as indicated by the appearance of white discharge (al-qassa al-bayda), clear discharge, or by being entirely dry when you check.

According to the Shafii school, menstrual blood may be black, red, brown, yellow, or dusky, but not clear or white. [Bafadl, al-Nabras fi Ahkam al-Hayd wa al-Istihada wa al-Nifas]

This settles your query regarding the timing as well: purity begins the moment the bleeding ceases, not on a particular day, and you will know that moment by the sign rather than by the calendar.

Guidance concerning the fifth or sixth day is part of a family tradition and not a legal rule, so you can disregard it in the future.

Your Clear Discharge and Your Brownish Discharge

The kind of discharge that you observed earlier on the fifth day is an indication of purity, since clear discharge is not one of the colors associated with menstruation. The white or creamy discharge, which has a slight brownish tinge later that same evening, is the more difficult case.

According to the relied-upon (mu’tamad) position in the school of thought, brown discharge is considered to be menstrual blood as long as you are within the fifteen-day limit, and therefore, one must wait until the discharge is white or clear before carrying out the ghusl. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin]

There is an alternative position that can be followed in the case of yellow discharge, but the description you have given refers only to a tint and not to a yellow color, so do not rely on that position here.

Why Your Prayers Stand

You are not sure that your ghusl was performed early; all you have is a concern that appeared a week later, not a memory of blood following bathing.

According to a well-established principle of Sacred Law, certainty is not removed by doubt (al-yaqin la yazul bi-l-shakk). [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir]

Since you were in a state which you had every reason to regard as one of purity, a later hesitation does not nullify worship which has already been carried out.

Add to this that if your ghusl came after that last tinted discharge, it was valid outright, and there is nothing further to weigh. Either way, no make-up prayers are due.

What Sincere Belief Does and Does Not Do

Sincere belief alone does not make someone pure, because proper purification is required for prayer. If someone prayed while certain they were in a state of major ritual impurity, they would need to repeat the prayer. That is not your case.

Yours is a doubt that came up later, and doubt does not undo what certainty has established.

Principle and Practical Guidance

From now on, you should perform your ghusl whenever you see clear or white discharge, or when you are completely dry when you check, rather than on a set day; just leave the situation of the past week as it is.

Trying to carry out a reconstruction that is impossible will only result in misgivings (waswasa), not in accuracy, and the Sacred Law does not require that of you.

For related guidance, see When Should I Ghusl After Menstruation?, Does a Creamy Colour Count as White Discharge after One’s Period?, and Is Brown Spotting Menstruation or Istihada in the Shafi’i School?.
references: Bafadl, al-Nabras fi Ahkam al-Hayd wa al-Istihada wa al-Nifas

records.title: Is an Interest-Free Student Loan Permissible for a Bursary?
records.question: My university requires students to take out a government student loan to be eligible for a bursary.
records.answer:
Yes, this is permissible. The loan carries no interest, the debt you take on is genuine, and you are not misrepresenting anything to the university.

The Loan Is Lawful

A loan free of any increase over the principal is a lawful transaction, and lending in that form is among the most praised of dealings in Islam.

The general principle governing transactions is that things are permissible until something establishes otherwise (al-asl fi al-ashya’ al-ibaha). [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir]

Since the government’s loan carries no interest, no fee, and no penalty for early settlement, there is nothing in the contract itself to object to.

Your Purpose Does Not Corrupt a Lawful Contract

You genuinely enter the loan, you genuinely become liable for the debt, and then you genuinely repay it. It is not a sham arrangement dressed up as a loan.

Once the money is lent, it is yours as the borrower, and holding it and returning it are your rights, just as spending it would be. Taking a lawful contract for a lawful purpose you have chosen can’t make it unlawful.

Where Deception Would Enter

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever deceives us is not of us.” [Muslim]

Deception here means stating something untrue on an application, overstating your need, or concealing something you were asked to disclose. None of that exists here.

The government assesses your financial position accurately, and then the university tells you it does not mind whether you spend the money or return it. You are satisfying a stated procedural requirement, openly and honestly.

Principle and Practical Guidance

Always be honest on both applications and share anything they ask about. Carefully read the terms of the loan and bursary and follow them. If either says the money must be used for study or limits early closure, you must respect that.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Muslims are bound by their conditions.” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi]

Keep the money safe until you close the loan, and do not invest it, because you have promised to return it. Once your bursary is processed, close the loan and pay back the debt as soon as possible.

records.title: Who Is Responsible for a Child’s Care?
records.question: Why are parents and siblings held more directly responsible for a child’s daily well-being than relatives, friends, coworkers, or teachers?
records.answer:
Sacred law assigns responsibility to those with authority, close family ties, and proximity, which is why parents are responsible first.

Others are encouraged to help as much as they can. The law only limits their authority, not the good they can do.

Where the Obligation Sits and Why

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.

The ruler is a shepherd and is responsible for his subjects. A man is a shepherd over his family and is responsible for them. A woman is a shepherd over her husband’s house and is responsible for it.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

Responsibility comes with the authority a person has been given.

Allah says: “O believers! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones.” [Quran 66:6]

The father is therefore responsible for the child’s support (nafaqa), and guardianship (wilaya) goes to him, then the paternal grandfather. This includes the child’s education, medical care, and property in general. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin]

These are legal duties which enforceable by the court. Siblings at home have a general duty to encourage good behavior and are often the first to notice problems.

Sharing a roof gives them real duty without giving them legal authority, so their share is moral rather than assigned by a court.

There Is No Ceiling on How Much Others May Help

Islam encourages every degree of care from anyone able to give it. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Allah is in the aid of His servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.” [Muslim]

A teacher who notices a child is not eating, a neighbor who feeds him, an aunt who tutors him, a coworker who advocates for him with the school, all of these are doing something beloved to Allah, and doing more of it is better.

Islam places no cap on generosity, and the guardian who welcomes such help is acting wisely.

What Is Limited Is Authority, Not Care

The decisions that belong to the guardian stay with the guardian. Schooling, medical treatment, travel, the child’s money, and later the child’s marriage are his to decide.

Someone outside the family may raise a concern, offer help, and support the child at length, and should do so through the parents rather than around them.

Setting oneself up as a replacement for a present and functioning parent, or forming a relationship with the child that the parents are not party to, is where good intentions turn into something else.

The ordinary rules of interaction apply here too, including avoiding seclusion (khalwa) with a child who is approaching or past puberty and is not one’s unmarriageable kin.

Principle and Practical Guidance

If you are the relative, teacher, or friend in this picture, give as much as you can and route it through the parents. Tell them what you have seen, offer specifically rather than generally, and keep them informed of anything you do.

Where the parents themselves are the difficulty, raise it with extended family, then with those who have standing, such as an imam or the school, and where a child is genuinely at risk of harm, with the authorities responsible for that.

Stepping in to protect a child from harm is a duty on whoever is able, and it does not require a title.

records.title: Is Loving and Imagining Fictional Characters Sinful?
records.question: I eased a lonely youth by imagining friendship with fictional characters, among them two cartoon robots who love each other, and I hope to meet them in Paradise.
records.answer:
There is nothing ridiculous about this. You are not sinning. Imagining kindness between two cartoon robots is not a sin, and the eleven months of thoughts telling you otherwise are misgivings (waswasa). You should ignore them.

You Are Not Held to Account for What Passes Through Your Mind

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Allah has pardoned my community for what occurs within themselves, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it.” [Bukhari; Muslim] This covers deliberate imagining as much as passing thought.

What Allah holds a person to is action, and the action you describe is finding comfort in a story.

Nothing You Have Described Is Unlawful

The characters are not real people, so there is no unlawful looking or no unlawful relationship.

You describe kind gestures, hand-holding, and companionship between two fictional robots, and you say plainly that you have never felt anything deviant in it.

Affection for a fictional character is not sinful in itself, and the strength of the affection does not change that.

Paradise Is Beyond Our Minds

Allah says of Paradise: “There will be whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you will be there forever.” [Quran 43:71]

No one can tell you that Allah will never do something that lies within His power, so set that thought aside as the false certainty it is.

What is true is that the realities of Paradise share only their names with what we know here, and that what Allah gives you there will satisfy you more than anything you can imagine. Leave the specifics with Allah and always keep a good expectation of Him.

What This Is

The mark of misgivings (waswasa) is exactly what you have described: you keep asking, you receive an answer, and it does not help. That is not a sign the answer was wrong, but rather the nature of the affliction.

The way of the scholars is to refuse to argue with misgivings and to turn the attention elsewhere.

Principle and Practical Guidance

Treat this answer as the last word on the question and stop searching for another. When the thought arrives, say “I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil” and move to something else without examining it, however unfinished that feels.

Give some of the warmth you have for these characters to people as well, starting with one person and something small, because ten years of this friendship shows you have a real capacity for loyalty, and it deserves somewhere to land.

And if the hopelessness you mention is weighing on you beyond this question, please speak to a doctor or counselor about it; there is no shame in that, and it is not a matter of weak faith.

Allah sees the loneliness that sent you to those stories in the first place, and He is nearer to you than the thoughts that have been troubling you.

For related guidance, see Is It Wrong to Feel Deeply Attached to a Fictional Character? and Can Desires For Fictional Figures Be Fulfilled In Paradise?.

records.title: Is It Haram to Make Non-Islamic Content as a Muslim YouTuber?
records.question: I want to start a YouTube channel on gaming, technology, and entertainment, with nothing in it that promotes alcohol, gambling, or immodesty, and I want a plain answer: is it unlawful for me to make content that is not Islamic, and is the income from it lawful?
records.answer:
Making content that is not religious in subject matter is lawful, and so is the income from it. Nothing is forbidden merely for not being Islamic. You are not standing at the edge of a sin.

Your question assumes that content must earn its legitimacy by being Islamic. The jurists work the other way round in worldly matters, where the default is permissibility (ibaha) [al-Mawsua al-Fiqhiyya al-Kuwaytiyya 12:192].

The Quran places the burden on whoever forbids something [Quran 7:32]. So ask only whether anything in your channel is forbidden. By your own description, nothing is.

Your income follows the same rule: a reward for lawful work is permitted, “whether religious or worldly.” [al-Mawsua al-Fiqhiyya al-Kuwaytiyya 15:77]

Ibn Abidin (Allah have mercy on him) seems to pull the other way: “unqualified amusement is proscribed except in three cases.” [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar 6:462] Read flatly, that would shut a gaming channel down.

It does not. Those three cases describe a man diverting himself; you are asking about a trade. Filming for an audience, for a fee, is work, and work is judged by the rules of hiring and earning. And the word Ibn Abidin uses is the Prophet’s own.

At a wedding among the Helpers the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) asked, “Was there no amusement with you? The Helpers are delighted by amusement.” [Mishkat al-Masabih 2:940]

Where Do You stand as a Hanafi

Here are the two things that could actually stop you. Keep instrumental music out of your videos; the game’s own sound and your voice do the job. Images on a screen are not the carved-and-hung images the prohibition was about, so film can be filmed.

What is left is what goes into the channel: on-screen immodesty, gambling mechanics in a game, the sponsors you take on, and the hours it eats up. Keep promotion apart from production.

Playing a game yourself is one thing; urging an audience to buy a game whose content is forbidden is helping others to sin.

Ibn Nujaym (Allah have mercy on him) states it: “what is unlawful to do is unlawful to ask for,” and “what is unlawful to take is unlawful to give.” [Ibn Nujaym, al-Ashbah wa al-Nazair 1:132]

What a Muslim may not do himself, he may not help others to do.

You asked for the majority position rather than one school’s, and there is nothing to choose between them here. Staying with one school will still serve you better than gathering rulings one by one.

Before You Publish

Nothing forbids you from having a technology and gaming channel. Take your first video through that list, and check again when sponsors start writing to you.

Keep the forbidden out of an ordinary trade, and what you earn is the lawful, wholesome earning Allah calls His servants to. There is nothing less about it. Write back with what your channel actually shows, and we can be more specific.

records.title: What is the Ruling of Spotting After Taking Period Delaying Pills?
records.question: My usual period lasts 6 days. My last period started on May 5 and lasted 6 days. I took period-delay pills from May 26 to June 10.
records.answer:
Allah Most High accepts your Hajj and makes it a means of continuous guidance and blessings in life.

The bleeding was caused by the pills, not menstruation, so the spotting and little blood are irregular bleeding due to the pills. All your Hajj rites and worship are valid. Bleeding from June 11-16 will be considered your menses since it occurred during your period.

Ruling of Irregular Bleeding

During irregular bleeding (istihada), one prays, fasts during Ramadan, recites and touches the Quran, enters a mosque, performs Tawaf with wudu, and may have intimacy with her husband. [Birgivi, Dhukhr al-Muta’ahhilin]

Menstruation is Blood From Uterus Within Time of Menses

Withdrawal bleeding is considered menses if it falls within the time of menstruation. Doctors generally say that withdrawal bleeding is not menstruation, but what they mean is that it is not the natural blood that occurs due to ovulation.

However, the legal definition of menstruation is not dependent upon ovulation. Rather, menstruation is blood that originates from the uterus. (Ibn’ Abidin, Manhal al-Waridin)

Advice

Every woman must record her menses, lochia, and purity habits. The date and time any vaginal blood begins, including the spotting of blood, and the date and time any vaginal blood ends.

I advise contacting a local, reliable female scholar who is well-versed in matters of menstruation. Also, try to attend any on-the-ground and online courses on menstruation.

Also, at your earliest convenience, buy books related to the topic; some are linked below.

It is a personal obligation (fard) for every adult woman to learn the basic rules of menstruation and to ask, as you’ve done, in the case of a complicated or unique situation.

The book A Woman’s Guide to Menstruation Rulings by Naielah Ackbarali is a good book for learning these rulings. It is in English and includes many practical examples, real-life experiences, and even charts to calculate menstruation.

Also, you can download the first-ever menstruation-tracking app, personalized for Muslim women, to understand menses, purity, irregular bleeding, lochia, and more at first glance.

The application is in harmony with religious scholarship.

records.title: Does the 99-to-1 Hadith Mean I Have Only a 1% Chance of Paradise?
records.question: I read in al-Bukhari that ninety-nine out of every hundred people go to the Fire, and it has left me sick with despair: if I never miss a prayer and try to do as much good as I can, do I really have only a one percent chance of Paradise?
records.answer:
No, the hadith you mentioned does not give you a one percent chance of Paradise. The hundred in it is not a hundred Muslims.

It is the whole of Adam’s children, first to last, and the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said so in the same sitting to men asking what you are asking. They said, “Messenger of Allah, if ninety-nine out of every hundred of us are taken, what is left of us?”

He answered, “My community among the nations is like a white hair on a black bull.” [Sahih al-Bukhari] The ninety-nine are drawn from all humanity across every age. This community is the white hair, not the black bull.

The Harder Report and the Answer He Gave to It

There is a second report, agreed upon, with a heavier ratio still, and you should hear it from me rather than come upon it alone.

In it, Allah Most High tells Adam (upon him be peace) to send forth the contingent of the Fire, “out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine…” The Companions (Allah be pleased with them) asked, “Messenger of Allah, which of us is that one?” He answered, “Rejoice, for from you there is one man…” [Sahih al-Bukhari]

Mulla Ali al-Qari (Allah have mercy on him), relaying Imam Tibi (Allah have mercy on him), reads their question as an alarm rather than a request for a name, and an alarm “…calls to be answered with what removes that fear, out of gentleness to the people; and the second is what is meant, because of his saying: Rejoice…” [Mulla Ali al-Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih 8:3518: 1]

Then Mulla Ali al-Qari clarifies: “And the meaning is: there will be found, for the number of every man among you, a thousand of Gog and Magog, so at that point the people of Paradise become many.

And in it is an indication that the people of the Fire are more numerous than the people of Paradise, and perhaps the people of Paradise become many through the presence of the angels brought near and the wide-eyed houris.

So the meaning of the divine saying holds true: My mercy has overcome My wrath.” [Mulla Ali al-Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih 8:3518: 2] He is weighing nations against each other across the whole of time, and even there he ends on the mercy that overcomes.

The Other Ninety-Nine Is Mercy, Kept Back for That Day

A second “ninety-nine” runs through the hadith literature, and it is the one to hold on to. “Allah has a hundred mercies,” the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) tells us.

And he explains: “He sent down one mercy among the jinn, mankind, beasts, and crawling creatures; through it they show one another affection and mercy, and through it the wild animal is tender toward its young. And Allah held back ninety-nine mercies, by which He will show mercy to His servants on the Day of Resurrection.” [Sahih Muslim ]

Every kindness you have ever been shown stems from the one that was sent down. The other ninety-nine have not been spent, and they are aimed at precisely the day you are dreading.

Imam Turbashti (Allah have mercy on him) warns against reading the number as a measurement at all: “The mercy of Allah Most High is not finite…” [Turbashti, al-Muyassar fi Sharh Masabih al-Sunna] A hundred is how the disparity was made teachable, not how much there is. Neither ninety-nine nor one is a probability; both are teaching instruments, carrying opposite ends of one truth.

In short, Allah is both Just and Wise–and All-Merciful.

Just, Merciful, Wise: What the Three Meanings of Him

Your question is about three of His attributes at once, so take them as our own theologians do. Imam al-Maturidi (Allah have mercy on him), one of the great imams of theology, gives a chapter of his Kitab al-Tawhid to the question underneath yours: why did Allah create creation at all?

He begins by closing the only two ways an act can fall short of wisdom: “…His actions do not admit of departing from wisdom, since an act departs from it either through ignorance of it or on account of a benefit one fears to lose were one to keep to the path of wisdom.

So when Allah, glorified is He, is knowing and does not fail to know, rich and untouched by any need whose removal would profit Him, it is void that His act should depart from the side of wisdom.” [Maturidi, Kitab al-Tawhid] Ignorance and need are the only two engines of a foolish act, and He has neither.

Then Imam Maturidi says what the “wisdom” means: “And the interpretation of wisdom is hitting the mark, which is putting each thing in its place, and that is the meaning of justice, and His act does not depart from it.” [Maturidi, Kitab al-Tawhid]

Justice is not a rival to wisdom here. Rather, justice is what wisdom looks like once you can see the whole picture.

And “mercy” is not at odds with wisdom either, because Imam Maturidi divides wisdom in two and gives the wider road away: “Then within wisdom there are two roads: one of them justice, and the second bounty; and there is no end to the bounties Allah is able to bestow.” [Maturidi, Kitab al-Tawhid]

This is the background through which we understand the hadith you mentioned:

One. In terms of justice, a wrong has a ceiling:

مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا ۖ وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

“Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten the like of it; And whoever brings an ill deed shall be requited but with its like, and they shall not be wronged.” [Quran 6:160; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

One sin counts once; one good deed counts tenfold and upward, which is why the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) could ask, “Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds each day?” and then set the price at a hundred glorifications. [Muslim]

Two. In terms of Diving Mercy, keep in mind the ninety-nine withheld mercies. Nothing obliged Allah Most High to keep them for the Day of Judgment, which is exactly what makes them bounty and not wages.

وَرَحْمَتِى وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَىْءٍۢ

“…While My mercy encompasses everything…” [Quran 7:156]

Imam Baghawi (Allah have mercy on him) explains this: “Al-Hasan and Qatada said: His mercy in this world encompassed the righteous and the corrupt, and on the Day of Resurrection it is for the godfearing in particular.” [Baghawi, Maalim al-Tanzil]

You are asking about the Day of Resurrection, which is where the withheld mercy is headed, and God-fearing (taqwa) is the quality you are already working to uphold.

Why the Question “Why?” Isn’t Ultimately Asked of Allah Most High

That leaves wisdom, the attribute you need to see in perspective. Here, Imam Maturidi says something bracing: the question is not merely hard; it is malformed. “…that the question about a cause is impossible, because it is impossible that anyone should hold authority over Him, or that His act should depart from wisdom, so that we might question Him about it.” [Maturidi, Kitab al-Tawhid]
references: Turbashti, al-Muyassar fi Sharh Masabih al-Sunna

records.title: Is a Marriage Contract Valid When Conducted Over a Video Call?
records.question: Is a marriage contract (nikah) valid when the bride, groom, and witnesses are all participating on the same video call?
records.answer:
From the details you are giving, if you, your wife, and the witnesses were all on the same video call together, yes, the marriage contract is valid. All parties present, all parties hearing the offer and acceptance, that fulfill the conditions. Please consult the detailed answer at the link below for the full explanation.

If people around you are still not satisfied, or if they are giving you a hard time about it, there is no harm in going through another basic marriage ceremony. Gather your wife, yourself, and two witnesses—ideally including a local scholar—and contract the marriage again in person. That would be the end of it.

This is not technically required. Your marriage was valid from the first time. But if it will silence their concerns, then it may be the way to go. You do not have to worry. The contract was sound: the witnesses heard the offer and acceptance, which fulfilled the conditions for a valid marriage. The scholars confirm that when all parties can see and hear one another in real time, the requirement of presence is met, even though they are not physically together. [Maydani, al-Lubab]

Keep your heart at ease. You have done what is lawful.

records.title: Does a Woman Have to Keep Waiting If a Man Keeps Postponing the Nikah Again and Again?
records.question: For a year, a man has told me he wants to marry me, but he has set and canceled the nikah more than six times without any explanation. Now he says he will marry me tomorrow if I can show him proof from the Quran or Sunna that a woman does not have to wait. What is the ruling?
records.answer:
A proposal is not a marriage and does not give anyone marital rights. You are free to end this at any time, and you do not have to wait, give notice, or explain your decision.

The Proof Is Owed by Him, Not by You

He is asking you to prove that a woman does not have to wait, but actually, it should be the other way around. In Sacred Law, no one is required to do something unless there is clear evidence for it. [Suyuti, al-Ashbah wa al-Naza’ir,:] There is nothing in the Quran or Sunna that says a woman must wait for a man who has not married her. The person who says you are obligated must prove it, but he cannot, because you are not.

Proposal is Not a Contract

Until the marriage contract is done, he is still considered a stranger (ajnabi) to you. Scholars say a proposal (khitba) is just a promise, and either person can change their mind, though leaving without a good reason is blameworthy. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin,:; Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj,:] He has already changed his mind six times.

Sunna to Hasten Marriage

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “O youth, whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry.” [Bukhari; Muslim] When both people are ready, and a good match is found, the Sunna is to complete the marriage contract, not to delay it for a long time. Allah Most High says: “O believers! Why do you say what you do not do? How despicable it is in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do!” [Quran, 61:2–3]

Another important rule in Sacred Law is to remove harm. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “[Let there be] no harm or reciprocation of harm.” [Ibn Maja; Malik] Setting dates and then canceling them at the last minute for a whole year, especially after you have asked for clarity, is clearly harmful.

Principle and Practical Guidance

Ask your guardian (wali) to set one date for the marriage. If that date passes and there is still no marriage contract, consider it finished and trust that Allah will bring you something better, in sha’ Allah.

There are two more things to think about. Spending a year in a close relationship with a man who is not your husband should end now, no matter what he decides. Ending it now will make things easier for you. Also, if he already has a wife and children, he has responsibilities to them. Before marrying someone in this situation, make sure he can be fair and honest with everyone. A man who will not explain why he cancels dates has not shown you these qualities.

records.title: Does Reciting a Supplication While Moving Between Prayer Positions Invalidate the Prayer?
records.question: If one is praying the night prayer (Isha) behind an imam, and during the imam’s second prostration, one recites the supplication “My Lord, forgive me” (rabbighfirli), uttering the last few letters while moving between positions, does this count as speech that invalidates the prayer, or is it a mistake carried by the imam?
records.answer:
No, your prayer was not invalidated by these words. It is a supplication and, therefore, permissible within the prayer, even though it was done during a movement. [Shurunbulali, Maraqi al-Falah]

I highly recommend that you study the rulings of purification and prayer. This knowledge greatly enhances one’s understanding of how to worship Allah and is empowering.

Allah bless you with the best of both worlds.

records.title: Do My Oaths and Vows Bind Me to the Hanafi Position?
records.question: I made oaths saying, “By Allah, if I marry while this house exists, I will become a kafir” and “I make a vow for Allah that in this matter I am Hanafi.” Can oaths and vows bind me to the Hanafi position and prevent me from following the Shafi’i opinion? Are they even validly concluded? How do I get free from them?
records.answer:
A vow only counts when you promise to do an act of worship, like fasting, giving charity, or praying. Saying you will be Hanafi in a matter is not an act of worship, but a legal choice. These vows were never valid in the first place. You do not need to do anything to be released from them.

The Oaths Do Not Bind You to a School or Invalidate Your Actions

Oaths made out of baseless doubts are not binding, and you are not held to them. Even if you had made a valid oath, the most you would need to do is offer the expiation for a broken oath. No oath can force you to follow a particular school, and it cannot make your worship or marriage invalid if you act on a sound opinion. Your prayers and your marriage, whenever they happen, are valid.

The Wording About Disbelief

Speaking words like these is sinful, and you should avoid them in the future. They did not make you a disbeliever, and there are no lasting consequences. Turn to Allah in repentance, say “There is no god but Allah” with a heart full of love, and move on. This matter is closed.

This Matter Is Now Closed

You have asked, and you have your answer. Changing the words will not change the ruling. Asking about more versions only feeds the doubts that trouble you. Do not repeat these statements or test yourself with them. If you find these thoughts keep coming back, it may help to speak with a mental health professional who understands OCD. Allah is Merciful, and He has made your religion easy.

records.title: Is It Permissible to Delay a Prayer to Later in Its Time?
records.question: In certain countries, the days are very short. Is it permissible to delay a prayer, other than praying it at the very beginning of its time, as long as it is still prayed within its time? For example, Isha enters at 6 pm, but due to work or training, a person prays it at 10 pm.
records.answer:
Yes, you may pray at any point within the prayer’s time. The only requirement is that each prayer is performed before its time ends. Whether you pray at the start or closer to the end, your prayer counts and you have fulfilled what is due.

Allah Most High says: “Indeed, performing prayers is a duty on the believers at the appointed times.” [Quran 4:103]

The angel Jibril (peace be upon him) led the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) in prayer on two successive days. On the first day, Jibril prayed with him at the beginning of each prayer time. On the second day, he prayed with him near the end of each prayer time. Jibril then concluded: “The time is between these two.” [Tirmidhi]

It is better to pray at the start of the time, and there is an extra reward in doing so. Take that opportunity when you can, but know that praying later is still accepted.

There are two things to watch for. Do not wait so long that you risk missing the prayer time. Keep your intention firm to pray before time runs out. Needing to work or train is a real reason to use the later part of the time. Pray your Isha at 10 pm with peace of mind.

records.title: How Do I Cope With Intense Emotions in Borderline Personality Disorder?
records.question: I have borderline personality disorder and struggle with self-harm urges, despite doing regular prayers, reading the Quran, and dhikr. Is my iman weak? Am I a bad Muslim?
records.answer:
My dear sister, Allah bless you and give you ease and well-being.

No, I don’t think your iman is weak at all. For you to regularly perform acts of worship and turn to Allah for help is not a sign of weak iman. It’s a sign that you have a healthy relationship with Allah.

If you fall short or make mistakes, Allah has given you the door of repentance. Each time you return to Him sincerely, you draw closer, not further away.

You are facing a test. Every test a believer faces carries good in it. Allah shapes each moment for your benefit, even when it is hard to see.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “I am amazed at the affair of the believer. Everything Allah has decreed for him is what is best for him.” [Ahmad]

Remember this hadith. Allah wants to give you a high place in Paradise. Many of the greatest rewards go to those who reach them through patience with hardship, not only through acts of worship.

Keep seeking professional help for your condition. Worship brings calm and steadiness in hard times, but Allah also calls us to use the means He has given for healing. Reach out to a doctor or therapist, and ask Allah for ease and well-being.

records.title: What Is the Ruling on Emojis and Photographs?
records.question: How do rulings on images of animate beings apply to AI-generated images, photographs, emojis, and everyday items like keychains, stickers, and clothing? Is there a distinction between items where images are primary versus items where images are incidental, such as textbooks or packaging?
records.answer:
The impermissibility of images centers on drawing or making them, especially by hand. The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Every image maker will be in the Hellfire.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

This refers to detailed images of living beings. It also applies to images intended to honor and revere someone, such as portraits. However, drawing other living things—such as plant life—is permissible. Drawing things without detailed features, such as silhouettes or stick figures, is also permissible. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Drawing images to facilitate education and learning is permissible when necessary. Such images in children’s educational materials are an effective teaching tool. Moreover, there is no honor involved in images given to children who may bite, tear, or throw them on the ground.

Using images such as emojis or a cat image is permissible. However, if images show a person’s body parts that must remain covered, displaying such images is sinful.

Praying with a detailed image in one’s presence is disliked to varying degrees depending on its positioning. An exception applies if the image is not in an honored position—for example, a tiger on a rug where you stand while praying. There is no honor in this situation. [Shurunbulali, Maraqi al-Falah]

records.title: How Do I Shorten Prayers When I Own Two Homes?
records.question: My parents own a second house over 50 miles from my primary home. We visit for two days every couple of weeks. This house is more of a vacation home since our obligations (school, work) are at the primary home, and it isn’t maintained as a permanent residence. My parents may retire there eventually, but for now, we don’t actively live there. Should I shorten prayers while at this second house, or pray in full?
records.answer:
Scholars differ on the distance required to be considered a traveler. Some state it is closer to 48 miles, while others say around 57 miles. [al-Fatawa al-Ridawiyya] This is close to what some scholars of Damascus say as well.

Because these distances are estimates, there is some room for ease. If your family’s other house is within this range, you pray in full. If it is farther, you still pray in full. This is because a second home owned by your parents counts as a place you can call home. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Allah bless you with the best of both worlds.

records.title: Should a Non-Muslim Wife Perform Ghusl After the End of Menstruation?
records.question: Does a non-Muslim wife need to perform ghusl (ritual bathing) after menstruation ends before resuming intercourse?
records.answer:
A non-Muslim wife does not need to perform a ritual bath after her period ends. This is because the rules of ritual purity apply to Muslims. You may encourage your wife to take a regular bath for cleanliness before resuming intimacy. This is a matter of care and respect, not a religious requirement for her.

Allah Most High says: “Do not approach them until they are pure; and when they have purified themselves, then approach them as Allah has commanded you.” [Quran 2:222]

Scholars have discussed whether non-Muslims are responsible for the details of Islamic law. All agree that the main responsibility for a non-Muslim is to find their way to faith. The details of ritual purity do not apply until someone accepts Islam.

May Allah Most High open her heart to faith and guide your family to what is best.

records.title: If Devils Are Chained in Ramadan, How Could Shaytan Be at Badr?
records.question: If the devils are chained in Ramadan, how could Shaytan be present at the Battle of Badr, which was fought in Ramadan?
records.answer:
Thank you for a careful question. Wanting to understand, not just explain away, is a sign of faith. There is no contradiction here.

Scholars never understood the chaining of the devils in Ramadan as a total lockdown. The Quran itself shows Shaytan at Badr, but only to show his defeat when Allah’s help arrives. Let us look at what the hadith means and what happened at Badr.

The Chaining Is a General Grace, Not an Absolute Lockdown

The hadith reads: “When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.” [Bukhari; Muslim]

Read alongside its sister narrations, the meaning becomes clearer. Several wordings restrict the chaining to the worst devils: “the devils and the rebellious jinn (marada al-jinn) are chained.” [Tirmidhi; Ibn Maja; Ibn Khuzayma] Imam al-Nasai has said: “The rebellious devils are shackled.” The reports never claimed that every devil, without exception, is bound.

The commentators drew the distinction you are reaching for—between “generally” and “absolutely.” Qadi Iyad writes that the chaining may be “from some things and not others, from some devils and not others, or in the dominant case.” [Qadi Iyad, Ikmal al-Mu’lim, 4:4–5] Imam Nawawi says the same: they are chained “from some things and not others, for some people and not others.” [Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim, 7:187] A general statement in Islamic law can hold true while admitting particulars and exceptions. This is how scholars constantly read Revelation.

This is also why sin does not disappear in Ramadan. Imam al-Qurtubi explains that even if all the devils were chained, evil would still happen. There are other causes: the self (nafs), bad habits, and even other people. [Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari, 4:114; Ayni, Umdat al-Qari, 10:268] Ramadan gives the believer an advantage, but the struggle remains. Imam Ayni points out that what we see is a clear drop in evil during the month. [Ayni, Umdat al-Qari, 10:268]

Iblis Himself May Stand Apart, Reprieved Until the Last Day

There is a further key bearing directly on Badr. Some scholars hold that Iblis—the chief of the devils—is not included in the chaining at all.

Mulla Ali al-Qari writes: “It is said that the leader of their host is excepted from the general ‘the devils are chained,’ because of the reprieve he sought from Allah and was granted—so what occurs of disobedience occurs through his tempting.” [Mulla Ali al-Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih, 4:391] Iblis alone was granted respite “until the Day of the appointed time.” [Quran 15:36–38] The one reprieved until the Last Day is not obviously among the bound.

Scholars differed on this point. Imam Ayni held that since the rebellious devils are chained, Iblis, as their leader, is also restrained. [Ayni, Umdat al-Qari, 7:191] Either view removes the problem. If Iblis is not chained, his presence at Badr is not an exception. If he is chained, his actions at Badr only show his weakness, just as the hadith describes.

Badr Displays the Devil’s Defeat, Not His Strength

Badr was fought on the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year of the Hijra—the first Ramadan in which the believers fasted. Allah named that day the Day of Distinction (Yawm al-Furqan), the day He parted truth from falsehood. [Quran 8:41] Imam Ibn Ashur explains that Badr earned this name because it was the first day weak believers overcame mighty idolaters—proof of who stood with truth. [Ibn Ashur, al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir]

Into this came the Devil. Quranic commentators relate that Iblis appeared to the Quraysh in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik, with a banner and a host of devils, whispering: “No one can overcome you today. I am surely by your side.” [Quran 8:48; Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-‘Azim,:; Qurtubi, al-Jami’ li-Ahkam al-Quran]

Then the angels descended. Allah had promised to reinforce the believers with a thousand angels. [Quran 8:9] The same verse tells what became of the Devil: “But when the two forces faced off, he cowered and said, ‘I have absolutely nothing to do with you. I certainly see what you do not see. I truly fear Allah.'” [Quran 8:48]

That is the whole point. The Devil’s role at Badr was to promise and then to flee. Imam Qatada put it forcefully: “That is the enemy of Allah’s habit with everyone who obeys him—until, when truth and falsehood meet, he abandons them in the worst way and disowns them.” [Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-‘Azim]

Badr does not go against the mercy of Ramadan. It shows it in action. The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said that Shaytan was never seen more humiliated or angrier than on the Day of Arafa, except for what he saw on the Day of Badr, when he saw the angels come down. [Malik, al-Muwatta] Both the month of mercy and the day of victory bring him low.

What the Devil Can Do, and What He Cannot

Beneath your question sits the deepest point, a matter of creed. The Devil’s entire power is invitation; he holds no power of compulsion. On the Day of Judgment, he will tell his followers, “I did not have any authority over you. I only called you, and you answered. So do not blame me; blame yourselves.” [Quran 14:22]

Imam al-Razi states plainly that the Devil cannot compel a person or strip him of his choice, with this very verse as his proof. [Razi, Mafatih al-Ghayb] “The schemes of Shaytan are ever weak.” [Quran 4:76]

This matches the creed of the Ash’aris and Maturidis. Everything happens by Allah’s will and wisdom: the chaining, the whispering, the angels coming down, and Iblis running away. Allah binds whom He wills and gives respite to whom He wills. He lets truth and falsehood meet so truth stands clear. The enemy is real, but he only begs at the door of the heart. He does not rule it. Whoever turns to Allah by fasting, reading the Quran, or seeking His protection finds that the door stays shut.

Turning a Hard Question Into Firmer Certainty

The main point is this: the hadith about chaining the devils describes a mercy that weakens them and helps the believer. Iblis at Badr shows that even his strongest effort fails as soon as Allah’s help comes. These two texts do not clash. They teach the same lesson from different sides.

If you face a question like this again, treat it as you did here. Look closer. You will often find not a problem, but a deeper harmony. May Allah, who defeated falsehood at Badr and chains the devils each Ramadan, keep your heart firm and reward you for asking so well.

records.title: If Dua with Certainty Is Answered, Why Ask Twice?
records.question: If making dua with certainty means it is answered, why do we need to ask more than once? Does asking again not show a lack of certainty in the first promise?
records.answer:
Asking again does not mean you lack certainty. Each time you ask, you are worshipping Allah as He commanded.

The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, said, “Supplication is itself worship.” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi, who graded it fine and rigorously authenticated] This means that making du’a is an act of worship every time you do it. Repeating your du’a is like praying again after you have already prayed. We do not question why we pray each day. In the same way, asking again is not a sign of doubt. It is part of how we serve Allah.

Allah Most High says: “And your Lord has said: ‘Call on Me and I will answer you'” [Quran 40:60; Keller, The Quran Beheld]. The command comes before the promise. He tells us to call, and then tells us He answers. We are not petitioning a reluctant authority that might have missed it the first time. We are doing the thing He asked us to do, and He has bound Himself to respond.

What the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) did warn against is the opposite of your worry. He said that a servant’s supplication “will be answered so long as he does not become hasty.” When he was asked what haste is, he explained: the man who says, “I have called, and I have called, and I do not see that He is answering me,” and then gives up and stops asking. [Bukhari; Muslim] Read that again with your question in mind. The tradition does not caution us against repeating. It cautions us against stopping.

Allah always keeps His promise, but the answer may come in different ways. The Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, said: “There is no Muslim who makes a supplication containing no sin and no severing of kinship but that Allah grants him by it one of three things: either He hastens its answer for him, or He stores it up for him in the next life, or He turns away from him an evil equal to it.” The Companions said, “Then we will make many supplications.” He said, “Allah is more abundant.” [Ahmad] The Companions wanted to ask more, not less.

Ask Again Because Asking Is Worship, Not Because the First Time Failed

Keep asking, and remember what you are doing. Each time you make du’a, you are obeying Allah and showing your trust in Him. Certainty is not about saying the perfect words once. It is about knowing that Allah hears you, has power over all things, and will give what is best. This certainty is what keeps you asking. Doubt is what makes a person stop.
references: Tirmidhi, who graded it fine and rigorously authenticated

records.title: Is It Permissible to Work as a Civil Engineer in the Armed Forces?
records.question: I am considering a career as a civil engineering officer in my country’s armed forces. According to the official role description, the position involves civil engineering and infrastructure rather than weapons or weapon systems. Duties include roads, airfields, bridges, sewerage systems, field defenses and obstacles, terrain assessment advice, and humanitarian missions. I intend to work as a civil engineer, not to design, manufacture, or operate weapons. I recognize, though, that the infrastructure I help build or maintain may indirectly support military operations. Is this permissible in the Hanafi school?
records.answer:
Yes, based on the details you have given, it would be permissible for you to work in this role. The job is, in and of itself, permissible, and there is no assisting in sin directly or even indirectly. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Make a good intention to serve the people of your country and to be a means of promoting well-being and safety in your country, and intend to please Allah. You will see much good.

records.title: Is Complaining Out Loud in Frustration a Sin or Objecting to Allah’s Decree?
records.question: A brother does not curse or insult, but when things go wrong, he complains out of distress. He says things like “What is wrong with this thing?” or “What is wrong with these phones?” He also says, “To Allah we belong, and to Him we return” (inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un). Is this unlawful, or is it objecting to Allah’s decree?
records.answer:
No. Saying such things in a moment of frustration is not unlawful, and it is not objecting to Allah’s decree. There is no insult to Allah in it, no blame directed at Him, and no disbelief.

Complaining to Allah and Complaining About Allah

There is a difference between complaining to Allah Most High and complaining about Allah. The Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him) said: “I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah.” [Quran 12:86]

Complaining about Allah means blaming Him for what happens or speaking as if He has treated you unfairly. Saying something about a phone or a small annoyance is not the same. These are just words of frustration, not blame toward Allah.

A Better Habit

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “If something afflicts you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such and such.’ Rather say, ‘This is what Allah has decreed, and He does as He wills.'” [Muslim]

So the brother should train himself to replace the complaint with these words, or with “Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un,” which he already says. That is the path of etiquette (adab), not a matter of sin.

records.title: Is a Non-Marital Relationship Ever Permitted to Help Someone Heal From Trauma?
records.question: I survived rape and severe domestic abuse and have been in trauma treatment for years. I cannot marry right now because I need significant time to establish that someone is safe, and I am considering consensual sexual relationships because I genuinely believe they may be part of my recovery. Does Islamic law make provision for serious psychological harm or necessity in a case like mine, and if so, what are its limits?
records.answer:
What happened to you was a deep injustice. The time and effort you have given to healing show real strength. Islamic law does not permit a sexual relationship outside marriage, even in hardship. This is not because your pain is ignored, but because the rule itself is clear.

Keep seeking healing, both with trusted professionals and by building support around you, socially and spiritually.

Try to build a steady circle of family, friends, and community. Reach out first if you can, and aim to connect every day or a few times a week.

Spiritually, tend to your relationship with Allah. SeekersGuidance offers many resources, and your local community may also offer learning circles and spiritual company.

The Legal Issue

Two maxims govern: necessity makes the unlawful lawful, and necessities are measured to the extent they require. The second exists precisely so the first never becomes a general license, and Imam Ibn Nujaym (may Allah have mercy on him) states the two together in al-Ashbah wa al-Nazaʾir [Ibn Nujaym, al-Ashbah wa al-Nazaʾir]. Their root text is the verse of compulsion: “So whoever is compelled by starvation, without liking to, or exceeding the least to survive, shall incur no sin thereby: Truly Allah is all-forgiving, all-compassionate.” [Quran 2:173; Keller, The Quran Beheld] Notice how much work the wording does: compelled, unwilling, and not one step past the minimum.

Why a Therapeutic Rationale Is Not the Compulsion the Maxim Contemplates

First, the harm must be what the jurists describe: real danger to life, limb, or a basic ability, not just pain or hardship. Your suffering is real, but it is not in this category. The verse speaks of someone forced, not someone choosing an act in hope of healing.

Second, the forbidden means must be an established remedy for the harm. Where the jurists permit an otherwise unlawful treatment, they require that a competent and trustworthy physician judge, with strong probability, that this specific thing will remove the harm, and that nothing lawful will do so [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar].

What you describe is a theory about how the body heals, not a treatment given by someone qualified to judge it. A relationship outside marriage carries its own risk of harm, including the same kind of hurt you are working to recover from.

Third, the allowance ends as soon as a lawful path is possible. By your own words, marriage is not impossible for you. You wrote that you need time to know someone is safe. Needing time is not a barrier.

The Lawful Door Is Slower Than You Want, and It Is Not Shut

Sacred law does not require you to marry quickly or move faster than you are ready. Take a year if you need. Take longer. Bring in family, a trusted scholar, or a counselor. Meet in safe public places for as long as you need. Share your story when you are ready, and stop at any time. A man worth marrying will accept your pace. His patience is itself a sign to look for.

What you are seeking—a body that feels safe again—is more likely to be found inside marriage. There, someone is committed to you, knows your history, can be asked to stop, and is still there the next day. This is not the second best. It is the setting where real healing is most likely.

Keep going with your treatment. If progress has stalled, try a new approach or a new clinician. Look for someone who understands sexual trauma and will work with your faith. Keep a short daily practice, even if it is just three minutes. Let your connection with Allah be steady, not something that depends on your feelings.

The Concession Does Not Open, and the Door You Named Is Still Yours

So your next step is not about a relationship. Ask your care team, clearly, why years of work have not brought the change you hoped for, and what else can be tried. Allah did not put your healing behind something He has forbidden. He does not ask you to rush.

records.title: May I Throw Away Food When Only Part of It Has Spoiled?
records.question: If mold has spread over part of a dish or a loaf and some of it still looks sound, may I throw the whole thing away? What if separating the good from the spoiled would be tedious, or I cannot tell whether the food has gone bad at all? And may I simply wash away the small pieces of pureed vegetable left stuck to the walls of a food processor?
records.answer:
If the food has truly spoiled, you can throw it away. You are not sinful if you also discard parts that still look sound, especially if sorting them out would be difficult or time-consuming.

Wasting Wealth

Wasting wealth is disliked (makruh), and active wastefulness—waste made a habit—is sinful. The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Allah, Exalted, has forbidden you: disobeying mothers, withholding what is due and demanding what is not one’s right, and burying daughters alive. And He has made disliked for you: idle talk, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.” [Agreed upon]

Allah Most High says, “and devour it not in prodigal waste: Verily He loves not those who exceed lawful bounds.” [Quran 6:141; Keller, The Quran Beheld] Slight waste is improper, and considerable waste is disliked. Neither describes throwing out what has already spoiled.

Visible Mold Spoils the Whole Dish
