Paying for the opportunity to engage in the activity rests on the type of transaction. If it’s a chance transaction, then it would remain impermissible. In most situations, if a person wants to win something and the owner of the activity withholds the prize, most people would have an issue with this. Therefore, it remains a chance transaction. If one paid simply to have a go and nothing more, without even looking back for the prize, this would be permissible but a waste of money, so best avoided.

The arcade games you mentioned are akin to loot boxes in video games. Payment is made to get an unspecified digital currency from which things can later be purchased. This lack of specificity is the issue, and therefore, the transaction will not be permissible. [Maydani, al-Lubab]

records.title: Is It Permissible to Hide Things or Tease Loved Ones Playfully?
records.question: Is it permissible to playfully hide someone’s things, or tease them while playing, if it causes only momentary fear or annoyance rather than real distress? For example, when my small nephew keeps trying to get all the pillows onto the bed, I throw each one back so he has to go again—is this kind of playful annoyance allowed, even right up to the point where he starts to lose his patience?
records.answer:
Yes. Jesting with those you love is permissible, and at times a Sunna, when it is a healthy jest: truthful, gentle, and free of fear or harm to the other person. The moment play frightens, vexes, or hurts, it is no longer jest, and it enters what the Sacred Law forbids.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) Jested, and Spoke Only the Truth

The Companions said, “Messenger of Allah, you jest with us.” He said, “I say only what is true.” [Tirmidhi]

His jest was affectionate and true. He said to an old woman, “No old woman shall enter Paradise.” She said, “What is the matter with them?” [Razin] He then reminded her of the verse, “Verily those on them We have brought forth in consummate perfection” [Quran 56:35; Keller, The Quran Beheld]: she would enter it, but not as an old woman.

He said to Anas (Allah be pleased with him), “O you of the two ears.” [Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi] A man asked him for a mount, and he said, “I shall carry you on the offspring of a she-camel.” The man said, “What shall I do with the offspring of a she-camel?” The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Do camels give birth to anything but she-camels?” [Tirmidhi; Abu Dawud]

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) also played with children. Anas (Allah be pleased with him) reported: “The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) would mix with us so freely that he would say to a young brother of mine, ‘Abu Umayr, what has the little sparrow done?'” [Bukhari; Muslim] The boy’s little sparrow, which he used to play with, had died.

The Companions jested as well. When the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) invited Awf ibn Malik (Allah be pleased with him) into his small leather tent, Awf said, “All of me, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “All of you.” [Abu Dawud]

A man of the Helpers (Ansar) who was given to jesting was poked in the side by the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) with a stick, and asked to get even. He said, “You are wearing a shirt, and I have no shirt on.” When the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) raised his shirt, the man embraced him and kissed his side, saying, “This is all I wanted, Messenger of Allah.” [Abu Dawud]

What the Jurists Say

Ibn Abidin (Allah have mercy on him), citing Imam Ghazali, explains these sayings: “Allusive speech is permitted for a real purpose, such as gladdening another’s heart with jest, like his saying (Allah bless him and give him peace), ‘No old woman will enter Paradise,’ and ‘There is white in your husband’s eye,’ and ‘We will carry you on a camel’s young,’ and the like.” [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Ibn Abbas (Allah be pleased with him): “Jesting in what is seemly is permissible; the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) jested, and said only what was true.”

The Conditions of Permissible Jest

Imam Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him) names the conditions. If you can manage “what the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) and his Companions were able to do, which is to jest while saying only what is true, hurting no heart, not going to excess in it, and keeping to it now and then, rarely, then there is no harm in it for you.” [Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din]

The Hanafi faqih and hadith master Mulla Ali al-Qari (Allah have mercy on him) draws the line in one sentence: “Jesting is being at ease with another without hurting him; if it reaches hurt, it becomes mockery.” [Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih, 1, 7.3061] Mockery is what Allah forbids: “O you who believe: Let no people mock another, for they may well be better than themselves.” [Quran 49:11; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

So a healthy jest is truthful, causes no fear or hurt, humiliates no one, is not made a habit, and is something the other person enjoys too.

Is a Momentary Fright Really Included?

You are right that these hadith concern a real effect on a person. But look at what happened. Ibn Abi Layla related: “The Companions of Muhammad (Allah bless him and give him peace) told us that they were traveling with the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) when one of them fell asleep. Some of them went to a rope he had and took it, and he was startled. The Beloved Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, ‘It is not lawful for a Muslim to frighten another Muslim.'” [Abu Dawud] Nothing was stolen, and the fright was brief. Still, he forbade it.

He also said (Allah bless him and give him peace), “None of you should take his brother’s staff, whether in jest or in earnest; and whoever takes his brother’s staff, let him return it to him.” [Tirmidhi; Abu Dawud]

Mulla Ali al-Qari relays Abu Ubayd’s explanation: “It is that he takes his belongings not intending to steal them, but only intending to bring vexation upon him: he is playing at the theft, but in earnest in bringing vexation, alarm, and hurt upon him.” [Qari, Mirqat al-Mafatih]

So the measure is not how big the fear is, but what the act does to the other person’s heart. Hiding your sister’s phone so that she searches for it, worried, even for a minute, is taking a thing in jest while being earnest in alarm. A game in which she knows it is you and laughs along is shared play. When unsure, ask yourself: would their first feeling be laughter, or a sinking heart?

Playing With Your Nephew

Playing with a small child is from the Sunna. Throwing the pillow back is fine as long as he takes it as a game and laughs. Do not play until just before he loses his temper: the aim is his delight, not the edge of his patience. Stop while he is still laughing, let him win in the end, and leave him happy.

Let Your Jest Gladden Hearts

Jest that gladdens a heart follows the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace); jest that alarms or vexes does not. Keep it true, gentle, occasional, and welcome, and your play with your family becomes a way of giving them their due, with reward.

records.title: Is Asking AI About the Wisdom Behind Events Shirk, and Is It Forgiven If Repeated?
records.question: Can shirk be forgiven if it happens more than once? I started asking AI about the possible wisdom behind events and feared future outcomes, even though I know only Allah holds that wisdom. I sincerely repented and tried to limit my use of AI, but over time, I fell into the same pattern again, fixating on feared outcomes and asking the same kind of questions for reassurance, even though nothing had actually changed. I worry this counts as shirk, especially since it seems tied to doubt or discomfort about past events, even though those arose from my own free-will choices.
records.answer:
Based on your description, this is not shirk. As for repentance, it is accepted; many times, a sincere servant comes back to Allah. The pattern evident from your description carries the marks of baseless misgivings (waswasa), and the cure is to stop feeding it altogether.

Whether this concerns you or someone close to you, the fear behind the question is a sign of a heart that cares about its standing with Allah.

Asking About Wisdom Is Reflection

Imam Nawawi (Allah have mercy on him) defines leaving Islam as cutting it off through an intention, a statement of disbelief, or an act of disbelief. [Nawawi, Minhaj al-Talibin] Shirk means ascribing to another what belongs to Allah alone, such as believing that someone besides Him knows the unseen. What you have stated is the opposite: only Allah holds the wisdom behind what He decrees. Your wondering about what that wisdom might be is a type of reflection, which the Quran praises in those who say, “Our Lord, You have not created all this in vain” [Quran 3:191; Keller, The Quran Beheld].

Regret Over the Past Leaves Faith Intact

Regretting something about the past, or your own choices in it, is part of being human. When his son Ibrahim (Allah be pleased with him) died, the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “The eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord.” [Bukhari; Muslim] What he taught us to leave is the endless “if only”: “Say, ‘Allah decreed, and He did what He willed,’ for ‘if’ opens the door to the work of Shaytan.” [Muslim] Your “what if” questions belong to that door, so it is best kept shut.

Repentance Is Accepted Every Time

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) spoke of a servant in a cycle of sinning and asking forgiveness, and each time Allah said, “My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sin.” Then He said, “Do what you will, for I have forgiven you.” [Bukhari; Muslim] Imam Nawawi explains its meaning: as long as you sin and then repent, I forgive you. [Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim, in meaning]

Leave the Question With Allah

Some of the Companions once told the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) that they found thoughts within themselves too terrible to say aloud. He replied, “That is clear faith.” [Muslim] The distress you feel at the mere possibility of shirk is that same faith at work.

You need to stop this cycle. The fear will keep asking for reassurance, and every answer, whether it comes from AI or elsewhere, satisfies it only until the next time. So stop answering it. When the thought comes, say, “Allah decreed, and He did what He willed,” and carry on with whatever is in front of you. It will feel uncomfortable at first, and then, with Allah’s help, it will fade. Speak to an Allah-conscious counselor who understands obsessive doubt, and to a teacher you trust. Seeking help is part of taking the means Allah has given you.
references: Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim, in meaning

records.title: Can I Follow Ibn Hazm and Ibn Taymiyya Instead of Making Up Fifteen Years of Prayers?
records.question: For about fifteen years, I sometimes did not pray, sometimes prayed without wudu or ghusl, and sometimes prayed to be seen. I have recently repented and now keep my five daily prayers. Must I make up fifteen years of prayers? I do not know how many were valid. Can I follow Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn Hazm, who held that repentance is enough? I do not want to meet Allah having taken the easy way out, but around 27,000 prayers feels beyond me.
records.answer:
Your repentance and return to the obligatory prayers are a gift from Allah, and seeing your other sins in a new light is a sign that the repentance is real.

In the Shafiʿi school, and in all four schools, every obligatory prayer you neglected or prayed without the required purification must be made up, and our school requires it without delay. What you owe is likely far fewer than 27,000 prayers.

Making Up the Prayers Is Agreed Upon

Imam Nawawi (Allah have mercy on him) records the consensus (ijmaʿ) of the recognized scholars that anyone who deliberately leaves a prayer must make it up. Ibn Hazm (Allah have mercy on him) dissented, and Imam Nawawi judges his view contrary to consensus and unsupported by the evidence. [Nawawi, al-Majmuʿ] Imam Ibn Taymiyya (Allah have mercy on him) later took a similar position. The four schools stand united on this, and their agreement is what you follow. A view that departs from the consensus of the scholars is not one a Muslim may adopt, and the Hanbali school itself, to which Imam Ibn Taymiyya belonged, requires the makeup; Shaykh Faraz Rabbani’s answer below sets out the evidence. Your fear of choosing the easy way is a good fear to have, as long as it is grounded in knowledge.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, its expiation is to pray it when he remembers it.” [Bukhari; Muslim] If the one who forgot a prayer must make it up, the one who left it deliberately owes it all the more.

Count Only What You Owe

Prayers you neglected, and those you offered without ablution (wudu) or the ritual bath (ghusl) must be made up.

Prayers offered to be seen need a closer look. Imam Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him), quoted by Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami (Allah have mercy on him), explains that if showing off was your only reason for praying, such that you would not have prayed had you been alone, the prayer was invalid. If you had prayed anyway and the desire to be seen was the weaker motive, the prayer remains valid, though its reward is decreased. Simply being pleased that others saw you does not affect validity at all. He also warns against invalidating worship over the slightest passing thought. [Ghazali, Ihyaʾ Ulum al-Din; Haytami, al-Zawajir] Ask yourself one question about those years: would I have prayed that prayer if no one were there?

Then make a careful estimate, counting every prayer you are not certain you prayed validly. [Haytami, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj] You mentioned that it happened sometimes, so the total is a portion of fifteen years, not all of it. My earlier answer below explains how to reach a number you can confidently rely on, and how to pace yourself.

Begin Today, Without Delay

The relied-upon position in our school is strict here. Imam Ibn Hajar al-Haytami rules that one who owes prayers missed without an excuse must make them up immediately, and may not spend time on anything else, voluntary prayers included, beyond what he needs for sleep, supporting his dependents, and other pressing obligations. [Haytami, Tuhfat al-Muhtaj] That is the rule our school holds you to.

For someone who cannot yet carry that, Imam Abdullah al-Haddad (Allah have mercy on him) taught that the repentant must make up what he neglected, gradually and according to his ability, neither straining himself nor growing lax, and Bughyat al-Mustarshidin records this as more fitting than requiring all one’s time, because of the severe hardship involved. [Mashhur, Bughyat al-Mustarshidin] At the least, pray one makeup prayer with each of your five prayers, and add more whenever you can. One with each prayer fulfills a full year of missed prayers every year, and two with each prayer halves the time. Continue in this manner to the best of your ability, and trust that Allah sees the effort of a sincere servant who has turned back to Him.

Allah Most High says: “Say, ‘O My servants who have committed excesses against their very selves, despair not of the mercy of Allah: Verily Allah forgives all sins soever: Truly He is the All-forgiving, the All-compassionate.'” [Quran 39:53; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

records.title: Must I Return Extra Food a Shop Gives Me When I Cannot Tell If It Was Intentional?
records.question: A local chicken shop sometimes gives me one or two more wings than I paid for. This is sometimes intentional, for example, when the wings are small, but I cannot always tell whether it is intentional or accidental. Must I try to return the extra whenever I notice it? If this happens often, and they usually say it is fine when I try to give the money back, must I keep trying to give it back?
records.answer:
No. In the Hanafi school, you may take what the shop hands you and enjoy it, with no need to return it or to keep asking. Speak up only when something is clearly a mistake.

Custom Decides What the Extra Means

The governing principle is one of the great maxims of the law: custom is decisive (al-ada muhakkama). Imam Ibn Nujaym (Allah have mercy on him) writes: “Know that regard for habit and custom is referred to in fiqh in many questions, so much so that the jurists made it a foundational principle.” [Ibn Nujaym, al-Ashbah wa al-Nazaʾir]

Imam Hamawi (Allah have mercy on him), commenting on this maxim, explains that custom means “the repetition of a thing, and its recurring so often that it ceases to be something that happens by chance.” [Hamawi, Ghamz Uyun al-Basaʾir]

That describes your shop exactly. An extra wing that turns up again and again is not an accident. It is how they serve their customers, making up for small pieces or looking after their regulars. The server packs it knowingly and hands it over willingly.

Their Word Settles It

Allah Most High says: “devour not your wealth between you through falsehood; But only through trade by your complete mutual consent.” [Quran 4:29; Keller, The Quran Beheld] Here, the consent is plain. They added the extra themselves, and when you offered to pay, they told you it was fine. Nothing more is owed.

The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “May Allah have mercy on a man who is easygoing when he sells, when he buys, and when he calls in a debt.” [Bukhari] The seller who adds a wing is being easygoing. Meet him in the same spirit: accept it with thanks.

A Simple Rule to Live By

Accept what is given ordinarily. If something is clearly a mistake, such as someone else’s order in your bag or far too much change, say so plainly, once. A mere possibility of error creates no duty to investigate, and once they tell you it is fine, the matter is closed. Repeated checking in matters like this is not an act of caution. It is a burden that Allah has not placed on you.

Taqwa Is Shown in Everyday life

Your concern for other people’s rights is praiseworthy. It is part of the mindfulness of Allah (taqwa), which extends to what we eat and how we deal with others. Keep it healthy by putting it where it belongs: pay what you owe, keep your word, and treat the people who serve you kindly.

Keep learning, too. A sound grasp of the basics of worship and dealings, taken step by step from qualified teachers, is the surest cure for doubts. Knowledge tells you what Allah asks of you, and just as clearly, what He does not.

records.title: Can I Rely on Halal Certificates for Machine-Slaughtered Chicken?
records.question: My parents buy machine-slaughtered chicken with a halal certificate. Furthermore, most restaurants serve such meats and label them halal. It is difficult for me to ensure that the meat is hand-slaughtered. The meat is physically pure (tahir) because the birds bleed out properly, so it does not affect my tahara for prayer, right? Is it valid for me to use a rukhsa based on contemporary fatwas and Islamic academies to trust these certificates and eat this meat—both at home and in restaurants—without it being an invalid talfiq and without sinning?
records.answer:
There is a genuine difference of opinion over machine-slaughtered chicken. We hold that hand-slaughtered meat is safer and more properly fulfills the criteria of lawful slaughter, so make it your practice at home and when you eat out, as far as you reasonably can.

Allah Most High says: “So eat but of that which the Name of Allah has been mentioned over when slaughtered, if believers in His verses you be.” [Quran 6:118; Keller, The Quran Beheld] And He says: “And eat not of what the Name of Allah has been purposely uninvoked upon at death: Truly it is godless iniquity.” [Quran 6:121; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) joined the cut and the Name: “Whatever makes the blood flow and over which the name of Allah is mentioned, eat it.” [Bukhari; Muslim] He also asked for care in the act itself: “Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has prescribed excellence (ihsan) toward everything. So when you kill, kill well; and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let one of you sharpen his blade and give ease to his animal.” [Muslim]

What the Hanafi School Requires

The Hanafi jurists give full weight to the word “purposely.” Imam Marghinani writes: “If the slaughterer leaves out the invocation deliberately, the slaughtered animal is carrion and is not eaten; if he leaves it out forgetfully, it is eaten.” [al-Marghinani, al-Hidaya]

Imam Kasani adds two details that bear directly on machines. The invocation must come “from the slaughterer, so that if someone else says it while the slaughterer is silent, remembering and not forgetting, it is not lawful.” [al-Kasani, Bada’i’ al-Sana’i’] Nor does one invocation carry over to the next animal: if he “slaughtered another sheep thinking the first invocation sufficed for both, it may not be eaten.” [Ibid.] Ibn Abidin gives the reason: “the invocation is a condition by explicit text, and it is by intention.” [Ibn Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

In a plant, a rotating blade can cut thousands of birds an hour. Who is the slaughterer, and does his intended invocation fall on each bird? That is where the doubt lies. A Muslim who cuts by hand and says the Name over each animal meets every condition beyond question.

Other scholars and certifying bodies permit machine slaughter under set conditions, and those who follow them in good faith are not to be censured.

Allah Rewards the Better Choice

Allah Most High praises “Those who listen to what is said and wholeheartedly follow the very best of it: Those are whom Allah has truly guided, and possessed of insight and mind.” [Quran 39:18; Keller, The Quran Beheld] And the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt, for truthfulness is tranquility and falsehood is disquiet.” [Ahmad; Tirmidhi; Nasa’i]

Following a qualified opinion in an open question is not, by itself, forbidden talfiq. But a dispensation (rukhsa) is for real need, and ease is not a need. Where hand-slaughtered meat is within reach, the question is not what you may do, but what is better for your religion.

At Home, When Eating Out, and in Prayer

One. At home: speak to your parents gently and gratefully, and offer to buy hand-slaughtered chicken from a Muslim butcher yourself. Never turn the tables into a dispute; excellence toward parents is itself a duty. Where declining what they serve would cause real hurt, eat without anxiety: you are following a recognized opinion.

Two. Eating out: ask how the meat was slaughtered. Favor places that serve hand-slaughtered meat; elsewhere, choose fish or vegetarian dishes.

Three. Prayer: eating or handling this meat does not break your ablution (wudu), and your past prayers are sound. Wash your hands and mouth after eating, as you would after any meal.

Scrupulousness Lightens the Reckoning

Imam Qushayri defines it: “As for scrupulousness (wara’)ت it is leaving the doubtful.” [al-Qushayri, al-Risala al-Qushayriyya] Yahya ibn Mu’adh said: “Scrupulousness is standing at the limit of knowledge without reinterpretation.” And Abu Uthman said: “The reward of scrupulousness is a lighter reckoning.” [Ibid.]

Choose the better course with quiet resolve and a gentle manner at your family’s table. What you leave for Allah’s sake is never a loss.

records.title: Will Jinn, Angels, and Animals Be Resurrected, and Will Jinn Cross the Sirat?
records.question: We know that humans will be resurrected in the same body and form as they were on Earth. Is this the same in the case of other creatures, like jinn, Angels, and animals? Furthermore, will jinns also cross the Sirat like us? Or is it better to refrain from commenting on such matters?
records.answer:
All three are raised, but not to the same end. The angels die at the first blast of the Trumpet and are then raised to live on. The jinn are raised and judged as we are, though their crossing of the Bridge over Hell (Sirat) is not decisively established. Animals are raised, the wrongs between them are redressed, and then they end, returning to dust.

Four Principles from the Books of Creed

One. What revelation reports, and reason allows, we affirm. The Hereafter is known by transmission (sam’), not by speculation. Imam Ghazali (Allah have mercy on him), the great Ashʿari theologian, states the rule while speaking of the questioning in the grave: “Reports have come of it, so affirming it is obligatory, because it is possible.” [Ghazali, Qawaʿid al-Aqaʾid]

Two. Raising the dead is within Allah’s power for every creature. Imam Jamal al-Din al-Ghaznawi, of the Hanafi-Maturidi theologians, writes: “The wild beasts, the birds, and the livestock are gathered on the Day of Resurrection, because that is possible to reason, as a manifestation of the power of Allah Most High.” [Ghaznawi, Usul al-Din] On these points, the two schools agree.

Three. Judgment follows responsibility. Humans and jinn were given the charge of faith and obedience (taklif), so they are judged. Allah Most High addresses the two together: “We shall devote Our undivided judgment to you two alone, O most weighty of all kinds of beings.” [Quran 55:31; Keller, The Quran Beheld] The angels are honored servants who do not disobey, and animals bear no charge, so neither stands trial.

Four. Where the texts are silent on details, we are silent. The texts are explicit that people return in their own bodies. For other creatures, they affirm the raising and leave their manner unstated, and so do we.

The Angels Die, Then Live On

Allah Most High says: “And the Trumpet is blasted, and all in the heavens and earth are thunderstruck dead, save whom Allah wills.” [Quran 39:68; Keller, The Quran Beheld] He also says: “Everything is perishing but the Face of His everlasting Being.” [Quran 28:88; Keller, The Quran Beheld] The angels are among the dwellers of the heavens, and the texts indicate that they too taste death, until none remains but Allah.

Then they are raised, and they live on without end. In Paradise, they come to its people with greetings of peace: “Angels entering upon them from every door.” [Quran 13:23; Keller, The Quran Beheld]

The Jinn Are Judged; the Sirat Is Left to Allah

The jinn are responsible as we are, so they are raised and judged as we are. Their believers are saved, and their disbelievers are punished.

Whether they cross the Sirat is another matter. The books of creed describe the Bridge stretched over Hell, on which the feet of the disbelievers slip, and the feet of the believers stand firm, as Imam Ghazali sets out in Qawaʿid al-Aqaʾid. No text states decisively that the jinn cross it, or how. One might infer it from their being judged, but an inference is not an established text. So we neither affirm it as creed nor deny it; we leave it with Allah.

Animals Are Gathered, Requited, and Then End

Allah Most High says: “And when wild beasts are massed for their retribution.” [Quran 81:5; Keller, The Quran Beheld] Abu Hurayra (Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Rights will surely be rendered to those who hold them on the Day of Resurrection, until even the hornless sheep will be granted retaliation against the horned sheep.” [Muslim]

This is justice made visible, not a trial of faith. No animal is rewarded or punished for belief, but the wrongs between them are set right. Then they end. Imam Baghawi relates in his commentary on the Quran that once the requital is complete, they are told, in meaning, to become dust. It is then that the unbeliever wishes he too had been dust [Quran 78:40].

Should You Refrain from Asking?

No. The Companions (Allah be pleased with them) asked about the Hereafter, and revelation answered. The right manner here (adab) is simple: ask, affirm what the texts affirm, and stop where they stop. What we refrain from is building on their silence.

records.title: How Can I Hide My Past From My Future Husband?
records.question: If one fornicated in the past but has repented, is it necessary to share it with one’s future husband? If the girl doesn’t want to share it due to the fear that he may leave her or that society won’t accept her anymore, can she keep it secret? Will he figure it out when they get intimate? How can I hide it?
records.answer:
I am pleased to hear that you have repented. You should not and may not tell your future husband about your fornication as exposing sin is sinful in itself.

Exposing Sin

Telling your future husband about this is not an option, as you would be exposing something that Allah kept hidden and it could ruin your marriage as well. Can We Deny Having Committed Sins After We’ve Repented From Them? Is It Permissible to Lie In Order to Conceal Past Sins?

Hiding It

In terms of him figuring it out, don’t worry about it. Just be modest, loving, cheerful, and take good care of him, and leave the rest up to Allah. If he directly asks you, which he should not, you should follow the tips in the link above and half-truth the answer. Will My Future Husband Find Out About My Virginity? Because I Committed Zina in the Past, Will I Ever Get Married to a Good Muslim Man?

records.title: Am I Sinful If I Don’t Serve the Ummah?
records.question: If a person worships Allah Most High obediently, prays, fasts, completes all obligations concerning their parents, children, and kin, however, is unable to help the Ummah in any form like donation, medication, or teaching, is this a selfish act?
records.answer:
In the Name of the Allah, Most Merciful and Compassionate

Our first obligation as believers is to save ourselves and our family from detrimental things to our faith in this world and the Hereafter. Allah Most High says,

“O believers! Save yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is humans and stones…” (Quran, 66:6)

Therefore, by covering your personal obligations and upholding your family’s rights, you are doing your duty and should hope for reward. Anything beyond this for the broader Ummah and community is praiseworthy and beneficial. Still, if your funds or time are limited and you do not have the means to do extra charity or volunteering, you are not sinful for this.

Your feeling of regret is a sign of your sincere wish and desire, and Allah Most High sees that and can reward you for that. However, you should not be stressed out, feel guilty, or pay attention to any misgivings in this regard. Instead, one thing you can do is keep praying for the Ummah whenever you pray for yourself.

records.title: Is it True that the Reward for Fasting Cannot Be Taken Away by Others on the Day of Judgement?
records.question: Is it true that fasting is the one good deed that other people can’t take from you on the Day of Judgement?
records.answer:
I have not found anything to prove that fasting is the only deed that other people cannot be taken from one’s account on the Day of Judgement.

On the contrary, there is a rigorously authenticated hadith in Sahih Muslim, narrated by Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Do you all know who the bankrupt person is?” The people around him said, “The bankrupt person, according to us, is the one who has no coin or possession.” So he replied, “The bankrupt of my Ummah is the one who will come on the Day of Judgement with prayer, and fasting, the zakat; he comes, but he also berated this person, and falsely accused that person, and embezzled the money of this other person, and spilt the blood of yet another person, and struck that one. So he will give this person from his good deeds, and that person from his good deeds, and if his good deeds run out before he pays back what is upon him, the sins of those people will be taken and thrown onto him, then he will be flung into the Hellfire.” [Muslim]

Therefore, this indicates that fasting and its reward can be given to another person on the Day of Judgement in light of wrongs that were done to that person in this world.

records.title: Can we Give Zakah to Ahl al-Bayt?
records.question: Zakah should not be given to the “Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib,” as they are the direct descendants of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace), also known as Sayyids.” If someone is a sayyid, can he/she give zakah to another sayyid/sayyida, as you would be giving to a relative who is (struggling financially)? Can we pay Zakah in installments? If, for example, we pay a certain amount this month and the rest in a different month?
records.answer:
Who Are the Ahl Al-Bayt in This Context?

The Ahl al-Bayt (the members of the Prophet’s household) is the tribe of ‘Abd al-Muttalib (the descendants of ‘Ali, the descendants of ‘Abbas, the descendants of Ja’far, the descendants of ‘Aqil, the descendants of al-Harith and the sons of ‘Abd al-Muttalib), and their freed slaves. [Al-Mawsua al-Fiqhiyya]

Can the Ahl Al-Bayt Receive Zakah?

There is an Ijma (consensus) among Muslim scholars that it is not lawful to give Zakah (obligatory charity) to the family members of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace), and nor should they receive it. [Nawawi, Majmu’]

In light of the above, the beloved Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) said: “Charity and Zakah are not lawful for the family members of the Prophet, since they would be considered as the dirt of the people who give them.” [Muslim]

Instead, Sacred Law allotted a one-fifth share of the collective booty. Allah says: “Know that whatever spoils you take, one-fifth is for Allah and the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travelers if you ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and what We revealed to Our servant on that decisive day when the two armies met ˹at Badr˺. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.” [Quran, 8:41]

May the Ahl Al-Bayt Receive Zakah in the Absence of Booty?

Though not the majority or strongest view, some scholars opine that when the allotted share of booty is not available, and the members of his noble family (may Allah bless him and give him peace) are in need, they may be given Zakah. The official view in the Shafi’i School is that it is not befitting and impermissible, and Allah knows best. [Nawawi, Majmu’]

Can the Family of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) Give Each Other Zakah?

As with the above ruling, a minority of scholars [Hanbali School] opine that the Ahl Al-Bayt may receive each other’s Zakah. The majority, however, disagree with this opinion, and Allah knows best. [Mardawi, Al-Insaf]

The late contemporary Shafi’i Mufti, Muhammad Taha Karaan (may Allah have mercy on him), opined that even though the above minority views exist, there are nobler alternatives. He advocated that it is more befitting that Muslims honor the noble family of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) by setting up special non-Zakah-based funds specifically for them. He initiated one such fund in South Africa.

May One Pay Zakah in Installments?

Zakah should be given to its rightful owners as soon as it is due. One may pay Zakah before it is due, and in that case, one may pay it in installments, and Allah knows best. [Misri, ‘Umdat al-Salik]

records.title: How to Manage the Joint Family Crisis and Its Effect on My Sons?
records.question: I have two boys who are 3 years old. I live in a joint family with my sister-in-law who has two older boys. They have behavior issues like hitting everyone and screaming. They especially hit my boys whenever they get a chance. Can you please give me a dua to protect my kids from their aggression?
records.answer:
I empathize with your difficult situation; this is not right by any means and your children are in harm’s way. I can give you some duas, but you must do more.

The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “Whosoever of you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is not able to do so, then [let him change it] with his tongue; and if he is not able to do so, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.” [Muslim]

Try to Move Out

Living in a joint family system is difficult and it is not meant for all families. Sit with your husband and ask yourselves if you can move out. What would be the benefits and disadvantages? Is this the right time to go or should you move later? Come up with a plan because living with non-mahram men in the house is also a hardship, and this can impede the upbringing of your children and your ability to serve your family.

Please see these links for more detail: My Brother-In-Law Is Violent. Do I Have the Right to Move Out? A Wife’s Right to Housing Separate From Her In-Laws

Talk to Your Sister-in-Law

Whether you decide to move or not, you must sit down with her immediately and discuss the situation. You have to be polite, yet firm, and tell her that you want to come up with a plan to deal with her boys’ aggression. It will no longer be tolerated. Tell her that your husband is insisting on this, too. (Do talk to him too!) You can try anything from time-outs to deprivation of a privilege, to a firm holding down of the boy’s hands, while getting down to his eye level and telling him, “I won’t let you hit him, it hurts.”

See the following link for more useful ideas: If Gentle Discipline Isn’t Working, This Might Be the Reason

If Talking Doesn’t Work

In the worst-case scenario, that is if your sister-in-law doesn’t help you, you will have to take the matter into your own hands. Tell the boys yourself that you will take away their toys if they hit. Keep the children in your room more often with the door locked and take your boys out on your own more often. Another approach is to involve all the boys in listening to Islamic stories of good character and discipline, involving them in gentle, quiet play like coloring and building, and all in all, encouraging quieter and peaceful games at home.

Last but Not Least-Deen and Duas

Most importantly, do not expect your home to be trouble-free if you are not fulfilling Allah’s obligations. Be sure that your family is praying five times a day, fasting, paying zakat on time, eating only the halal, and that the ladies are covering when they leave the house. Read some Quran every day with the meaning, be an example of good character, honesty, patience, generosity, and serving neighbors, the poor, the needy, and family. Through all this good, you will Insha Allah, see good come to you as well. You will find these 15 duas perfectly suited for your needs and the children’s needs.

records.title: What Will Be Considered Devotion of a Wife to Her Husband in Paradise?
records.question: If a person gets what they desire in paradise, what will a wife do for her husband in paradise that will be considered devotion to her husband?
records.answer:
The inner subtleties of paradise are unknown to us. However, a wife will be delighted with her husband and all the other luxuries; she will, like everyone else, have no emotions of less or more. A paradise is a place of no feelings. One will continuously feel devoted, in total pleasure and bliss eternally.

Please take some time out to read the Reader on Women’s Ranks in the Hereafter.

records.title: Does the Urdu Expression “Tum Azad Ho Meri Tarf Se” Count as Divorce?
records.question: Does the Urdu expression “tum azad ho meri tarf se” count as divorce? Would it still count if a husband says that to his wife without the intention to divorce her? This phrase is used for divorce in my location.
records.answer:
Amin.

The expression in question is considered allusive and would only constitute divorce if said with the intention of divorce, and Allah knows best.

Explicit and Allusive Expressions of Divorce

Expressions such as “you are free from me” and “I free you from our relationship” in any language are allusive terms (kinaya). Allusive expressions affect divorce, but only if the husband intends to divorce. If he did not intend to divorce, no divorce occurred. [Al-Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

Divorce in a Language Other than Arabic

Only the word ‘divorce (talaq),’ when translated into any language, is considered explicit (sarih) and will therefore affect a divorce with or without the intention to do so. [Al-Shirbini, Mughni al-Muhtaj]

Plain Words of Divorce

The words that effect a divorce may be plain or allusive. Plain words effect divorce whether one intends it or not, while allusive words do not effect it unless one intends to divorce.

Using plain words to effect a divorce means expressly pronouncing the word divorce (in any language) or terms derived from it. When the husband says: “I divorce you” or “You are divorced,” the wife is immediately divorced whether he has made the intention or not.

Here and in the rulings below, expressions such as “the wife is divorced” or “the divorce is effected” mean just one of the three times necessary to finalize it unless the husband intends a two or threefold divorce or repeats the words three times.

When a husband is asked, “Have you divorced your wife?” and he says, “Yes,” she is divorced even if he does not intend it. [Keller, Reliance of the Traveler]

Allusive Words of Divorce

Using allusive words to effect a divorce includes:

When one intends divorce by any of the above, the words effect it, but if one does not, they do not. [ibid.]

records.title: Is the Hadith About the Sahaba Move during Dhikr Authentic and Is It Permissible to Move (Sit) during Dhikr?
records.question: if the hadith where the sahaba move during dhikr is authentic. Is this proof that it is permissible to move (sit) during dhikr?
records.answer:
I am not sure of the grading of the narration which you mentioned. However, the validity of the Hadra is not dependent on that specific narration. The following proofs have been mentioned by great scholars in support of the permissibility of the Hadra:

The Hadra

The term Hadra refers to the heart’s presence (hudur) with Allah Most High.

As it pertains to the spiritual path (tasawwuf) it is a gathering of remembrance of Allah Most High organized by a spiritual mentor (shaykh) or his appointee. It contains (generally speaking) recitation of the Quran and reading of Prophetic narrations, sayings, or poems of the scholars; thereafter, everyone engages in remembrance of Allah. [Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya fi Bayan Adilla al-Sufiyya]

Afterward, there is generally a closing talk and recitation of some portion of the Quran. [Ibid.]

The History of the Hadra

The Hadra has been established and transmitted by the elite of scholars and knowers of Allah. It is recorded in their books and has become a manifest symbol of the spiritual path. [Ibid.]

Among these scholars were Ahmad al-Rifa’i, Junaid al-Baghdadi, ‘Abdul Qadir al-Jaylani; Abu Hasan al-Shadhili, Imam al-Sh’arani; Imam al-Hatimi; Imam al-Qushayri, and many others. [Ibid.]

Allah is pleased with them all and allows us to benefit from them. [Ibid.]

Evidence for the Hadra

Allah Most High says, “…those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides…” [Qur’an; 3:191]

Remembering Allah in Congregation

This above verse and other (some mentioned below) are evident in establishing the permissibility of remembering Allah Most High collectively.

All the verses of the Qur’an that command or encourage remembering Allah Most High, and grammatically are in the plural, are sufficient proof to collectively remember Allah Most High.

For example, if three people are listening to the recitation of the Qur’an and hear this verse:

“O believers, remember Allah much and glorify Him day and night.” [Quran, 33:41]

… then they all, in obedience to this command, begin remembering Allah by saying subhanAllah (glory be to Allah). No sound-minded believer would object to that.

As for the Prophetic narrations, they are many:

Proof From Prophetic Narrations

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “When you (all) pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze.” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?” He said, “The circles of knowledge.” [Ahmad]

He also said, “Indeed Allah has angels that travel the lands seeking out remembrance gatherings. If they find one, they sit with those gathered and crowd around one another with their wings until all that is between the heavens and Earth is filled. When the people disperse, they ascend to the heavens. Allah Exalted and Majestic then ask them, although He knows best, “From where have you come?” They reply, “We have come from being with Your servants on the Earth; they are declaring Your glory (i.e., saying subhanAllah), You’re being the only one worthy of worship (i.e., saying la ilaha ill Allah), and Your praise (i.e., saying alhamdulillah)” [Bukhari; Muslim: the specific wording here being from Muslim]

It is clear from this narration, found in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, that remembering Allah is not limited to reciting the Qur’an or circles of knowledge, as some wrongly professed.

Reciting Quran and seeking knowledge is part of remembering Allah, just as repeating praises and glorifications of Allah.

Opinions of the Scholars

Imam Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (Allah have mercy on him) was asked regarding the validity of remembering Allah collectively, aloud, in the mosques; he said the following:

“There is no dislike in doing so. ‘Izz ibn ‘Abd al-Salaam, Balqini, and many others have deemed it permissible.” [Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya fi Bayan Adilla al-Sufiyya]

The Term Hadra

The term Hadra as explained briefly above, means for the heart to be present with Allah Most High. It is a term coined by scholars of the spiritual path (tasawwuf). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and give him peace) referred to parallel realities in other terms, such as the following:

No Arguing Over Terms

Others may call it by other names. However, the name does not matter as much as what is being discussed; this is in line with the axiom: There is no argumentation concerning terms.

Allah Most High says, “Remember Allah abundantly…” [Ibid.]

General Commands and Encouragements

In the various verses mentioned above, and others, in which we are commanded or encouraged to remember Allah, Allah Most High does not specify any method. He has left it general, and the address is plural in the verses. [Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya]

Imam, Doctor Muhammad Sa’id Ramadan al-Buti (Allah have mercy on him, and allow us to continue to benefit from him) said, “Those who come together to attend the gatherings of remembrance (such as the Hadra), do so based upon the general meanings of Allah’s statement: “And those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides…” [Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya]

This is a clear, general statement that should not be taken from its original basis unless another text comes as an exception or specification. [Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya]

Likewise, no text has been transmitted limiting the remembrance of Allah to any specific method or time, and no text has been transmitted commanding to abstain from any particular method or time.” [Ibid.]

Closing: Respecting Differing Opinions

The Hadra is permissible in the Sacred law, as explained above. However, each Muslim is not obligated to do or even agree with. What is required of each Muslim is to respect the difference of opinions of the Scholars.

If one does not wish to partake in a Hadra, that is their right; however, they are not permitted to object to others who wish to. This is based on the axiom: There is no objection to a valid difference of opinion. Furthermore, matters of differing opinions are not for ordinary Muslims to argue about; these matters are for scholars to discuss.
references: Khatar Muhammad, al-Mawsu’a al-Yusufiyya fi Bayan Adilla al-Sufiyya

records.title: Is It Necessary to Send Blessings on the Prophet?
records.question: Is it mandatory to send blessings upon the Prophet whenever I get any thought or mention of the Prophet in my head? Sometimes, I get his name in my head throughout the day and send blessings. But sometimes, even when I go to sleep, I get Prophet’s name mentioned after closing my eyes and wanting to sleep. Then I open my eyes and send blessings. A few moments ago, I took a nap, but I barely could; I kept getting his name mentioned in my head. What should I do about this? And also, what should be done in general whenever we think of our Prophet or get his name mentioned in our head?
records.answer:
ّSending blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) takes on various rulings in the Hanafi school – obligatory, necessary, and recommended – based on the circumstance. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

Obligation (Fard) of Sending Blessings

Every Muslim must send blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) once in their lifetime. This is out of obedience to Allah’s command in the Qur’an [Ibid.]

“Indeed, Allah showers His blessings upon the Prophet, and His angels pray for him. O, believers! Invoke Allah’s blessings upon him, and salute him with worthy greetings of peace.” [Qur’an; 33:56]

Necessity (Wajib) of Sending Blessings

It is necessary to send blessings on the Prophet once in each gathering that his blessed name is audibly mentioned. [Ibn ‘Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar]

The exception to this ruling is if there is an Islamically recognized excuse preventing one from sending blessings on the Prophet, such as if one is in prayer or using the restroom. [Ibid.]

Repeating Mention of His Blessed Name

It is not obligatory to repeat the sending of blessings if the blessed name of the Prophet is repeated, although it is recommended. [Ibid.]

It is unnecessary to send blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) just by thinking of his blessed name. [Ibid.]

Recommended: Sending Abundant Blessings

It is recommended to send blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) abundantly, especially if his name is mentioned by one or in one’s presence. [Ibid.]

The exception to this will be if one is legally unable to send blessings for Islamically recognized reasons, such as being in prayer, reciting the Qur’an, calling the call to prayer, etc… [Ibid.]

The Virtues of Sending Blessings of the Prophet

Despite the obligation of sending blessings on the Prophet being limited to once per gathering, one is still encouraged to send abundant blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace). [Ibid.]

Many narrations indicate immense blessings for the one who sends blessings on the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) even once, let alone abundantly. We will suffice with one narration. [Ibid.]

Ubay bin K’ab (Allah be pleased with him) narrates that a man said, “O Messenger of Allah! I have a lot of time to send blessings upon you. How much should I do?” He replied, “As much as you wish.” The man replied, “I will do 1/4th.” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but if you were to increase, it would be better for you.” The man said, “I will do 1/2.” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but if you were to increase, it would be better for you.” The man said, “I will do 2/3rds.” The Prophet said, “As you wish, but if you were to increase, it would be better for you.” The man said, “I will take all my time to send blessings upon you.” The Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, “In that case, you will be sufficed of all your worries and all your sins will be expiated for.” [Tirmidhi]

records.title: How to Deal with My Father Who Refuses to Meet Me Until I Convert to Islam?
records.question: I have been in touch with my father for roughly two years now. He abandoned me as a young child to raise his other children abroad. He is Muslim, but I was not raised as a Muslim. He refuses to have a relationship or meet with me unless I convert to Islam.
records.answer:
Honestly, I admire your strength. Instead of responding to him in anger at his absence, you are considering his request and finding a way to practice Islam. No child deserves to be abandoned, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, and I praise your resolve and confidence.

It wasn’t clear from your question whether you have converted yet, but you are absolutely on the right path and on the right website.

Quran

No better thing is there for a new Muslim than reading the words of God himself. Reading the Quran with its translation, I recommend Yusuf Ali’s translation because I read it as a teenager, is the most eye-opening and enlightening thing for you. You will find in its injunctions, prohibitions, warnings, commands, stories, morals, rewards and punishments, and much more. Try to read it every day, even if only a little, and contemplate its meanings.

Du’a (Supplication)

Du’a is worship, as the Prophet told us (Allah bless him and give him peace). Use this powerful tool to invoke Allah with no other mediator in between. Ask Him genuinely to guide you to the truth and to help you practice. Ask Him to send you a good company that can teach and positively influences you. Ask Him to uncover the steps you should take in your journey and let you reach your spiritual goals.

Please see this link about du’a: Is Making Dua in My Heart Enough?

Take a Course at SeekersGuidance

Knowledge is power. Knowledge gives you the power to change yourself and confidently practice your religion. Please see this link for answers on conversion and links to courses about Islam. Muslim Convert: Would My Family Be Okay With Islam?

Learn about the daily rituals of Muslims and the do’s and don’ts of Islam.

Tell your father you want to learn more about Islam and ask him what he recommends you read. Take some time to visit a local mosque and spend some quiet reflection time there. Tell him that you are trying your best and would like him to try and meet you halfway through this effort. Pray that Allah opens your hearts to each other and develops a bond that will never be broken.

records.title: Am I Allowed to Say Inaccurate Impressions?
records.question: I have a question about the permissibility of small lies. For example, if my mother made a soup and I didn’t like it, and she asked me if I tried it, I said yes to not upset her. The second example is if someone asks me how many driving lessons I have had and I forget how many, I make up the number 40 and say that is that haram.
records.answer:
The above is not considered lying. These are just exaggerated and estimated statements based on our cultural norms, which most people utter and speak in a way in our day-to-day life.

Lying means to inform another about something that is otherwise than it is. In your case, you are just estimating. Rest assured. Just work on yourself to not speak in the way you mention above.

If you don’t like a specific type of food, taste it, and say it was good. It might not be tasty to you, but it is good overall as it is food and nutrition for all.

The proof that exaggeration is sometimes permissible and not considered lying is the hadith related in Bukhari and Muslim that the Prophet (Allah bless him and give him peace) said, …“as for Jahm, his stick never leaves his shoulder, while Muawiya (Allah bless him and give him peace) does not own a thing,” is being understood that the latter owned the garment he was wearing. The former set his stick aside when he slept and at other times. [Nawawi, Al-Adhkar al-Muntakhab min kalam Sayyid al-Abrar]

I recommend you go through the lessons on Permissible Lying and the Importance of Speech from imam Birgivi’s The Path of Muhammad Explained.

records.title: How To Compensate for Lying and Using Sick Leave To Remain Absent From Work?
records.question: I worked for a company that gave their employees sick pay. Sometimes I was tired and didn’t want to go to work so every once in a while I would take the day off telling work I was sick when I wasn’t. I received sick pay for those days.
records.answer:
You should approach the company now, and speak to whoever would be in charge of dealing with this matter. The money owed to the company then will be owed to the current owners. You may find that they will forgo it and excuse you.

Returning the rights of others is one of the conditions of valid repentance. The others are remorseful for having done the deed, ceasing immediately, and resolving never to return to it. [Nawawi, Riyadh al-Salihin]

Give Charity to Compensate

One thing you should do, however, is to give some regular charity intending the reward of it to go to those to who you owe the money to. This way, you will have compensated them and will have a defense on the Day of Judgement. In fact, this is a good practice everyone should adopt to compensate all those who we have wronged. [Sha’rani, al Kawkab al-Shahiq]

It’s best to set things right now before the coming of “a fearsome day when even the truly chivalrous man will flee from his bother, his mother and father, his lifelong wife, and his children. Every single person, on that day, will have enough to truly worry them.” [Quran, 80:34-37]
